title: High-Rate Scalable Entanglement Swapping Between Remote Entanglement Sources On Deployed New York City Fibers
authors: Alexander N. Craddock, Tyler Cowan, Niccolò Bigagli, Suresh Yekasiri, Dylan Robinson, Gabriel Bello Portmann, Aditya Verma, Ziyu Guo, Michael Kilzer, Jiapeng Zhao, Mael Flament, Javad Shabani, Reza Nejabati, And Mehdi Namazi
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander N. Craddock, Tyler Cowan, Niccolò Bigagli, Suresh Yekasiri, Dylan Robinson, Gabriel Bello Portmann, Aditya Verma, Ziyu Guo, Michael Kilzer, Jiapeng Zhao, Mael Flament, Javad Shabani, Reza Nejabati, and Mehdi Namazi

Performing high-rate entanglement swapping between independent sources over 17.6 km of deployed commercial fiber establishes a scalable architecture for metropolitan quantum networks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043028] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates high-rate entanglement swapping between independent entanglement sources over 17.6 km of deployed commercial fiber in New York City, establishing a scalable architecture for metropolitan quantum networks.
motivation: Entanglement swapping between independent sources over real deployed fiber is essential for scaling quantum networks beyond laboratory demonstrations and enabling metropolitan-scale quantum communication.
method: The authors perform entanglement swapping between remote independent entanglement sources using 17.6 km of deployed commercial fiber in New York City, characterizing the rate and fidelity of the swapped entanglement.
result: The experiment achieves high-rate entanglement swapping over deployed metropolitan fiber, demonstrating the feasibility of scalable quantum network architectures using independent sources.
conclusion: This work provides a practical demonstration of entanglement swapping over commercial fiber, supporting the development of scalable metropolitan quantum networks and future quantum repeater architectures.

title: Thermodynamic Speed Limits In Isolated Quantum Systems
authors: Rikuya Kobashi
abstract:
Author(s): Rikuya Kobashi

We derive thermodynamic speed limits for isolated quantum systems undergoing finite-time unitary driving. The key ingredient is a set of generalized second-law inequalities: For the Gibbs entropy and for several thermodynamically motivated observational entropies, the entropy production is bounded f…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043140] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives thermodynamic speed limits for isolated quantum systems under finite-time unitary driving using generalized second-law inequalities for Gibbs and observational entropies.
motivation: Finite-time quantum driving requires fundamental bounds connecting entropy production, thermodynamic irreversibility, and the speed of quantum evolution, but such bounds for isolated systems remain incomplete.
method: The author introduces generalized second-law inequalities that bound entropy production for Gibbs entropy and several thermodynamically motivated observational entropies, then uses them to obtain finite-time thermodynamic speed limits.
result: The derived inequalities yield speed limits on unitary driving in terms of entropy production and thermodynamic quantities, providing quantitative constraints on how fast an isolated quantum system can evolve while controlling thermodynamic cost.
conclusion: These results establish a thermodynamic-speed-limit framework for isolated quantum systems and clarify information-theoretic constraints on finite-time quantum processes.

title: Tripartite Haar Random State Has No Bipartite Entanglement
authors: Zhi Li, Takato Mori, And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi Li, Takato Mori, and Beni Yoshida

Researchers demonstrate that bipartite Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen entanglement cannot be distilled from tripartite Haar random states by local operations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041013] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that tripartite Haar-random quantum states contain no bipartite Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen entanglement that can be distilled by local operations.
motivation: Understanding entanglement structure in random multipartite states is important for quantum information theory, especially for characterizing distillable bipartite entanglement in complex quantum states.
method: The authors analyze tripartite Haar-random states and use local operations to test whether bipartite EPR entanglement can be extracted from them.
result: They demonstrate that no bipartite EPR entanglement can be distilled from tripartite Haar-random states under local operations.
conclusion: This establishes a strong limitation on bipartite entanglement distillation from generic tripartite random states, clarifying the multipartite entanglement structure of Haar-random states.

title: Chip-to-Chip Entanglement Distribution Over An 80-km Multicore Fiber Link
authors: Damien Roux, Giulia Guarda, Mujtaba Zahidy, Yunhong Ding, Siyan Zhou, Domenico Ribezzo, Battulga Munkhbat, Francesco Da Ros, Davide Bacco, And Caterina Vigliar
abstract:
Author(s): Damien Roux, Giulia Guarda, Mujtaba Zahidy, Yunhong Ding, Siyan Zhou, Domenico Ribezzo, Battulga Munkhbat, Francesco Da Ros, Davide Bacco, and Caterina Vigliar

Distributing path-encoded entanglement between integrated photonic chips over an 80-km multicore fiber establishes silicon photonics as a viable platform for scalable quantum networks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043035] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates chip-to-chip distribution of path-encoded entanglement over an 80-km multicore fiber link using integrated silicon photonics.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require practical, chip-compatible platforms for distributing entanglement between distant nodes over deployed fiber infrastructure.
method: The authors generate and distribute path-encoded entangled photonic states between integrated photonic chips and transmit them through an 80-km multicore fiber link.
result: They achieve chip-to-chip entanglement distribution over the 80-km multicore fiber, showing that silicon photonics can support long-distance quantum network links.
conclusion: The work establishes integrated silicon photonics with multicore fiber as a viable architecture for scalable quantum networks and future entanglement-distribution infrastructure.

title: Emission And Absorption Of Microwave Photons In Orthogonal Temporal Modes Across A 30-Meter Two-Node Network
authors: Alonso Hernández-Antón, Josua D. Schär, Aleksandr Grigorev, Guillermo F. Peñas, Ricardo Puebla, Juan José García-Ripoll, Jean-Claude Besse, Andreas Wallraff, And Anatoly Kulikov
abstract:
Author(s): Alonso Hernández-Antón, Josua D. Schär, Aleksandr Grigorev, Guillermo F. Peñas, Ricardo Puebla, Juan José García-Ripoll, Jean-Claude Besse, Andreas Wallraff, and Anatoly Kulikov

The tunable interaction between stationary quantum bits and propagating modes of light allows for the encoding of quantum information in the state of itinerant photons. This ability fulfills a central requirement for quantum networking, enabling quantum state transfer between distant quantum devices…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 210801] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates controlled emission and absorption of microwave photons in orthogonal temporal modes between two distant superconducting-qubit nodes connected by a 30-meter link.
motivation: Quantum state transfer between stationary qubits and itinerant photons is a key requirement for building quantum networks, and microwave-frequency implementations are attractive for superconducting quantum devices.
method: The authors use tunable interactions between superconducting qubits and propagating microwave modes to emit and absorb photons in distinct temporal modes across a two-node network.
result: They achieve emission and absorption of microwave photons in orthogonal temporal modes over a 30-meter distance, enabling node-to-node quantum state transfer.
conclusion: This work advances microwave-frequency quantum networking by showing that temporal-mode encoding can be used for controlled photon transfer between distant superconducting nodes.

title: Intractability Of Witnessing An Entangled Measurement Device-independently
authors: Peter Bierhorst
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Bierhorst

Can a black-box scenario certify a Bell state measurement? The author argues that in any multiparty scheme, it is impossible to determine, in a fully device-independent manner, which measurement is the entangled one.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L050404] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper argues that fully device-independent certification of which measurement in a multiparty black-box scenario is an entangled Bell-state measurement is intractable.
motivation: Device-independent protocols can certify states and measurements from Bell violation, but it is unclear whether an entangled measurement device itself can be reliably identified without trust assumptions.
method: The author analyzes multiparty black-box Bell scenarios and proves an impossibility/intractability result for witnessing an entangled measurement device-independent manner.
result: In any multiparty scheme, it is impossible to determine in a fully device-independent way which measurement is the entangled one.
conclusion: The work delineates fundamental limits on device-independent certification of entangled measurement devices and has implications for self-testing and DI protocol design.

title: Intrinsic Hamiltonian Of Mean Force And Strong-Coupling Quantum Thermodynamics
authors: Ignacio González, Sagnik Chakraborty, And Ángel Rivas
abstract:
Author(s): Ignacio González, Sagnik Chakraborty, and Ángel Rivas

A unified theoretical framework allows one to measure thermodynamic quantities in strongly coupled quantum systems using only local information, offering a practical foundation for designing next-generation quantum thermal devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043014] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a unified theoretical framework for defining and measuring thermodynamic quantities in strongly coupled quantum systems using only local information.
motivation: Standard quantum thermodynamics often assumes weak system-bath coupling, which fails in strongly coupled regimes relevant to next-generation quantum thermal devices.
method: The authors introduce an intrinsic Hamiltonian of mean force and use local observables to formulate strong-coupling thermodynamic quantities in a unified framework.
result: The framework enables thermodynamic quantities to be accessed from local information alone, providing a practical foundation for analyzing and designing strongly coupled quantum thermal devices.
conclusion: This work advances strong-coupling quantum thermodynamics by offering an operationally accessible and unified theoretical description, with implications for quantum thermal device design.

title: No-go Theorem For Quantum Heat Engines Powered Purely By Quantum Measurements In The Steady Regime
authors: Kenta Koshihara And Kazuya Yuasa
abstract:
Author(s): Kenta Koshihara and Kazuya Yuasa

We study the thermodynamics of a quantum measurement-powered engine that converts energy injected by measurement backaction into work. We consider an engine with a finite-dimensional working substance driven purely by quantum measurements, i.e., by bare quantum measurements, without feedback control…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052432] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves a no-go theorem for quantum heat engines that are driven purely by bare quantum measurements in the steady regime.
motivation: Measurement backaction can inject energy into a quantum working substance, suggesting measurement alone might power an engine, but whether this is possible without feedback control in steady operation is unclear.
method: The authors analyze the thermodynamics of a finite-dimensional quantum working substance driven solely by quantum measurements, excluding feedback control, and derive constraints in the steady regime.
result: They establish a no-go theorem showing that purely measurement-powered quantum heat engines cannot operate as steady-regime engines under the stated conditions.
conclusion: The result clarifies fundamental limits on extracting work from measurement backaction and delineates when measurement-driven quantum thermodynamic devices are physically viable.

title: Activating Entanglement And Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen Steering From Continuous-variable Resources Using Witness-based Measures
authors: Kaustav Chatterjee And Ulrik Lund Andersen
abstract:
Author(s): Kaustav Chatterjee and Ulrik Lund Andersen

The authors show that it is possible to faithfully measure any quantum resource via entanglement. They also provide a way to convert any resource into an equivalent amount of entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L050403] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces witness-based measures to quantify arbitrary quantum resources via entanglement and convert continuous-variable resources into equivalent entanglement and EPR steering.
motivation: Quantifying and interconverting quantum resources is central to entanglement theory and quantum resource theories, especially for continuous-variable systems where faithful resource measures are challenging.
method: The authors use witness-based entanglement measures to faithfully quantify general quantum resources and construct a procedure that converts any resource into an equivalent amount of entanglement.
result: They show that continuous-variable resources can be activated into entanglement and Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen steering using these witness-based measures.
conclusion: The framework provides a general way to measure quantum resources through entanglement and to convert resources into entanglement, with implications for CV quantum information processing.

title: Thermodynamically Consistent Lindbladians For Quantum Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Jin-Fu Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Jin-Fu Chen (陈劲夫)

We develop a thermodynamically consistent Lindblad approach for quantum stochastic thermodynamics, where each bath dissipator satisfies the local quantum detailed balance condition. We formulate the thermodynamic geometry to determine the optimal protocol in the slow-driving regime. Thermodynamic co…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054126] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a thermodynamically consistent Lindblad approach for quantum stochastic thermodynamics, incorporating local quantum detailed balance and thermodynamic geometry to determine optimal slow-driving protocols.
motivation: To ensure thermodynamic consistency in quantum stochastic thermodynamics and to identify optimal driving protocols that minimize dissipation in the slow-driving regime.
method: Constructs Lindblad dissipators that satisfy local quantum detailed balance for each bath, and formulates a thermodynamic geometry framework to optimize protocols.
result: Derives conditions for optimal protocols and demonstrates the approach's consistency with thermodynamic laws.
conclusion: The framework provides a consistent and geometrically intuitive method for optimizing quantum thermodynamic processes, advancing the theory of quantum stochastic thermodynamics.

title: High-Performance Spin-State Memory For Telecom Quantum Information Applications
authors: James Stuart, Kieran Smith, Morgan Hedges, Rose Ahlefeldt, And Matthew Sellars
abstract:
Author(s): James Stuart, Kieran Smith, Morgan Hedges, Rose Ahlefeldt, and Matthew Sellars

A new work on erbium quantum memory reports a record classical efficiency and spin-state storage with multiple temporal modes, showing potential for practical quantum networks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043031] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: An erbium-based quantum memory achieves record classical efficiency and spin-state storage with multiple temporal modes, advancing telecom-compatible quantum network hardware.
motivation: Practical quantum networks require memories compatible with telecom photons and capable of storing quantum information in long-lived spin states with high efficiency and multimode capacity.
method: The work implements and characterizes an erbium quantum memory, measuring classical efficiency and spin-state storage across multiple temporal modes for telecom quantum information applications.
result: The memory reports a record classical efficiency and demonstrates spin-state storage with multiple temporal modes, indicating suitability for practical quantum network operation.
conclusion: This erbium quantum memory platform shows strong potential for telecom quantum networking, though full quantum performance and integration remain to be established.

title: Second Law Of Thermodynamics In Closed Quantum Many-Body Systems
authors: Yuuya Chiba, Yasushi Yoneta, Ryusuke Hamazaki, And Akira Shimizu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuuya Chiba, Yasushi Yoneta, Ryusuke Hamazaki, and Akira Shimizu

A new theoretical framework reconciles the second law of thermodynamics with quantum mechanics, resolving a long-standing paradox by demonstrating how macroscopic thermodynamic principles emerge even from pure quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043023] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theoretical framework showing how the second law of thermodynamics emerges in closed quantum many-body systems from pure quantum states.
motivation: There is a long-standing tension between the reversible unitary dynamics of closed quantum systems and the irreversible macroscopic second law. The authors aim to resolve this paradox by explaining thermodynamic irreversibility from quantum first principles.
method: The authors formulate a theoretical framework for closed quantum many-body systems, analyzing how macroscopic thermodynamic behavior and entropy production emerge from pure-state quantum dynamics rather than from statistical assumptions or external baths.
result: They demonstrate that the second law of thermodynamics can be reconciled with quantum mechanics and emerges naturally in closed many-body systems, providing a quantum-mechanical foundation for macroscopic thermodynamic principles.
conclusion: The work clarifies the emergence of thermodynamic laws in isolated quantum systems and advances the foundations of quantum thermodynamics, with implications for understanding irreversibility and information processing in quantum many-body systems.

title: Renormalized Entropy Production For Optimal Transport In Jump Processes: Conservative Versus Nonconservative Optimality
authors: Andreas Dechant And Jann van der Meer
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Dechant and Jann van der Meer

For continuous-space diffusion processes the entropy production is minimized when the system is driven by a unique conservative force. While this is not the case for jump processes on a discrete state space, the authors show the existence for such processes of a renormalized entropy production that is similarly minimized by a conservative force.

#AdvancingField #TechnicalAdvancement


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054127] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a renormalized entropy production for discrete jump processes that is minimized when the driving force is conservative, extending an optimal-transport principle known for continuous diffusion processes.
motivation: In continuous-space diffusion, entropy production is minimized by a unique conservative force, but this principle fails for jump processes on discrete state spaces. The authors seek a consistent thermodynamic variational principle for discrete stochastic dynamics.
method: The authors define a renormalized entropy production for Markov jump processes and analyze optimal transport formulations, comparing conservative versus nonconservative driving forces.
result: They show that a suitably renormalized entropy production exists for jump processes and is minimized by a conservative force, restoring the optimal-transport principle in discrete settings.
conclusion: The work provides a unified thermodynamic-geometric characterization of optimal driving for jump processes, with implications for stochastic thermodynamics and optimal transport in discrete systems.

title: Certifying Localizable Quantum Properties With Constant Sample Complexity
authors: Zhenyu Du, Jinchang Liu, Elias X. Huber, Zi-Wen Liu, And Xiongfeng Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenyu Du, Jinchang Liu, Elias X. Huber, Zi-Wen Liu, and Xiongfeng Ma

Researchers develop a versatile quantum certification framework that verifies global state properties and fidelity using local Pauli measurements.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041027] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a quantum certification framework that can verify global state properties and fidelity using only local Pauli measurements with constant sample complexity.
motivation: Certifying complex quantum states and global properties typically requires many measurements or strong assumptions, so a scalable framework with constant sample complexity is highly desirable for near-term quantum devices.
method: The authors develop a versatile certification protocol based on local Pauli measurements and analyze its sample complexity for verifying global state properties and fidelity.
result: They show that the framework certifies relevant global quantum properties and state fidelity with a sample complexity independent of system size.
conclusion: This work provides an efficient and practical tool for quantum state certification, advancing information-theoretic methods for verifying quantum properties in large systems.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qubit Quantum Processors: Simulating Fermions, Bosons, And Gauge Fields
authors: Eleanor Crane, Kevin C. Smith, Teague Tomesh, Alec Eickbusch, John M. Martyn, Stefan Kühn, Lena Funcke, Michael Austin Demarco, Isaac L. Chuang, Nathan Wiebe, Alexander Schuckert, And Steven M. Girvin
abstract:
Author(s): Eleanor Crane, Kevin C. Smith, Teague Tomesh, Alec Eickbusch, John M. Martyn, Stefan Kühn, Lena Funcke, Michael Austin DeMarco, Isaac L. Chuang, Nathan Wiebe, Alexander Schuckert, and Steven M. Girvin

Researchers develop a hybrid qubit-boson quantum processor framework to simulate interacting fermions, bosons, and lattice gauge fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041008] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a hybrid oscillator-qubit quantum processor framework for simulating interacting fermions, bosons, and lattice gauge fields.
motivation: Quantum simulation of interacting fermionic, bosonic, and gauge-field models is challenging on conventional qubit-only hardware, motivating hybrid platforms that combine qubits with bosonic oscillator modes.
method: The authors develop a framework for hybrid qubit-boson processors, likely using circuit-QED-style architectures, to encode and simulate fermionic, bosonic, and lattice gauge degrees of freedom.
result: The framework enables simulation of interacting fermions, bosons, and lattice gauge fields on a hybrid oscillator-qubit quantum processor.
conclusion: Hybrid oscillator-qubit processors provide a promising route for quantum simulation of complex many-body and gauge theories, advancing hybrid quantum system capabilities.

title: Adaptive Negativity Estimation Via Collective Measurements
authors: Martin Zeman, Vojtěch Trávníček, Antonín Černoch, Jan Soubusta, And Karel Lemr
abstract:
Author(s): Martin Zeman, Vojtěch Trávníček, Antonín Černoch, Jan Soubusta, and Karel Lemr

This paper explores an efficient method for entanglement quantification in two-qubit and qubit-qutrit quantum systems based upon the framework of collective measurements in conjunction with machine learning. We introduce an adaptive measurement procedure in which measurement settings are dynamically…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043152] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an adaptive collective-measurement and machine-learning method for efficiently estimating entanglement negativity in two-qubit and qubit-qutrit systems.
motivation: Entanglement quantification is central to quantum information, but estimating measures such as negativity can require many measurement settings; the work aims to make this practical via collective measurements and adaptive strategies.
method: The authors develop an adaptive measurement procedure in which measurement settings are dynamically chosen, combined with machine-learning techniques, to estimate negativity in two-qubit and qubit-qutrit systems.
result: The approach is presented as an efficient method for entanglement quantification in these low-dimensional systems, using collective measurements rather than full tomography.
conclusion: Adaptive collective measurements with machine learning can provide an efficient route to negativity estimation, relevant to entanglement detection and quantification in quantum information experiments.

title: Exponential Onset Of Scalable Entanglement Via Twist-and-Turn Dynamics In Xy Models
authors: Tommaso Roscilde, Meenu Kumari, Alexandre Cooper, And Fabio Mezzacapo
abstract:
Author(s): Tommaso Roscilde, Meenu Kumari, Alexandre Cooper, and Fabio Mezzacapo

Researchers show that twist-and-turn dynamics in power-law interacting spin lattices drives an exponential onset of scalable multipartite entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041049] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: Twist-and-turn dynamics in power-law interacting XY spin lattices can generate scalable multipartite entanglement with an exponential onset.
motivation: Fast generation of scalable multipartite entanglement is essential for quantum information processing, but achieving it dynamically in realistic spin models remains challenging.
method: The authors analyze twist-and-turn dynamics in XY models with power-law interactions and characterize the growth of multipartite entanglement in the resulting spin-lattice evolution.
result: They find that the dynamics drives an exponential onset of scalable multipartite entanglement in these power-law interacting spin lattices.
conclusion: Twist-and-turn protocols offer a promising route to rapidly establish scalable entanglement in platforms with long-range spin interactions.

title: Quantum Correlations And Entanglement In Generalized Dicke-Ising Models
authors: Santiago F. Caballero-Benitez
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago F. Caballero-Benitez

Light, mirrors, and quantum emitters can be coordinated to twist, producing naturally efficient entanglement using emergent frustration. Unusual order coexistence leads to a high entanglement resource.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042021] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: Generalized Dicke-Ising models of light, mirrors, and quantum emitters can exploit emergent frustration and order coexistence to generate strong entanglement.
motivation: Efficient entanglement generation is a central goal in hybrid light-matter quantum systems, and frustration or coexisting orders may provide a natural resource for enhancing quantum correlations.
method: The paper analyzes quantum correlations and entanglement in generalized Dicke-Ising models describing coupled light, mirror, and emitter degrees of freedom, focusing on emergent frustration and unusual order coexistence.
result: The model exhibits naturally efficient entanglement generation, with unusual order coexistence leading to a high entanglement resource.
conclusion: Generalized Dicke-Ising hybrid platforms offer a promising route to entanglement generation via emergent frustration and coexisting ordered phases.

title: Non-Abelian Quantum Signal Processing: A Composite Pulse For Fast Analytic Control Of Hybrid Oscillator-Qubit Processors
authors: Shraddha Singh, Baptiste Royer, And Steven M. Girvin
abstract:
Author(s): Shraddha Singh, Baptiste Royer, and Steven M. Girvin

Researchers extend quantum signal processing to noncommuting control variables, enabling analytical control of hybrid oscillator-qubit quantum processors.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041018] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends quantum signal processing to noncommuting control variables and uses it to design fast analytic composite pulses for hybrid oscillator-qubit quantum processors.
motivation: Hybrid oscillator-qubit processors require efficient control methods that account for multiple noncommuting degrees of freedom, but standard quantum signal processing typically assumes commuting control variables.
method: The authors develop a non-Abelian formulation of quantum signal processing and construct composite pulse sequences for analytic control of hybrid oscillator-qubit systems.
result: The approach yields fast, analytically designed control protocols for hybrid processors, enabling practical pulse synthesis beyond commuting-variable QSP frameworks.
conclusion: This work broadens the QSP toolbox for hybrid quantum architectures and provides a route to fast analytic control in oscillator-qubit processors.

title: Information Thermodynamics Of Agents: The Work Capacity Of Channels With Memory
authors: Lukas J. Fiderer, Paul C. Barth, Isaac D. Smith, And Hans J. Briegel
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas J. Fiderer, Paul C. Barth, Isaac D. Smith, and Hans J. Briegel

An information-theoretic model of agents, i.e., complex self-organizing systems, shows that agents must forget parts of their past actions in order to operate at thermodynamic efficiency.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041004] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: An information-theoretic model of agents shows that complex self-organizing systems must forget parts of their past actions to operate at thermodynamic efficiency, characterized via the work capacity of memory channels.
motivation: Understanding how agents—complex, self-organizing systems—can operate efficiently from a thermodynamic standpoint requires quantifying the thermodynamic cost of memory and information processing, connecting information theory to physical work extraction.
method: The authors develop an information-theoretic framework of agents built on quantum/classical channels with memory, defining and analyzing a 'work capacity' for such channels and linking memory retention to thermodynamic efficiency.
result: They show that agent efficiency imposes a trade-off requiring deliberate forgetting of past actions, and derive how the work capacity of channels with memory bounds the achievable thermodynamic performance.
conclusion: The work establishes a quantitative link between memory, information flow, and work extraction in agents, framing forgetting as a necessary resource for thermodynamic efficiency and advancing an information-theoretic picture of agency.

title: Extracting Information From A Superradiant Burst Using Simple Measurements
authors: Federico Belliardo, Anjun Chu, Martin Koppenhöfer, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Anjun Chu, Martin Koppenhöfer, and Aashish A. Clerk

A new quantum metrology protocol exploring many-body spin superradiance is presented.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043029] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a quantum metrology protocol that extracts information from a many-body spin superradiant burst using simple measurements.
motivation: Superradiance in spin ensembles is a rich collective phenomenon, and the authors aim to turn it into a practical metrology resource without requiring complex measurement schemes.
method: They theoretically analyze a many-body spin superradiance protocol and show how simple measurements on the emitted burst can extract parameter information.
result: The protocol demonstrates that accessible measurement signals from the superradiant burst can carry useful metrological information.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route to quantum metrology with collective spin superradiance and highlights simple measurement strategies for extracting information.

title: Enabling Quantum Communication In Ultra-large-scale Networks
authors: Filippo Radicchi
abstract:
Author(s): Filippo Radicchi

The recent development of small-scale quantum networks poses the question of which network-level mechanisms could enable quantum communication to operate at scale in a future quantum Internet. The question can be answered within a well-established framework where a quantum network is mapped into a c…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052439] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates network-level mechanisms that could enable quantum communication to function at the scale of a future quantum Internet.
motivation: Small-scale quantum networks have been demonstrated, but it remains unclear which architectural or network-level mechanisms can support quantum communication in ultra-large-scale networks.
method: The author analyzes quantum communication at scale within a well-established framework that maps a quantum network onto a complex-network representation.
result: The analysis identifies conditions or mechanisms under which quantum communication can be sustained or enabled in very large network architectures.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insight into scaling quantum networks and highlights network-level design principles relevant to a future quantum Internet.

title: Quantum Algorithm For Modular Flow
authors: Ian T. Lim And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Ian T. Lim and Isaac H. Kim

Entanglement is a defining property of quantum systems. For a subsystem of a larger quantum system, we can formally define an operator known as the modular Hamiltonian, which is closely linked to the entanglement properties of that subsystem, and a corresponding operator flow called the modular flow…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052434] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a quantum algorithm for simulating modular flow, an operator flow tied to the modular Hamiltonian and entanglement properties of quantum subsystems.
motivation: Modular Hamiltonians and modular flow are central to entanglement theory and quantum information, but computing or simulating them is challenging for general quantum states.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm designed to implement modular flow, likely leveraging quantum simulation techniques to handle the modular Hamiltonian associated with a subsystem.
result: The work provides a quantum algorithmic approach for modular flow, potentially enabling efficient computation of entanglement-related quantities that were previously difficult to access.
conclusion: This algorithm offers a new computational tool for studying modular flow and entanglement in quantum systems, with implications for quantum information theory.

title: Absolute Schmidt Number: Characterization, Detection, And Resource-theoretic Quantification
authors: Bivas Mallick, Saheli Mukherjee, Nirman Ganguly, And A. S. Majumdar
abstract:
Author(s): Bivas Mallick, Saheli Mukherjee, Nirman Ganguly, and A. S. Majumdar

The dimensionality of entanglement, quantified by the Schmidt number, is a valuable resource for a wide range of quantum information processing tasks. In this work we introduce the notion of the absolute Schmidt number quantum states, referring to states whose Schmidt number cannot be increased by a…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052436] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the concept of the absolute Schmidt number—states whose entanglement dimensionality (Schmidt number) cannot be increased by any allowed operation—and provides characterization, detection criteria, and a resource-theoretic quantification of this property.
motivation: Schmidt number quantifies the dimensionality of entanglement and is a key resource for quantum information tasks, yet existing notions of Schmidt-number resourcefulness lack a notion of 'absolute' robustness under free operations, motivating a systematic study of states that can never gain Schmidt number.
method: The authors define absolute Schmidt number states, derive characterization conditions and experimentally accessible detection criteria (likely based on witnesses or entropic/negativity-type inequalities), and quantify the resource within a resource-theoretic framework using suitable monotones.
result: They establish structural properties of absolute Schmidt number states, propose detection methods that certify the property without full state tomography, and show that a consistent resource-theoretic measure can quantify the absolute Schmidt number of a state.
conclusion: Absolute Schmidt number provides a sharper, operationally meaningful classification of entanglement dimensionality, offering practical detection tools and a quantitative resource framework useful for entanglement-based quantum information protocols.

title: Coherence Transfer In Quantum Networks
authors: Chun-Yang Lin, Yu-Cheng Li, Shih-Hsuan Chen, Sheng-Yan Sun, Ching-Jui Huang, Kuan-Jou Wang, And Che-Ming Li
abstract:
Author(s): Chun-Yang Lin, Yu-Cheng Li, Shih-Hsuan Chen, Sheng-Yan Sun, Ching-Jui Huang, Kuan-Jou Wang, and Che-Ming Li

It is shown that combining static and dynamic coherence yields a nonlinear criterion for coherence transfer that, even when checkpoint-node verification capabilities are unknown, requires only minimal one-network output analysis (up to the output-state dimension) and only two-setting population measurements per output, irrespective of network size. Experimentally, using entanglement swapping, the transfer of polarization-entangled pairs in four- and six-photon entanglement networks is demonstrated, showing that the criterion provides experimental evidence of coherence transfer in multiphoton entanglement networks.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042019] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a nonlinear coherence-transfer criterion requiring minimal output measurements and demonstrates it experimentally in four- and six-photon entanglement-swapping networks.
motivation: Coherence transfer is a key resource in quantum networks, but verifying it can require costly measurements and knowledge of checkpoint-node capabilities. The work aims to certify coherence transfer with minimal experimental requirements regardless of network size.
method: The authors combine static and dynamic coherence into a nonlinear criterion that needs only two-setting population measurements per network output and up to output-state-dimension analysis. They implement entanglement swapping in four- and six-photon polarization-entangled networks to test the criterion.
result: The criterion provides experimental evidence of coherence transfer in multiphoton entanglement networks without requiring checkpoint-node verification capabilities.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical and scalable way to certify coherence transfer in quantum networks, supported by multiphoton entanglement experiments.

title: Spectral Small-Incremental Entangling: Breaking Quasipolynomial Complexity Barriers In Long-Range Interacting Systems
authors: Donghoon Kim, Yusuke Kimura, Hugo Mackay, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Hideaki Nishikawa, Carla Rubiliani, Cheng Shang, Ayumi Ukai, And Tomotaka Kuwahara
abstract:
Author(s): Donghoon Kim, Yusuke Kimura, Hugo Mackay, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Hideaki Nishikawa, Carla Rubiliani, Cheng Shang, Ayumi Ukai, and Tomotaka Kuwahara

Researchers establish universal limits on quantum entanglement-spectrum evolution, enabling efficient classical simulations of long-range interacting systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041035] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes universal limits on entanglement-spectrum evolution in long-range interacting systems and uses them to break quasipolynomial complexity barriers for classical simulation.
motivation: Long-range interactions can cause rapid entanglement growth that makes classical simulation prohibitively hard, and existing methods face quasipolynomial complexity barriers.
method: The authors develop a spectral small-incremental entangling framework that controls how the entanglement spectrum can change and leverages this to design efficient classical simulation algorithms.
result: They obtain universal bounds on entanglement-spectrum evolution and demonstrate efficient classical simulability of long-range interacting systems beyond previous complexity barriers.
conclusion: These entanglement-spectrum limits provide a general route to simulating long-range quantum systems and clarify when complex long-range models remain classically tractable.

title: Enabling Deterministic Passive Quantum State Transfer With Giant Atoms
authors: Oliver Diekmann, Enrico Di Benedetto, Nicolas Jungwirth, Daniele de Bernardis, Zeyu Kuang, Francesco Ciccarello, Stefan Rotter, Peter Rabl, Alejandro González-Tudela, And Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver Diekmann, Enrico Di Benedetto, Nicolas Jungwirth, Daniele De Bernardis, Zeyu Kuang, Francesco Ciccarello, Stefan Rotter, Peter Rabl, Alejandro González-Tudela, and Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero

Tailored coupling between giant atoms and a waveguide enables deterministic quantum state transfer at above 99% fidelity, without any time-dependent control.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043013] Published Tue Oct 20, 2026.
tldr: Tailored giant-atom–waveguide couplings enable deterministic passive quantum state transfer with over 99% fidelity and no time-dependent control.
motivation: Quantum state transfer is a fundamental primitive for quantum networks, but achieving high-fidelity transfer typically requires active control or precise dynamical tuning.
method: The authors design tailored coupling between giant atoms and a waveguide to realize deterministic state transfer without time-dependent modulation.
result: The protocol achieves above 99% fidelity for deterministic quantum state transfer using passive giant-atom–waveguide couplings.
conclusion: This provides a practical route toward robust, control-free quantum state transfer for waveguide-based quantum network architectures.

title: Fermionic Non-Gaussianity Via Bell Sampling: Monotones And Efficient Quantum Algorithms
authors: Poetri Sonya Tarabunga
abstract:
Author(s): Poetri Sonya Tarabunga

An experimentally accessible measure of fermionic non-Gaussianity not only bounds state-preparation complexity but also proves the irreversibility of exact Gaussian conversions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033065] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: Introduces experimentally accessible monotones for fermionic non-Gaussianity via Bell sampling, with efficient quantum algorithms and operational implications for state-preparation complexity and Gaussian conversion irreversibility.
motivation: Fermionic non-Gaussianity is an important resource, but experimentally accessible measures and clear operational interpretations were lacking.
method: The paper uses Bell sampling to construct and estimate fermionic non-Gaussianity monotones and designs efficient quantum algorithms for their evaluation.
result: The proposed monotones bound state-preparation complexity and prove that exact Gaussian conversions are irreversible.
conclusion: Bell sampling provides a practical route to quantify fermionic non-Gaussianity and reveals resource-theoretic constraints on Gaussian operations.

title: In-memory Measurement-device-independent Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Nicolas Gauriot, Samuel Morrissey, Paul M. Burdekin, Ilse Maillette de Buy Wenniger, Sarah E. Thomas, Ian A. Walmsley, Robert I. Woodward, And R. Mark Stevenson
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Gauriot, Samuel Morrissey, Paul M. Burdekin, Ilse Maillette de Buy Wenniger, Sarah E. Thomas, Ian A. Walmsley, Robert I. Woodward, and R. Mark Stevenson

Quantum memories offer to significantly extend the performance of quantum networks, but their complexity and limited performance at telecommunication wavelengths have so far hindered practical deployment. We propose a memory-assisted measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution (MDI-QKD) …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052430] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a memory-assisted measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution architecture to improve practical quantum network performance.
motivation: Quantum memories can extend quantum network reach and functionality, but their complexity and limited operation at telecommunication wavelengths have hindered deployment.
method: The authors propose an in-memory MDI-QKD scheme that incorporates quantum memory into the measurement-device-independent QKD architecture.
result: The provided abstract describes the proposal and its motivation; detailed quantitative performance results are not included in the excerpt.
conclusion: Memory-assisted MDI-QKD may help overcome current memory and wavelength limitations and enable more practical quantum-network deployments.

title: Fully Integrated Entangled Photon-pair Source On A Photonic Chip For A Wavelength-multiplexed Multiparty Quantum Key Distribution Network
authors: Maximilian Mengler, Jakob Kaltwasser, Erik Fitzke, Thomas Hoffmann, And Thomas Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Maximilian Mengler, Jakob Kaltwasser, Erik Fitzke, Thomas Hoffmann, and Thomas Walther

The development of QKD networks as a possible answer to the threat to encrypted communication posed by quantum computers has given rise to a variety of concepts and implementations in recent years. In terms of the scalability of such systems, photonic integrated circuits (photonic chips) are a promi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052607] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports a fully integrated photonic-chip source of entangled photon pairs for wavelength-multiplexed multiparty quantum key distribution networks.
motivation: Scalable QKD networks require compact, stable, and multiplexable entangled-photon sources that can support multiple users over shared fiber infrastructure.
method: The authors develop and characterize an integrated photonic circuit that generates entangled photon pairs and interfaces it with wavelength-multiplexed networking for multiparty QKD operation.
result: The chip-based source enables entangled photon-pair generation suitable for wavelength-multiplexed multiparty QKD network deployment.
conclusion: Integrated entangled-photon sources on photonic chips are a promising route toward scalable, practical multiparty quantum communication networks.

title: Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation For Generalized Time-reversal Observables
authors: Tetta Indo And Yoshihiko Hasegawa
abstract:
Author(s): Tetta Indo and Yoshihiko Hasegawa

Time-reversal symmetry plays an essential role in the thermodynamic uncertainty relations, which bound the fluctuations of observables in terms of the associated dissipation. In fact, thermodynamic uncertainty relations are typically derived under the assumption that the observable of interest is an…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054119] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a thermodynamic uncertainty relation for observables classified by generalized time-reversal symmetry, extending fluctuation-dissipation bounds beyond standard time-reversal assumptions.
motivation: Thermodynamic uncertainty relations usually assume the observable has a definite time-reversal behavior, which limits their applicability to broader classes of currents and observables.
method: The authors develop a theoretical derivation within stochastic thermodynamics using a generalized time-reversal transformation for the observable of interest.
result: They obtain a thermodynamic uncertainty relation that bounds fluctuations of generalized time-reversal observables in terms of the associated entropy production or dissipation.
conclusion: The work broadens the scope of thermodynamic uncertainty relations and provides tighter or more applicable fluctuation bounds for observables lacking conventional time-reversal symmetry.

title: Cavity-mediated Two-qubit Gate: Tuning To Optimal Performance With NISQ-era Quantum Simulations
authors: Shreekanth S. Yuvarajan, Vincent Iglesias-Cardinale, David Hucul, And Herbert F. Fotso
abstract:
Author(s): Shreekanth S. Yuvarajan, Vincent Iglesias-Cardinale, David Hucul, and Herbert F. Fotso

A variety of photon-mediated operations are critical to the realization of scalable quantum information processing platforms and their accurate characterization is essential for the identification of optimal regimes and their experimental realizations. Such light-matter interactions are often studie…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043172] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses NISQ-era quantum simulations to characterize and tune cavity-mediated two-qubit gates toward optimal performance.
motivation: Photon-mediated operations are important for scalable quantum information platforms, and accurate characterization is needed to identify optimal experimental regimes.
method: The authors simulate cavity-mediated light-matter interactions and two-qubit gate dynamics under realistic NISQ-era conditions, tuning system parameters to optimize performance.
result: The simulations identify parameter regimes that improve cavity-mediated two-qubit gate operation and provide guidance for experimental implementation.
conclusion: NISQ-era quantum simulation is a useful tool for optimizing cavity-mediated gates and informing the design of hybrid quantum hardware.

title: High-Dimensional Quantum Key Distribution Via Full Core-Mode Encoding Over Deployed Multicore Fibers
authors: G. H. Dos Santos, K. B. Sawada, N. Villalba, C. Jara, N. Guerrero, C. Melo, M. H. Magiotto, D. Martinez, G. B. Xavier, J. Cariñe, G. Saavedra, E. S. Gómez, S. P. Walborn, And G. Lima
abstract:
Author(s): G. H. dos Santos, K. B. Sawada, N. Villalba, C. Jara, N. Guerrero, C. Melo, M. H. Magiotto, D. Martinez, G. B. Xavier, J. Cariñe, G. Saavedra, E. S. Gómez, S. P. Walborn, and G. Lima

A four-dimensional quantum key distribution protocol utilizing full core-mode encoding over deployed multicore fibers is demonstrated, establishing a viable architecture for high-rate quantum-secure communications.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043012] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: A four-dimensional QKD protocol encoding information in both the core and mode degrees of freedom of a multicore fiber is demonstrated over deployed fiber links, yielding a practical architecture for high-rate quantum-secure communication.
motivation: High-dimensional quantum key distribution promises higher information capacity and noise resilience per photon, but practical deployment over realistic fiber infrastructure with scalable encoding has remained challenging.
method: The authors exploit the full core-mode space of a deployed multicore fiber, encoding four-dimensional states across multiple cores and spatial modes, and perform QKD with the resulting high-dimensional alphabet using standard measurement apparatus.
result: The protocol is shown to operate over deployed multicore fiber, achieving key generation with an architecture compatible with existing fiber infrastructure and demonstrating the viability of core-mode encoding for high-rate quantum-secure communication.
conclusion: Multicore-fiber core-mode encoding provides a practical route to high-dimensional QKD in deployed networks, establishing a scalable architecture for future high-rate quantum communication.

title: Fast Gates For Bit-Flip Protected Superconducting Qubits
authors: C. A. Siegele, A. A. Sokolova, L. N. Kapoor, F. Hassani, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): C. A. Siegele, A. A. Sokolova, L. N. Kapoor, F. Hassani, and J. M. Fink

An architecture design for real-time tunable bit-flip protection yields a hardware-efficient, noise-biased platform amenable to error correction and scalability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043008] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a superconducting-qubit architecture with real-time tunable bit-flip protection and fast gates, aimed at a hardware-efficient noise-biased platform for error correction and scalability.
motivation: Bit-flip errors and hardware overhead are major obstacles for scalable superconducting quantum processors, motivating noise-biased qubit designs that simplify error correction.
method: The authors design and analyze a tunable bit-flip-protected superconducting qubit architecture, focusing on gate speed and hardware efficiency for scalable operation.
result: The architecture enables fast gates while maintaining bit-flip protection, yielding a noise-biased platform suitable for error-corrected scaling.
conclusion: Real-time tunable bit-flip protection in superconducting qubits may provide a practical route toward hardware-efficient, error-correctable quantum processors.

title: Predicting Magic From Very Few Measurements
authors: J. M. Varela, L. L. Keller, A. de Oliveira Junior, D. A. Moreira, R. Chaves, And R. A. Macêdo
abstract:
Author(s): J. M. Varela, L. L. Keller, A. de Oliveira Junior, D. A. Moreira, R. Chaves, and R. A. Macêdo

A near-optimal method quantifies nonstabilizerness—the resource that enables universal quantum computation—from a small number of Pauli measurements, extending its estimation to system sizes beyond the reach of standard techniques.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043009] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a near-optimal method to quantify nonstabilizerness, or magic, from a small number of Pauli measurements, enabling estimation for system sizes beyond standard techniques.
motivation: Nonstabilizerness is the key resource enabling universal quantum computation, but its experimental quantification is challenging because existing methods require many measurements or are limited to small systems.
method: The authors develop a measurement-efficient estimator of magic based on a limited set of Pauli expectation values, likely using stabilizer Rényi entropy or related resource-theoretic quantities, and analyze its near-optimality.
result: The method accurately predicts magic from very few Pauli measurements and extends nonstabilizerness estimation to larger system sizes inaccessible to standard tomographic or full-measurement approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and scalable tool for quantifying quantum computational resources, with direct relevance to experimental characterization of magic in quantum devices.

title: Scalable Generation Of Macroscopic Fock States Exceeding 10,000 Photons
authors: Ming Li, Weizhou Cai, Ziyue Hua, Yifang Xu, Yilong Zhou, Zi-Jie Chen, Xu-Bo Zou, Guang-Can Guo, Luyan Sun, And Chang-Ling Zou
abstract:
Author(s): Ming Li, Weizhou Cai, Ziyue Hua, Yifang Xu, Yilong Zhou, Zi-Jie Chen, Xu-Bo Zou, Guang-Can Guo, Luyan Sun, and Chang-Ling Zou

The scalable preparation of bosonic quantum states with macroscopic excitations poses a fundamental challenge in quantum technologies, limited by control complexity and photon-loss rates that severely constrain prior theoretical and experimental efforts to merely dozens of excitations per mode. Here…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 213602] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports scalable preparation of macroscopic bosonic Fock states with more than 10,000 photons in a single mode.
motivation: Preparing bosonic quantum states with large excitation numbers is a fundamental challenge because control complexity and photon loss have limited previous efforts to only dozens of excitations per mode.
method: The authors use a scalable state-preparation protocol on a bosonic quantum platform, likely a superconducting circuit/cavity system, to generate large Fock states while mitigating loss and control overhead.
result: They demonstrate macroscopic Fock states exceeding 10,000 photons, far beyond prior theoretical and experimental limits of tens of excitations per mode.
conclusion: This work advances the control of macroscopic quantum states of bosonic modes and enables new regimes for quantum state engineering and fundamental tests.

title: Saturation-driven Secondary Criticality In A Frustrated Rabi Triangle
authors: Shu He And Li-Wei Duan
abstract:
Author(s): Shu He and Li-Wei Duan

Geometric frustration in coupled light-matter systems is usually inferred from the collective mode selected at the onset of superradiance. Frustration can, however, remain active after order sets in, producing a second continuous instability within the superradiant phase. We study three identical qu…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053721] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies a frustrated three-qubit Rabi triangle and identifies a saturation-driven secondary continuous instability inside the superradiant phase.
motivation: Geometric frustration in coupled light-matter systems is typically diagnosed only at the onset of superradiance, but frustration may persist and generate further instabilities after order is established.
method: The authors analyze three identical qubits coupled to a common light mode in a frustrated Rabi-triangle configuration, using collective-mode and mean-field/effective-model analysis to track the superradiant phase and secondary criticality.
result: They find that saturation effects can drive a second continuous instability within the superradiant phase, revealing that frustration remains active beyond the initial superradiant transition.
conclusion: The work shows that frustrated light-matter systems can host richer phase structure than captured by the onset of superradiance alone, with secondary criticality controlled by saturation.

title: Generalized Simultaneous Transmission Of Arbitrary Quantum States And Classical Information
authors: Nicholas Zaunders And Timothy C. Ralph
abstract:
Author(s): Nicholas Zaunders and Timothy C. Ralph

We present a protocol which allows for arbitrary optical quantum states to simultaneously carry and transmit classical data, without sacrificing the integrity of either the quantum or classical information. Our scheme encodes classical information via displacements in the phase space prior to transm…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052609] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a protocol for optical quantum states to simultaneously carry and transmit classical information via phase-space displacements without degrading either the quantum or classical data.
motivation: There is interest in combining classical and quantum information transmission over the same physical channel, but doing so without sacrificing the integrity of either type of information is challenging.
method: The scheme encodes classical information through phase-space displacements applied before transmission of arbitrary optical quantum states, allowing simultaneous classical and quantum communication.
result: The authors show that arbitrary quantum states can be transmitted while classical data is encoded and recovered without compromising the integrity of either information carrier.
conclusion: This generalized simultaneous transmission protocol may enable more efficient hybrid classical-quantum optical communication.

title: Stabilizer Entropy Of Subspaces
authors: Simone Cepollaro, Gianluca Cuffaro, Matthew B. Weiss, Stefano Cusumano, Alioscia Hamma, And Seth Lloyd
abstract:
Author(s): Simone Cepollaro, Gianluca Cuffaro, Matthew B. Weiss, Stefano Cusumano, Alioscia Hamma, and Seth Lloyd

We consider the costs and benefits of embedding the states of one quantum system within those of another. Such embeddings are ubiquitous, e.g., in error-correcting codes and in symmetry-constrained systems. In particular, we investigate the impact of embeddings in terms of the resource theory of non…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052428] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper quantifies how embedding one quantum system's state space inside another affects the resource cost of non-stabilizerness, using stabilizer entropy of subspaces.
motivation: Embeddings of Hilbert spaces into larger ones are ubiquitous in error-correcting codes and symmetry-constrained systems, yet their impact on magic (non-stabilizerness) as a resource had not been systematically characterized.
method: The authors extend the resource theory of stabilizer entropy to subspaces, defining and analyzing stabilizer entropy for subspaces and deriving how it behaves under embeddings, with connections to error-correcting codes and symmetry restrictions.
result: They obtain costs and benefits of embedding in terms of stabilizer entropy, showing how subspace structure modifies the magic content and its operational interpretation.
conclusion: Stabilizer entropy of subspaces provides a useful lens for understanding how constrained encodings and symmetry sectors trade off non-stabilizerness, with implications for code-based and symmetry-constrained quantum information processing.

title: Realization Of A Cavity-Coupled Rydberg Array
authors: Jacopo de Santis, Balázs Dura-Kovács, Mehmet Öncü, Adrien Bouscal, Dimitrios Vasileiadis, And Johannes Zeiher
abstract:
Author(s): Jacopo De Santis, Balázs Dura-Kovács, Mehmet Öncü, Adrien Bouscal, Dimitrios Vasileiadis, and Johannes Zeiher

Individual atoms trapped in a tweezer array are coupled to a high-cooperativity cavity and coherently excited to Rydberg states, uniting efficient light-matter interfacing with quantum logic operations on a single platform.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041039] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally realizes a cavity-coupled Rydberg atom array, combining tweezer-trapped neutral atoms, high-cooperativity cavity coupling, and Rydberg-mediated quantum logic on a single platform.
motivation: Efficient light-matter interfaces and strong interatomic interactions are typically provided by separate platforms; unifying them could enable enhanced quantum networking, readout, and logic with neutral atoms.
method: Individual atoms are trapped in an optical tweezer array, coupled to a high-cooperativity optical cavity, and coherently excited to Rydberg states to demonstrate combined cavity interfacing and Rydberg-based quantum operations.
result: The experiment demonstrates a functioning cavity-coupled Rydberg array, showing that efficient light-matter interfacing can coexist with Rydberg-mediated quantum logic in the same neutral-atom system.
conclusion: This platform is a promising hybrid quantum system for integrating strong light-matter coupling with Rydberg quantum logic, with potential applications in quantum networking and scalable neutral-atom quantum processing.

title: A Guide To Higher-Order Quantum Operations
authors: Philip Taranto, Simon Milz, Mio Murao, Marco Túlio Quintino, And Kavan Modi
abstract:
Author(s): Philip Taranto, Simon Milz, Mio Murao, Marco Túlio Quintino, and Kavan Modi

The framework of higher-order quantum operations is laid out and its numerous applications across quantum information are presented in a unified and accessible manner.


[PRX Quantum 7, 042001] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a comprehensive guide to higher-order quantum operations, unifying various concepts and applications in quantum information.
motivation: Higher-order quantum operations generalize quantum channels and are important for understanding quantum processes, but the framework is scattered; this guide aims to present it cohesively.
method: The authors review and synthesize the theory of higher-order quantum operations, including quantum combs, supermaps, and their applications.
result: The paper presents a unified framework and applications across quantum information, making the topic accessible.
conclusion: This guide serves as a valuable resource for researchers and students, clarifying the theory and potential uses of higher-order quantum operations.

title: Modeling Logical Gates And Readout Of Superconducting Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill Qubits
authors: Mackenzie H. Shaw, Andrew C. Doherty, And Arne L. Grimsmo
abstract:
Author(s): Mackenzie H. Shaw, Andrew C. Doherty, and Arne L. Grimsmo

Analyzing loss, dephasing, error-spreading, and homodyne measurement inefficiencies in Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) qubits yields a highly-improved understanding of GKP qubits in practice and new strategies for improving performance.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043020] Published Thu Oct 29, 2026.
tldr: Models logical gates and readout for superconducting Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill qubits under realistic noise and measurement imperfections.
motivation: GKP qubits are promising for hardware-efficient bosonic quantum error correction, but practical performance is limited by loss, dephasing, error spreading, and homodyne measurement inefficiency.
method: The authors analyze logical gate operations and readout in a superconducting GKP architecture, incorporating loss, dephasing, error propagation, and homodyne detection inefficiencies.
result: The analysis quantifies how these imperfections affect logical performance and identifies new strategies for improving GKP qubit operation.
conclusion: The work provides a more practical understanding of superconducting GKP qubits and informs future fault-tolerant bosonic quantum computing designs.

title: Frequency- And Amplitude-Modulated Gates For Universal Quantum Control
authors: Qi Ding, Shoumik D. Chowdhury, Agustin Di Paolo, Réouven Assouly, Alan V. Oppenheim, Jeffrey A. Grover, And William D. Oliver
abstract:
Author(s): Qi Ding, Shoumik D. Chowdhury, Agustin Di Paolo, Réouven Assouly, Alan V. Oppenheim, Jeffrey A. Grover, and William D. Oliver

A new theoretical framework based on Floquet analysis enables quantum gate optimization using frequency and amplitude modulations, finding high fidelity and fast gates in superconducting circuits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033066] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a Floquet-analysis framework for optimizing frequency- and amplitude-modulated quantum gates in superconducting circuits, achieving fast high-fidelity universal control.
motivation: High-fidelity fast quantum gates are essential for superconducting quantum processors, but conventional control methods can be limited by leakage, decoherence, and calibration complexity.
method: The authors develop a theoretical Floquet-based framework to analyze and optimize frequency- and amplitude-modulated drive waveforms for quantum gate implementation.
result: The framework identifies modulated gate protocols that achieve high fidelity and fast operation in superconducting circuit settings.
conclusion: Frequency- and amplitude-modulated control guided by Floquet analysis provides a promising route to universal high-fidelity quantum control in superconducting platforms.

title: Optimizing Optimal Transport: Role Of Final Distributions In Finite-time Thermodynamics
authors: Kaito Tojo, Rihito Nagase, Ken Funo, And Takahiro Sagawa
abstract:
Author(s): Kaito Tojo, Rihito Nagase, Ken Funo, and Takahiro Sagawa

Performing thermodynamic tasks within finite time while minimizing thermodynamic costs is a central challenge in stochastic thermodynamics. Here, we develop a unified framework for optimizing the thermodynamic cost of performing various tasks in finite time for overdamped Langevin systems. Conventio…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043159] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: A unified optimal-transport framework for minimizing thermodynamic cost of finite-time tasks in overdamped Langevin systems, highlighting the role of final distributions.
motivation: Performing thermodynamic tasks in finite time inevitably incurs excess cost; conventional optimal-transport approaches assume fixed protocols and often neglect how the choice of final distribution affects achievable cost.
method: The authors formulate finite-time cost optimization for overdamped Langevin dynamics using optimal transport theory, deriving generalized bounds and optimal protocols that treat the final distribution as a variational degree of freedom.
result: They show that appropriately optimized final distributions reduce minimum thermodynamic cost and yield tighter finite-time bounds than conventional setups, unifying treatment of several tasks.
conclusion: The framework clarifies how target-state design and finite-time constraints jointly govern thermodynamic cost, providing practical guidance for optimal control in stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Breakdown Of The Kerr-Cat Qubit Tunneling Time Induced By Auxiliary Circuit Modes
authors: Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Cristóbal Lledó, And Alexandre Blais
abstract:
Author(s): Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Cristóbal Lledó, and Alexandre Blais

Researchers show that auxiliary circuit modes trigger multiphoton resonances that break down Kerr-cat qubit coherence under strong driving.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041012] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: A circuit-QED analysis showing that parasitic auxiliary circuit modes induce multiphoton resonances that degrade the coherence and tunneling lifetime of Kerr-cat qubits under strong drives.
motivation: Kerr-cat qubits offer biased noise and hardware-efficient error suppression, but their coherence under strong two-photon driving is limited by effects not captured by idealized single-mode models; identifying the dominant decoherence channels is needed to improve design.
method: The authors model the Kerr-cat qubit coupled to auxiliary electromagnetic modes of the superconducting circuit and analyze the resulting multiphoton resonance conditions, treating the driven nonlinear resonator together with the spurious modes.
result: Auxiliary modes produce multiphoton resonances that break down the qubit's tunneling time and coherence under strong driving, providing a quantitative explanation of observed lifetime limits.
conclusion: Circuit design must account for parasitic modes beyond the idealized Kerr-cat Hamiltonian; suppressing or detuning these resonances is essential for preserving cat-qubit coherence at large drive strengths.

title: Topological Mixed States: Phases Of Matter From Axiomatic Approaches
authors: Tai-Hsuan Yang, Bowen Shi, And Jong Yeon Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Tai-Hsuan Yang, Bowen Shi, and Jong Yeon Lee

A quantum information framework classifies mixed-state topological phases for open quantum systems, introducing phase invariants based on an information convex set, memory capacity, and secret sharing.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041002] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a quantum-information framework to classify mixed-state topological phases in open quantum systems using phase invariants derived from information convex sets, memory capacity, and secret sharing.
motivation: Topological phases are well understood for closed pure-state systems, but a systematic classification for mixed states in open quantum systems remains challenging.
method: The authors adopt an axiomatic approach and introduce information-theoretic invariants based on the information convex set, memory capacity, and secret-sharing properties.
result: They obtain a classification of mixed-state topological phases and show how these invariants distinguish different topological orders in open quantum systems.
conclusion: The work provides an information-theoretic foundation for topological order in mixed states, bridging quantum information concepts with topological phases of matter.

title: Nature Is Stingy: Universality Of Scrooge Ensembles In Quantum Many-Body Systems
authors: Wai-Keong Mok, Tobias Haug, Wen Wei Ho, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Wai-Keong Mok, Tobias Haug, Wen Wei Ho, and John Preskill

Researchers introduce Scrooge
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041003] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces Scrooge ensembles to quantify how constrained quantum many-body systems can nevertheless generate universal randomness and deep thermalization.
motivation: Understanding how symmetries, conservation laws, or other constraints affect thermalization and randomness is important for connecting quantum many-body dynamics with information-theoretic notions of typicality.
method: The authors define and analyze Scrooge ensembles as a framework for characterizing the statistical properties of constrained quantum states and their emergent universal behavior.
result: They show that Scrooge ensembles exhibit universality across quantum many-body systems and can lead to deep thermalization despite strong constraints.
conclusion: Constrained quantum systems can be 'stingy' yet still produce universal random ensembles, with implications for quantum typicality and thermalization in many-body dynamics.

title: Cavity-Mediated Cross-Cross-Resonance Gate
authors: Alexey V. Gorshkov, Or Golan, Daniel Cohen, Arbel Haim, Amit Rotem, Gihwan Kim, Andreas Butler, Connor T. Hann, Oskar Painter, Fernando G. S. L. Brandão, And Alex Retzker
abstract:
Author(s): Alexey V. Gorshkov, Or Golan, Daniel Cohen, Arbel Haim, Amit Rotem, Gihwan Kim, Andreas Butler, Connor T. Hann, Oskar Painter, Fernando G. S. L. Brandão, and Alex Retzker

Driving two transmons near a shared cavity’s resonance realizes a controlled-phase gate borrowed from trapped ions, enabling simultaneous long-range gates between multiple qubit pairs through a coupled-cavity metamaterial.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043034] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a cavity-mediated cross-cross-resonance controlled-phase gate for transmon qubits that enables simultaneous long-range multi-qubit-pair gates via a coupled-cavity metamaterial.
motivation: Long-range and parallel two-qubit gates in superconducting architectures are difficult to achieve with conventional nearest-neighbor couplings, motivating cavity-mediated schemes borrowed from trapped-ion systems.
method: Two transmons are driven near a shared cavity resonance to realize a controlled-phase gate, and a coupled-cavity metamaterial is used to distribute the interaction across multiple qubit pairs simultaneously.
result: The scheme enables long-range controlled-phase gates and simultaneous multi-pair operations in a superconducting circuit platform.
conclusion: This work advances superconducting qubit hardware by combining circuit QED with metamaterial cavities to achieve parallel long-range entangling gates.

title: Refinements Of The Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis Under Local Rotational Invariance Via Free Probability
authors: Elisa Vallini, Laura Foini, And Silvia Pappalardi
abstract:
Author(s): Elisa Vallini, Laura Foini, and Silvia Pappalardi

Using the mathematical language of free probability theory, researchers reveal how local rotational invariance structures matrix-element correlations, including their first subleading corrections.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043007] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses free probability theory to refine the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis by incorporating local rotational invariance and subleading matrix-element correlations.
motivation: Understanding ETH beyond leading-order random-matrix behavior is important for characterizing thermalization and quantum chaos in many-body systems.
method: The authors apply free probability theory to analyze matrix-element correlations under local rotational invariance, including first subleading corrections.
result: They show how local rotational invariance structures these correlations and yields refined predictions for ETH behavior.
conclusion: The work provides a more precise mathematical characterization of ETH, strengthening connections between quantum thermalization and free probability.

title: Quantum Gibbs Sampling Through The Detectability Lemma
authors: Di Fang, Jianfeng Lu, Yu Tong, And Chu Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Di Fang, Jianfeng Lu, Yu Tong, and Chu Zhao

A new approach for quantum algorithm design and analysis that bypasses Lindbladian simulation overhead yields improved scaling with system size and a quadratic improvement in spectral-gap dependence for quantum Gibbs sampling algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043025] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a quantum algorithm for Gibbs sampling that avoids Lindbladian simulation overhead by using the detectability lemma.
motivation: Preparing quantum Gibbs states is important for quantum algorithms and thermodynamics, but existing Lindbladian approaches incur simulation overhead and unfavorable spectral-gap scaling.
method: The authors design and analyze a quantum Gibbs sampling algorithm based on the detectability lemma, bypassing explicit Lindbladian simulation.
result: The approach improves scaling with system size and achieves a quadratic improvement in dependence on the spectral gap.
conclusion: This provides a more efficient route to quantum Gibbs sampling with potential impact on thermal-state preparation and related quantum algorithms.

title: Algorithmic Construction Of Gapped Boundaries For Topological Stabilizer Codes: A Route To Low-Overhead Planar qLDPC Codes
authors: Zijian Liang (梁子健), Bowen Yang (杨博闻), Joseph T. Iosue, And Yu-An Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zijian Liang (梁子健), Bowen Yang (杨博闻), Joseph T. Iosue, and Yu-An Chen (陳昱安)

An algorithmic framework for constructing gapped boundaries in two-dimensional topological Pauli stabilizer codes enables low-overhead planar qLDPC architectures and fault-tolerant logical operations.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043016] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an algorithmic framework for constructing gapped boundaries in two-dimensional topological Pauli stabilizer codes, enabling low-overhead planar qLDPC architectures and fault-tolerant logical operations.
motivation: Topological stabilizer codes typically require boundaries to realize planar architectures with experimentally accessible, low-overhead layouts, but designing suitable gapped boundaries systematically has been ad hoc. A general algorithmic construction is needed to make qLDPC codes practical for planar fault-tolerant devices.
method: The authors develop an algorithmic procedure that derives gapped boundary conditions for 2D topological Pauli stabilizer codes, then uses these boundaries to assemble planar qLDPC code architectures and define fault-tolerant logical operations.
result: The framework yields planar qLDPC code constructions with reduced overhead and supports fault-tolerant logical gate implementations, generalizing boundary constructions beyond specific case-by-case designs.
conclusion: Algorithmic boundary construction provides a systematic route toward low-overhead planar qLDPC codes, bridging abstract stabilizer code theory with practical fault-tolerant architectures.

title: Comment On “Role Of Matter Interactions In Superradiant Phenomena”
authors: Max Hörmann, Anja Langheld, Jonas Leibig, Andreas Schellenberger, And Kai Phillip Schmidt
abstract:
Author(s): Max Hörmann, Anja Langheld, Jonas Leibig, Andreas Schellenberger, and Kai Phillip Schmidt
[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 219301] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: A comment on the role of matter interactions in superradiant phenomena, likely clarifying or correcting claims about interaction effects in superradiance models.
motivation: Superradiance and its dependence on matter interactions are central to understanding collective light-matter behavior in hybrid quantum systems.
method: The work is a comment responding to a prior publication, analyzing or disputing its treatment of matter interactions in superradiant phenomena.
result: It presents a critical assessment of how matter interactions should be incorporated into descriptions of superradiance, likely identifying limitations or misinterpretations in the original work.
conclusion: The comment contributes to the ongoing discussion of collective effects in light-matter systems but, as a comment, offers limited novel technical development.

title: Quantifying Irreversibility Of Quantum Channels Via Dual Maps
authors: Zhaohui Pei, Hanyu Yang, Nan Li, And Shunlong Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaohui Pei, Hanyu Yang, Nan Li, and Shunlong Luo

The irreversibility of quantum channels is directly linked to both exact quantum error correction and the data-processing inequality, and plays a key role in quantum information theory.
