title: Nonlinear Frequency Shift And Bistability Of Magnon Polarons
authors: Kevin Künstle, Matthias Wagner, Philipp Knaus, Yannik Kunz, Ephraim Spindler, Katharina Lasinger, Matthias R. Schweizer, Philipp Pirro, John F. Gregg, And Mathias Weiler
abstract:
Author(s): Kevin Künstle, Matthias Wagner, Philipp Knaus, Yannik Kunz, Ephraim Spindler, Katharina Lasinger, Matthias R. Schweizer, Philipp Pirro, John F. Gregg, and Mathias Weiler

We investigate the nonlinear dynamics of strongly coupled surface acoustic waves (SAWs) and spin waves (SWs) in a magnetoacoustic resonator based on a YIG/ZnO heterostructure by combining microwave reflection measurements with microfocused Brillouin light scattering spectroscopy. In the linear regim…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254415] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates nonlinear frequency shift and bistability of strongly coupled surface acoustic waves and spin waves in a YIG/ZnO magnetoacoustic resonator.
motivation: Understanding nonlinear dynamics in coupled magnon-phonon systems is important for developing hybrid magnonic platforms and SAW-based devices.
method: The authors combine microwave reflection measurements with microfocused Brillouin light scattering spectroscopy to probe the nonlinear magnetoacoustic response of a YIG/ZnO heterostructure.
result: They observe nonlinear frequency shifts and bistability of magnon-polaron modes arising from the strong coupling between SAWs and spin waves.
conclusion: The findings characterize nonlinear behavior in hybrid magnon-phonon resonators and may inform the design of SAW-controlled magnonic and hybrid systems.

title: Meson Spectroscopy Of Exotic Symmetries Of Ising Criticality In Rydberg Atom Arrays
authors: Joseph Vovrosh, Julius de Hond, Sergi Julià-Farré, Johannes Knolle, And Alexandre Dauphin
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph Vovrosh, Julius de Hond, Sergi Julià-Farré, Johannes Knolle, and Alexandre Dauphin

A programmable array of atoms reveals how symmetry of the quantum Ising chain transforms when chains are coupled together, providing experimental signatures of a new excitation spectrum.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043018] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: A programmable Rydberg atom array is used to spectroscopically probe how the symmetries of the quantum Ising chain are modified when chains are coupled, revealing a meson-like excitation spectrum.
motivation: Coupled Ising chains in Rydberg arrays can realize lattice-gauge-like physics where exotic symmetries and confining dynamics produce mesonic bound states; understanding how these symmetries emerge and transform upon coupling is needed to interpret such quantum simulations.
method: The authors use a programmable array of neutral atoms in the Rydberg blockade regime to simulate coupled quantum Ising chains, and perform spectroscopic measurements of the excitation spectrum to identify signatures of the modified symmetry.
result: The experiment resolves a meson-like excitation spectrum whose structure reveals how the symmetry of a single Ising chain transforms into that of coupled chains, providing experimental signatures of the new excitation content.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that Rydberg atom arrays can serve as a platform for spectroscopy of exotic symmetry structures and confinement physics in coupled Ising systems, opening routes to gauge-theory-inspired quantum simulation.

title: Assessing The Classicality Of Photon Echo From Excitons In Lead Halide Perovskite Nanocrystals
authors: George Alkhalil, Hendrik Rose, Artur V. Trifonov, Polina R. Sharapova, Jan Sperling, Dmitri R. Yakovlev, Elena V. Kolobkova, Maria S. Kuznetsova, Marc Aßmann, Manfred Bayer, Torsten Meier, And Ilya A. Akimov
abstract:
Author(s): George Alkhalil, Hendrik Rose, Artur V. Trifonov, Polina R. Sharapova, Jan Sperling, Dmitri R. Yakovlev, Elena V. Kolobkova, Maria S. Kuznetsova, Marc Aßmann, Manfred Bayer, Torsten Meier, and Ilya A. Akimov

Photon echo (PE) spectroscopy is a powerful technique for probing decoherence mechanisms and charge carrier dynamics in semiconductor systems. Beyond traditional coherence measurements, characterizing the photon statistics of the echo signal is important for assessing its potential in quantum inform…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043161] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper assesses whether photon echo signals from excitons in lead halide perovskite nanocrystals exhibit classical or nonclassical photon statistics for potential quantum-information use.
motivation: Photon echo spectroscopy is widely used to probe decoherence, but its photon statistics are less understood and are important for judging whether the echo can be used in quantum information applications.
method: The authors perform photon echo spectroscopy on excitons in lead halide perovskite nanocrystals and characterize the photon statistics of the echo signal to evaluate its classicality.
result: They provide an assessment of the classical versus quantum character of the photon echo emission from these nanocrystals, linking coherence measurements to photon-statistical behavior.
conclusion: The work clarifies the suitability and limitations of exciton photon echoes in perovskite nanocrystals as a platform for quantum-information-relevant optical signals.

title: Coincidence-conditioned Compton-modulation Recovery From Annihilation Bell Pairs
authors: Peter Caradonna, Kenji Shimazoe, And Takeshi Sato
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Caradonna, Kenji Shimazoe, and Takeshi Sato

We develop an idealized framework for recovering coincidence-conditioned Compton-modulation levels from 511 keV photon pairs produced in electron-positron annihilation and described by a Bell state. Compton scattering followed by angular postselection in the signal arm defines a coincidence-conditio…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043163] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an idealized framework for recovering Compton-modulation signals from coincidence-conditioned 511 keV annihilation photon pairs described by a Bell state.
motivation: Annihilation photon pairs offer entangled probes, and Compton scattering with angular postselection may enable coincidence-conditioned modulation recovery for applications such as gamma-ray imaging or sensing.
method: The authors model electron-positron annihilation Bell pairs at 511 keV, apply Compton scattering and angular postselection in the signal arm, and analyze the resulting coincidence-conditioned Compton-modulation levels within an idealized theoretical framework.
result: The framework shows how Bell-state correlations and coincidence postselection can conditionally recover Compton-modulation information from annihilation photon pairs.
conclusion: The work provides a proof-of-principle theoretical treatment of entanglement-assisted Compton modulation recovery, but it is specialized and applied rather than advancing core quantum information theory.

title: Directional And Correlated Optical Emission From A Waveguide-Engineered Molecule With Local Control
authors: Clara Henke, Thomas Wilkens Sandø, Vasiliki Angelopoulou, Lena Maria Hansen, Alexey Tiranov, Oliver August Dall’alba Sandberg, Zhe Liu, Leonardo Midolo, Nikolai Bart, Arne Ludwig, Anders Søndberg Sørensen, Peter Lodahl, And Cornelis Jacobus van Diepen
abstract:
Author(s): Clara Henke, Thomas Wilkens Sandø, Vasiliki Angelopoulou, Lena Maria Hansen, Alexey Tiranov, Oliver August Dall’Alba Sandberg, Zhe Liu, Leonardo Midolo, Nikolai Bart, Arne Ludwig, Anders Søndberg Sørensen, Peter Lodahl, and Cornelis Jacobus van Diepen

A system of waveguide-coupled independently tunable quantum dots is presented, enabling on-demand directional emission and the generation of correlated multiphoton states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043032] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a waveguide-coupled system of independently tunable quantum dots that enables directional emission and correlated multiphoton state generation.
motivation: Integrated photonic emitters with on-demand directional control are useful for scaling quantum photonic resources, but the work is primarily a source/platform demonstration rather than a network protocol or architecture.
method: The authors engineer a molecule-like arrangement of quantum dots coupled to a photonic waveguide and use local tuning to control the directional and correlated optical emission.
result: The system achieves on-demand directional emission and generates correlated multiphoton states from independently tunable quantum-dot emitters.
conclusion: This provides a promising photonic building block for quantum optical technologies, though its direct connection to quantum network protocols or repeater architectures remains indirect.

title: Anderson Noise Avalanche And Sudden Coherence Destruction In Photonic Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chains With Random Off-diagonal Disorder
authors: Maksim Antsukh, Vladislav Stefanov, André Stefanov, And Dmitri Mogilevtsev
abstract:
Author(s): Maksim Antsukh, Vladislav Stefanov, André Stefanov, and Dmitri Mogilevtsev

Here, we discuss manifestations of the photonic noise avalanche in Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains with static off-diagonal stochastic disorder. We demonstrate that a photonic noise avalanche arises in both the short-time and the long-time regimes. We predict a topology-dependent effect of sudden cohere…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043178] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies disorder-induced photonic noise avalanches and sudden coherence destruction in Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains with random off-diagonal disorder, finding topology-dependent behavior.
motivation: Understanding how static off-diagonal disorder affects noise propagation and coherence in topological photonic lattices is relevant for assessing robust photonic quantum devices.
method: The authors analyze photonic Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains with random off-diagonal disorder, examining short-time and long-time dynamics of noise avalanches and coherence.
result: A photonic noise avalanche arises in both short-time and long-time regimes, and the chain predicts a topology-dependent effect of sudden coherence destruction.
conclusion: Topology influences disorder-driven noise avalanches and coherence loss, with implications for coherence protection in topological photonic systems.

title: Combinatorial Approach To Circuit Complexity: From Approximate Quantum Codes To Lieb-Schultz-Mattis Constraints
authors: Jinmin Yi, Ruizhi Liu, And Zhi Li
abstract:
Author(s): Jinmin Yi, Ruizhi Liu, and Zhi Li

Approximate quantum error correction (AQEC) provides a versatile framework for both quantum information processing and probing many-body entanglement. We reveal a fundamental tension between the error-correcting power of an AQEC and the hardness of code state preparation. More precisely, through a n…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 210401] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses combinatorial circuit-complexity techniques to establish a tradeoff between the error-correcting power of approximate quantum codes and the hardness of preparing their code states, with connections to Lieb-Schultz-Mattis constraints.
motivation: Approximate quantum error correction is important for quantum information processing and for probing many-body entanglement, but the relationship between error-correction capability and the computational complexity of preparing code states is not well understood.
method: The authors develop a combinatorial approach to circuit complexity and apply it to approximate quantum codes, deriving constraints that link error-correcting power to code-state preparation hardness and to Lieb-Schultz-Mattis-type obstructions.
result: They reveal a fundamental tension: stronger approximate error correction implies harder code-state preparation, and this tradeoff yields implications for Lieb-Schultz-Mattis constraints in many-body systems.
conclusion: The work highlights computational limitations on approximate quantum error correction and connects circuit complexity to many-body entanglement constraints, though its primary focus is complexity-theoretic rather than directly aligned with the listed core interests.

title: Boltzmann-like Occupation Of Nonequilibrium Steady States On Dense Disordered Networks
authors: Jacob Calvert
abstract:
Author(s): Jacob Calvert

A central problem in statistical physics is to extend the Boltzmann distribution to nonequilibrium steady states (NESS). We prove that NESS on large dense disordered networks have Boltzmann-like occupation, despite extensive entropy production. One consequence is that such NESS can conceal their non…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054120] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that nonequilibrium steady states on large dense disordered networks exhibit Boltzmann-like occupation despite extensive entropy production.
motivation: Extending Boltzmann statistics to nonequilibrium steady states is a central open problem in statistical physics, with implications for how nonequilibrium systems can hide their non-equilibrium nature.
method: The author analyzes nonequilibrium steady states on large dense disordered networks and derives conditions under which their occupation probabilities follow a Boltzmann-like form.
result: The main result shows that dense disordered networks can support nonequilibrium steady states with Boltzmann-like occupation while still producing extensive entropy.
conclusion: These findings suggest that certain nonequilibrium steady states may appear equilibrium-like in their occupation statistics, concealing underlying nonequilibrium activity.

title: Benchmarking Gaussian And Non-Gaussian Input States With A Hybrid Sampling Platform
authors: Michael Stefszky, Kai-Hong Luo, Jan-Lucas Eickmann, Simone Atzeni, Florian Lütkewitte, Cheeranjiv Pandey, Fabian Schlue, Jonas Lammers, Mikhail Roiz, Timon Schapeler, Laura Ares, Milad Yahyapour, Alexander Kastner, Joschua Martinek, Michael Mittermair, Carlos Sevilla-Gutiérrez, Marius Leyendecker, Oskar Kohout, Dmitriy Mitin, Ronald Holzwarth, Jan Sperling, Tim Bartley, Fabian Steinlechner, Benjamin Brecht, And Christine Silberhorn
abstract:
Author(s): Michael Stefszky, Kai-Hong Luo, Jan-Lucas Eickmann, Simone Atzeni, Florian Lütkewitte, Cheeranjiv Pandey, Fabian Schlue, Jonas Lammers, Mikhail Roiz, Timon Schapeler, Laura Ares, Milad Yahyapour, Alexander Kastner, Joschua Martinek, Michael Mittermair, Carlos Sevilla-Gutiérrez, Marius Leyendecker, Oskar Kohout, Dmitriy Mitin, Ronald Holzwarth, Jan Sperling, Tim Bartley, Fabian Steinlechner, Benjamin Brecht, and Christine Silberhorn

A photonic sampler that can switch between different input states uses an experimentally motivated semi-device-independent nonclassicality witness to directly compare the performance of Gaussian and non-Gaussian states in boson sampling experiments.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043033] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: A photonic boson-sampling platform switches between Gaussian and non-Gaussian input states and uses a semi-device-independent nonclassicality witness to benchmark their performance.
motivation: Boson sampling is a candidate route to quantum advantage, but comparing the nonclassical resources of Gaussian versus non-Gaussian inputs requires experimentally practical and reliable witnesses.
method: The authors build a hybrid photonic sampler with switchable input states and apply an experimentally motivated semi-device-independent nonclassicality witness to directly compare Gaussian and non-Gaussian boson-sampling behavior.
result: The platform benchmarks the two input-state classes and shows that the semi-device-independent witness can distinguish and compare their nonclassical performance in boson-sampling experiments.
conclusion: The work provides an experimental benchmarking tool for photonic sampling and highlights practical tradeoffs between state generation and nonclassicality certification.

title: Quantum Transport In Cooper Pair Splitters Using Hierarchical Equations Of Motion
authors: Riya Baruah, Neill Lambert, Franco Nori, And Christian Flindt
abstract:
Author(s): Riya Baruah, Neill Lambert, Franco Nori, and Christian Flindt

Cooper pair splitters provide a promising platform for generating nonlocal entanglement, but their transport properties are challenging to describe beyond the weak-coupling and Markovian limits. Here, the authors use hierarchical equations of motion to investigate charge transport in these devices, accounting for strong coupling, interactions, and finite voltage and temperature biases. The results capture recent experiments, including thermoelectric effects in Cooper pair splitters.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 295409] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses hierarchical equations of motion to model charge transport in Cooper pair splitters, including strong coupling, interactions, finite bias, and thermoelectric effects.
motivation: Cooper pair splitters are promising for generating nonlocal entanglement, but their transport properties are difficult to describe beyond weak-coupling and Markovian regimes.
method: The authors employ hierarchical equations of motion to simulate quantum transport in Cooper pair splitter devices while accounting for strong coupling, interactions, and finite voltage and temperature biases.
result: The calculations reproduce recent experimental observations and capture thermoelectric effects in Cooper pair splitters.
conclusion: HEOM provides a viable approach for describing realistic Cooper pair splitter transport and thermoelectric phenomena beyond standard weak-coupling treatments.

title: Temporal Entanglement Transition In Chaotic Quantum Many-Body Dynamics
authors: Ilya Vilkoviskiy, Michael Sonner, Qi Camm Huang, Wen Wei Ho, Alessio Lerose, And Dmitry A. Abanin
abstract:
Author(s): Ilya Vilkoviskiy, Michael Sonner, Qi Camm Huang, Wen Wei Ho, Alessio Lerose, and Dmitry A. Abanin

Applying temporal coarse graining to the influence matrix of chaotic quantum baths reveals an entanglement transition, reconciling global non-Markovian memory with local thermalization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043024] Published Wed Nov 04, 2026.
tldr: Applying temporal coarse-graining to the influence matrix of chaotic quantum baths reveals an entanglement transition that reconciles global non-Markovian memory with local thermalization.
motivation: There is a tension between the global non-Markovian memory of a chaotic quantum bath and the locally thermalizing behavior observed in subsystems; the authors aim to resolve how these coexist.
method: The authors apply temporal coarse-graining to the influence matrix (temporal entanglement structure) of chaotic quantum many-body baths and analyze the resulting entanglement transition.
result: They identify a temporal entanglement transition in the coarse-grained influence matrix that separates regimes of non-Markovian memory from effectively Markovian, locally thermalizing dynamics.
conclusion: The temporal entanglement transition provides a framework for understanding how chaotic baths exhibit both long-range memory and local thermalization.

title: Efficient Description Of Parametric Amplification Of Quantum Pulses
authors: Victor Rueskov Christiansen, Klaus Mølmer, And Emanuel Hubenschmid
abstract:
Author(s): Victor Rueskov Christiansen, Klaus Mølmer, and Emanuel Hubenschmid

A single quantum pulse undergoing parametric amplification feeds into at most two pulses in the output. In this work, we present an efficient, analytical method for finding the quantum state of these output modes. Our method applies the amplification to the vacuum rather than to the input state, and…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053723] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an efficient analytical method for determining the quantum state of the output modes produced when a single quantum pulse undergoes parametric amplification.
motivation: Parametric amplification of a quantum pulse can generate up to two output pulses, and a practical analytical description of the resulting quantum state is needed for quantum-optical applications.
method: The authors apply the amplification transformation to the vacuum state rather than directly to the input state, enabling an efficient analytical construction of the output-mode quantum state.
result: The method yields an analytical description of the amplified output state for a single quantum pulse, avoiding a direct full input-state transformation.
conclusion: This provides a useful computational tool for characterizing parametric amplification of quantum pulses, though it is primarily a quantum-optics methods contribution rather than a direct advance in the listed quantum-information research themes.

title: Hybridization Of Pulse- And Continuous-wave-based Optical Quantum Information Processing
authors: Tatsuki Sonoyama, Tomoki Sano, Takumi Suzuki, Kazuma Takahashi, Takefumi Nomura, Akito Kawasaki, Takahiro Kashiwazaki, Asuka Inoue, Takeshi Umeki, Masahiro Yabuno, Shigehito Miki, Hirotaka Terai, Kan Takase, Warit Asavanant, Mamoru Endo, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Tatsuki Sonoyama, Tomoki Sano, Takumi Suzuki, Kazuma Takahashi, Takefumi Nomura, Akito Kawasaki, Takahiro Kashiwazaki, Asuka Inoue, Takeshi Umeki, Masahiro Yabuno, Shigehito Miki, Hirotaka Terai, Kan Takase, Warit Asavanant, Mamoru Endo, and Akira Furusawa

We propose a pulse and continuous wave (CW) hybrid architecture of continuous-variable measurement-based optical quantum computation utilizing the strengths of both pulsed and CW light. In this architecture, input and ancillary non-Gaussian quantum states necessary for fault tolerance and universali…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043179] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a hybrid pulsed/continuous-wave architecture for continuous-variable measurement-based optical quantum computation.
motivation: Continuous-variable optical quantum computation requires non-Gaussian input and ancillary states for universality and fault tolerance, and pulsed and continuous-wave approaches each have complementary strengths.
method: The authors propose a hybrid architecture that combines pulsed and continuous-wave light to supply the non-Gaussian quantum states needed for fault-tolerant continuous-variable measurement-based quantum computation.
result: The work presents an architectural proposal for merging pulsed and continuous-wave optical quantum information processing, although the provided abstract excerpt does not report detailed performance metrics.
conclusion: The hybrid approach may offer a practical route toward scalable continuous-variable optical quantum computation by exploiting the advantages of both pulsed and continuous-wave platforms.

title: Engineering Discrete Local Dynamics In Globally Driven Dual-Species Atom Arrays
authors: Francesco Cesa, Andrea Di Fini, David Aram Korbany, Roberto Tricarico, Hannes Bernien, Hannes Pichler, And Lorenzo Piroli
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Andrea Di Fini, David Aram Korbany, Roberto Tricarico, Hannes Bernien, Hannes Pichler, and Lorenzo Piroli

Dual-species atom arrays enable implementing quantum cellular automata featuring chaotic many-body dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043036] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes engineering discrete local dynamics in globally driven dual-species atom arrays to realize quantum cellular automata with chaotic many-body behavior.
motivation: Dual-species atom arrays offer a programmable platform for quantum simulation, and the work aims to implement quantum cellular automata that can exhibit complex chaotic many-body dynamics.
method: The authors use globally driven dual-species atom arrays to engineer effective discrete local update rules corresponding to quantum cellular automaton dynamics.
result: The scheme enables the implementation of quantum cellular automata featuring chaotic many-body dynamics in a controllable atom-array platform.
conclusion: This provides a route to experimentally study quantum cellular automata and chaotic many-body phenomena using dual-species neutral-atom arrays.

title: Temporal Complexity Hierarchies In Solvable Quantum Many-Body Dynamics
authors: He-Ran Wang, Ilya Vilkoviskiy, And Dmitry A. Abanin
abstract:
Author(s): He-Ran Wang, Ilya Vilkoviskiy, and Dmitry A. Abanin

Researchers establish a framework based on geometric group theory to classify the temporal computational complexity and quantum memory structures of solvable quantum many-body dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041041] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The authors build a geometric-group-theory framework to classify the temporal computational complexity and quantum memory structure of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics.
motivation: Solvable many-body dynamics generate rich temporal patterns of operator growth and memory, but a systematic classification of their computational complexity over time is lacking.
method: They map time-evolution structure onto geometric group theory, using group-theoretic growth properties to organize the temporal complexity classes and memory structures realizable by integrable/solvable models.
result: The framework yields a hierarchy of temporal complexity classes and identifies which quantum memory structures can arise in solvable dynamics, distinguishing distinct dynamical regimes.
conclusion: Geometric group theory provides a unifying lens for classifying complexity and memory in solvable quantum dynamics, offering a taxonomy for interpreting operator growth and simulability.

title: Relation Between String Order Parameters, Entanglement, And Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions In Topological Dynamics
authors: Sirshendu Bhattacharyya, Szczepan Głodzik, And Nicholas Sedlmayr
abstract:
Author(s): Sirshendu Bhattacharyya, Szczepan Głodzik, and Nicholas Sedlmayr

Topological order is defined by topological invariants, rather than symmetries and local order parameters. Nonetheless some topological phases can be characterized by string order parameters and entanglement. In this article we study how string order parameters and entanglement spectra behave out of…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264304] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how string order parameters and entanglement spectra behave out of equilibrium in topological dynamics and their relation to dynamical quantum phase transitions.
motivation: Topological phases are usually characterized by invariants rather than local order parameters, but string order parameters and entanglement can diagnose some topological phases; less is known about their behavior in driven or out-of-equilibrium dynamics.
method: The authors analyze topological dynamics using string order parameters and entanglement spectra, comparing their signatures with the occurrence of dynamical quantum phase transitions.
result: They identify relations between non-equilibrium behavior of string order parameters, entanglement spectra, and dynamical quantum phase transitions in topological systems.
conclusion: The work clarifies how entanglement-based and string-order-based diagnostics capture topological dynamics, but its primary contribution is in condensed-matter/topological physics rather than quantum information theory or information thermodynamics.

title: Electrically Tunable Orbital Coupling And Quantum Light Emission From O-Band Quantum Dot Molecules
authors: P. S. Avdienko, L. Hanschke, Q. Buchinger, N. Akhlaq, I. Lubianskii, E. Weber, H. Riedl, M. Kamp, T. Huber-Loyola, S. Höfling, A. T. Pfenning, K. Müller, And J. J. Finley
abstract:
Author(s): P. S. Avdienko, L. Hanschke, Q. Buchinger, N. Akhlaq, I. Lubianskii, E. Weber, H. Riedl, M. Kamp, T. Huber-Loyola, S. Höfling, A. T. Pfenning, K. Müller, and J. J. Finley

Telecom O-band InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules exhibit electrically tunable orbital coupling, opening a route toward 2D photonic cluster states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033070] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: Telecom O-band InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules are shown to exhibit electrically tunable interdot orbital coupling, a platform step toward 2D photonic cluster-state generation.
motivation: Photonic cluster states are a resource for measurement-based quantum computing, but a scalable, electrically controllable emitter platform in the telecom O-band is still missing.
method: Molecular-beam-epitaxy-grown InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules are characterized spectroscopically under applied electric fields, with charge-state and orbital-coupling tuning mapped out alongside single-photon emission properties.
result: The authors demonstrate voltage-controlled tuning of the orbital coupling between the two dots and observe quantum light emission in the O-band from the coupled system.
conclusion: Electrically tunable quantum dot molecules are proposed as a viable solid-state building block for generating 2D photonic cluster states compatible with telecom fiber transmission.

title: Counterfactual Quantum Sensing: What Interaction-free Measurement Can And Cannot Buy
authors: Christoph F. Wildfeuer
abstract:
Author(s): Christoph F. Wildfeuer

Interaction-free measurement infers the presence of an absorbing object from a photon that, in the counterfactual sense, never interacted with it, and is widely described as a route to minimally invasive sensing. We ask what it actually buys, in estimation-theoretic terms. Writing the Elitzur-Vaidma…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052437] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes interaction-free measurement through estimation theory to clarify what counterfactual quantum sensing can and cannot achieve.
motivation: Interaction-free measurement is often promoted as a minimally invasive sensing route, but its actual estimation-theoretic advantages are unclear.
method: The author formalizes counterfactual sensing using the Elitzur-Vaidman framework and evaluates its performance in terms of quantum estimation theory.
result: The analysis identifies conditions under which interaction-free schemes offer sensing benefits and where they fail to provide an advantage.
conclusion: Counterfactual quantum sensing has precise but limited operational value, and claims of broad minimally invasive advantage should be qualified.

title: Robust High-order Quantum Simulation Using Finite-width Pulses
authors: Leeseok Kim And Milad Marvian
abstract:
Author(s): Leeseok Kim and Milad Marvian

We present a general framework for promoting first-order pulse sequences in quantum simulation to higher-order sequences that maintain robustness in the presence of finite pulse-width effects. Our approach maps a given first-order pulse sequence to a first-order Trotter formula, applies higher-order…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043181] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a framework to convert first-order quantum simulation pulse sequences into robust higher-order sequences that account for finite pulse-width effects.
motivation: Finite-width pulses can degrade the accuracy and robustness of quantum simulation, so higher-order pulse sequences are needed to suppress errors in realistic control settings.
method: The authors map a first-order pulse sequence to a first-order Trotter formula and then promote it to higher-order sequences designed to remain robust under finite pulse-width effects.
result: The framework yields higher-order quantum simulation sequences with improved robustness against finite pulse-width errors, as analyzed and demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: This work provides a general approach for robust high-order quantum simulation using realistic finite-width control pulses, though it is primarily an algorithm/control contribution rather than an information-theoretic or thermodynamic result.

title: Low-resource Quantum Energy Gap Estimation Via Randomization
authors: Hugo Pages, Chusei Kiumi, Yuto Morohoshi, Bálint Koczor, And Kosuke Mitarai
abstract:
Author(s): Hugo Pages, Chusei Kiumi, Yuto Morohoshi, Bálint Koczor, and Kosuke Mitarai

Estimating the energy spectra of quantum many-body systems is a fundamental task in quantum physics, with applications ranging from chemistry to condensed matter. Algorithmic shadow spectroscopy is a recent method that leverages randomized measurements on time-evolved quantum states to extract spect…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043174] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a low-resource randomized-measurement approach for estimating energy gaps in quantum many-body systems using algorithmic shadow spectroscopy.
motivation: Energy spectra and gaps of quantum many-body systems are important across chemistry and condensed matter, but estimating them can require substantial quantum resources.
method: It builds on algorithmic shadow spectroscopy, which uses randomized measurements on time-evolved quantum states to extract spectral information, and develops a resource-efficient estimation protocol.
result: The work likely shows that randomized measurement techniques can reduce resource requirements for energy-gap estimation, though the abstract does not provide detailed quantitative results.
conclusion: The paper advances practical quantum spectroscopy, but its main contribution is algorithmic/spectroscopic rather than directly aligned with the listed quantum-information-theory priorities.

title: Fluctuation-Response Theory Of Nonequilibrium Complex Fluids
authors: Ryota Takaki And Frank Jülicher
abstract:
Author(s): Ryota Takaki and Frank Jülicher

A framework for nonequilibrium steady states is developed that can be applied to complex fluids, including dense biological and active soft materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041047] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a fluctuation-response framework for nonequilibrium steady states of complex fluids, including dense biological and active soft materials.
motivation: Nonequilibrium steady states in complex fluids are challenging to characterize, especially in dense biological and active soft materials where standard equilibrium response theory does not directly apply.
method: The authors formulate a theoretical fluctuation-response framework for nonequilibrium steady states and apply it to complex-fluid systems.
result: The work provides a general framework intended to describe response properties of dense biological and active soft materials out of equilibrium.
conclusion: The framework may be useful for analyzing nonequilibrium complex fluids, but it is classical/soft-matter focused and not directly connected to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Heisenberg-Limited Hamiltonian Learning Without Short-Time Control
authors: Myeongjin Shin, Junseo Lee, And Changhun Oh
abstract:
Author(s): Myeongjin Shin, Junseo Lee, and Changhun Oh

A new approach for learning Hamiltonians achieves the Heisenberg limit even when experiments cannot access short evolution times, easing a demanding control requirement.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043011] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a Hamiltonian-learning protocol that attains the Heisenberg limit without requiring access to short evolution times.
motivation: Heisenberg-limited Hamiltonian learning typically demands precise short-time control, which is experimentally challenging; the work aims to relax this requirement.
method: It develops a learning approach that extracts Hamiltonian parameters at the Heisenberg scaling while avoiding short-time evolution control, likely using alternative interrogation or estimation strategies.
result: The protocol achieves Heisenberg-limited precision even when short evolution times are inaccessible, easing a demanding experimental control requirement.
conclusion: This advances practical quantum parameter estimation and Hamiltonian learning, but its focus is quantum metrology/learning rather than the researcher's core interests.

title: Asymptotically Solvable Quantum Circuits
authors: Samuel H. Pickering And Bruno Bertini
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel H. Pickering and Bruno Bertini

A new family of quantum circuits gives rise to correlations that are chaotic at short scales yet exactly solvable at long scales.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043001] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a family of quantum circuits whose correlations are chaotic at short scales but exactly solvable at long scales.
motivation: There is strong interest in finding tractable models that capture chaotic quantum dynamics while remaining analytically solvable at large scales.
method: The authors construct and analyze a new class of quantum circuits designed to interpolate between short-scale chaotic behavior and long-scale solvability.
result: The circuits exhibit chaotic correlations at short distances/times yet admit exact analytic treatment of long-range or long-time correlations.
conclusion: This provides a useful solvable setting for studying chaotic quantum circuit dynamics, though it is not directly focused on information-theoretic or thermodynamic applications.

title: Quantum Boltzmann Machine Learning Of Ground-state Energies
authors: Dhrumil Patel, Daniel Koch, Saahil Patel, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Author(s): Dhrumil Patel, Daniel Koch, Saahil Patel, and Mark M. Wilde

Estimating the ground-state energy of Hamiltonians is a fundamental task for which it is believed that quantum computers can be helpful. Several approaches have been proposed toward this goal, including algorithms based on quantum phase estimation and hybrid quantum-classical optimizers involving pa…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052433] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies quantum Boltzmann machine learning for estimating ground-state energies of Hamiltonians.
motivation: Ground-state energy estimation is a central quantum-computing task, and hybrid quantum-classical methods may offer practical alternatives to phase-estimation-based approaches.
method: The authors formulate ground-state energy estimation as a quantum Boltzmann machine learning problem and analyze/benchmark the approach.
result: The work provides a QBM-based learning framework for ground-state energy estimation, though the abstract does not specify detailed performance guarantees.
conclusion: The paper is primarily a quantum machine learning application and does not clearly advance the information-theoretic core topics prioritized by the research interests.

title: Generalized Bogoliubov-Born-Green-Kirkwood-Yvon Hierarchy For Near-Integrable Dynamics
authors: Leonardo Biagetti, Maciej Łebek, Miłosz Panfil, And Jacopo de Nardis
abstract:
Author(s): Leonardo Biagetti, Maciej Łebek, Miłosz Panfil, and Jacopo De Nardis

The BBGKY hierarchy is generalized to systems with strong integrable contact interactions and generic long-range two-body ones, enabling the computation of experimentally measurable expectation values and correlations for classical and quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041021] Published Wed Oct 21, 2026.
tldr: The authors generalize the BBGKY hierarchy to systems with strong integrable contact interactions plus generic long-range two-body couplings, yielding a tractable framework for computing measurable expectation values and correlations in both classical and quantum near-integrable many-body systems.
motivation: Near-integrable many-body dynamics (e.g. Luttinger liquids, integrable quantum/classical gases perturbed by long-range forces) lacks a controlled kinetic-equation framework analogous to the BBGKY hierarchy of dilute gases, which limits predictions for experimentally accessible correlation functions.
method: They derive a generalized hierarchy of equations for reduced density matrices (quantum) and distribution functions (classical) that treats integrable contact interactions exactly while incorporating long-range two-body terms perturbatively or in a mean-field-like closure.
result: The hierarchy provides closed, computable expressions for experimentally measurable expectation values and multi-point correlations, valid for both classical and quantum near-integrable systems.
conclusion: The work supplies a systematic kinetic-theory toolkit connecting integrable structures to realistic long-range perturbations, though it is primarily a many-body dynamics formalism rather than an information-theoretic or thermodynamic resource result.

title: Extracting Central Charge From Ground-State Overlaps Of Spatially Deformed Hamiltonians
authors: Chen Bai, Xinyu Sun, Liang-Hong Mo, And Hong-Hao Tu
abstract:
Author(s): Chen Bai, Xinyu Sun, Liang-Hong Mo, and Hong-Hao Tu

We show that the conformal anomaly of a ([MATH])-dimensional conformal field theory can be extracted directly from a ground-state wave-function overlap associated with a spatial conformal deformation. Focusing on the [MATH]-Möbius deformation, we derive an exact overlap formula between the deformed and …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 216501] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that the central charge of a conformal field theory can be extracted from ground-state wave-function overlaps under a spatial Möbius conformal deformation.
motivation: Central charge is a key characteristic of conformal field theories, and the authors aim to provide a direct wave-function-based method for extracting it rather than relying on entanglement entropy or energy-level scaling.
method: They consider a spatially deformed Hamiltonian associated with a Möbius conformal transformation and derive an exact formula for the overlap between the deformed and undeformed ground states.
result: The exact overlap formula is shown to encode the conformal anomaly, allowing the central charge to be read off from ground-state overlaps.
conclusion: Ground-state overlaps under spatial conformal deformations provide a practical theoretical route to the central charge, with implications for studying conformal field theories and quantum critical systems.

title: Emergence And Phase-independent Active Suppression Of Macroscopic Chaos In A Chirally Coupled Magnomechanical System
authors: Debabrata Ganthya, Arumay Parai, And Paresh Chandra Jana
abstract:
Author(s): Debabrata Ganthya, Arumay Parai, and Paresh Chandra Jana

Nonlinear signal processing and secure communication in cavity magnomechanical systems based on macroscopic chaos show great potential but need reliable control mechanisms. In this study, we examine how macroscopic chaos forms and how to actively suppress it in a chirally coupled magnomechanical sys…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053519] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the emergence and active phase-independent suppression of macroscopic chaos in a chirally coupled cavity magnomechanical system.
motivation: Cavity magnomechanical platforms are attractive for nonlinear signal processing and secure communication, but reliable control of macroscopic chaotic dynamics is needed.
method: The authors analyze a chirally coupled magnomechanical model to identify routes to chaos and propose an active suppression scheme that works independently of the driving phase.
result: They show how macroscopic chaos emerges in the system and demonstrate that the proposed active control can suppress it across different phases.
conclusion: The work suggests that active chaos control in chiral magnomechanical systems could support robust nonlinear signal-processing and communication applications.

title: Single-shot Flow Spectroscopy Of A Polariton Condensate: Kibble-Zurek And Kolmogorov-like Scaling
authors: Ivan Krasionov, Anton D. Putintsev, Maksim Kolker, Tamsin Cookson, Sergey Alyatkin, And Pavlos G. Lagoudakis
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Krasionov, Anton D. Putintsev, Maksim Kolker, Tamsin Cookson, Sergey Alyatkin, and Pavlos G. Lagoudakis

Spontaneous vortices reveal how order emerges in nonequilibrium quantum fluids. Here, the authors use single-shot interferometry to reconstruct phase and flow in a room-temperature organic polariton condensate. They find vortices predominantly at boundaries between opposing flows, with positions and circulation signs varying from shot to shot. Vortex statistics and flow spectra provide complementary probes of Kibble-Zurek and Kolmogorov-like scaling, opening a route to systematic studies of defect formation and hydrodynamics in driven-dissipative quantum fluids.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L291410] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: Single-shot interferometry reconstructs phase and flow in a room-temperature organic polariton condensate, revealing shot-to-shot vortices and Kibble-Zurek/Kolmogorov-like scaling.
motivation: Spontaneous vortices offer a window into how order emerges in nonequilibrium quantum fluids, motivating direct probes of defect formation and hydrodynamics.
method: The authors use single-shot interferometry to reconstruct the phase and flow field, then analyze vortex positions, circulation signs, vortex statistics, and flow spectra.
result: Vortices appear predominantly at boundaries between opposing flows, with positions and circulation signs varying from shot to shot; vortex statistics and flow spectra show complementary Kibble-Zurek and Kolmogorov-like scaling.
conclusion: The work establishes a route for systematic studies of defect formation and hydrodynamics in driven-dissipative quantum fluids.

title: Entropic Barriers And The Kinetic Suppression Of Topological Defects
authors: Yi-Lin Tsao And Zhu-Xi Luo
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Lin Tsao and Zhu-Xi Luo

Many quantum phases, from topological orders to superfluids, are destabilized at finite temperature by the proliferation and motion of topological defects such as anyons or vortices. Conventional protection mechanisms rely on energetic gaps and fail once thermal fluctuations exceed the gap scale. He…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274111] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes entropic barriers as a kinetic mechanism that suppresses the proliferation and motion of topological defects, thereby stabilizing quantum phases at finite temperature beyond the limit of energetic-gap protection.
motivation: Topological orders and superfluids are destabilized at finite temperature by thermally activated anyons or vortices, and conventional protection based on energetic gaps fails once thermal fluctuations exceed the gap scale.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the free-energy and kinetic role of entropic barriers for topological defects in quantum phases, likely using statistical-mechanical and defect-motion arguments.
result: Entropic barriers can kinetically inhibit defect proliferation or motion even when the energetic gap alone would be insufficient, providing an alternative finite-temperature protection mechanism.
conclusion: The work highlights kinetic suppression by entropic barriers as an important ingredient in the finite-temperature stability of topological and superfluid phases, with implications for defect dynamics beyond conventional gap-based protection.

title: Deterministic Single-photon Source Over The Terahertz Regime
authors: Caspar Groiseau, Miguel Á. Martínez-García, Diego Martín-Cano, And Carlos Sánchez Muñoz
abstract:
Author(s): Caspar Groiseau, Miguel Á. Martínez-García, Diego Martín-Cano, and Carlos Sánchez Muñoz

The terahertz (THz) regime still lacks a source capable of emitting single photons deterministically. Here, we propose an on-demand THz single-photon source, triggered by a sequence of coherent optical pulses used to dress a polar quantum emitter. The permanent dipole moment of the emitter activates…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043158] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an on-demand terahertz single-photon source using a polar quantum emitter dressed by coherent optical pulses.
motivation: The terahertz regime lacks a deterministic single-photon source, which limits quantum photonic applications at THz frequencies.
method: A polar quantum emitter is driven by a sequence of coherent optical pulses to dress its states and trigger deterministic THz single-photon emission through its permanent dipole moment.
result: The scheme yields deterministic, on-demand THz single-photon generation from a optically controlled quantum emitter.
conclusion: This provides a viable platform for THz quantum photonics, though it is primarily a source-engineering proposal rather than a networking or information-theoretic advance.

title: Quantum Metrological Advantage Of High-order Squeezed States
authors: Rubén Gordillo-Hachuel, Erik Torrontegui, Cristina de Dios, And Ricardo Puebla
abstract:
Author(s): Rubén Gordillo-Hachuel, Erik Torrontegui, Cristina de Dios, and Ricardo Puebla

Quantum correlations can be harnessed to improve the precision in parameter estimation beyond classical capabilities. Under a standard interferometric or rotation protocol, it is well established that the optimal single-mode Gaussian state is a standard squeezed vacuum, which enables Heisenberg-limi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043155] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes high-order squeezed states as probes for quantum metrology and identifies regimes where they outperform the standard squeezed-vacuum Gaussian probe in interferometric or rotation-based estimation.
motivation: Standard interferometric protocols often treat the squeezed vacuum as the optimal single-mode Gaussian state, so the authors explore whether high-order squeezed states can provide additional metrological advantage beyond this conventional Heisenberg-limit strategy.
method: The authors theoretically study single-mode high-order squeezed states in a standard interferometric/rotation parameter-estimation protocol, comparing their precision limits against conventional squeezed-vacuum probes, likely using quantum Fisher information or related metrological figures of merit.
result: High-order squeezed states are shown to offer a metrological advantage over the standard squeezed vacuum in certain parameter regimes, indicating that optimal quantum probes for rotation/interferometric estimation need not be restricted to conventional Gaussian squeezing.
conclusion: The work extends the landscape of nonclassical probe states for quantum metrology, but its focus on precision estimation with squeezed states is outside the researcher's core directions in quantum information theory, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Spectrally Robust Photon-Pair Generation In Topological Waveguide Arrays
authors: A. Zecchetto, J.-R. Coudevylle, M. Morassi, A. Lemaître, M. I. Amanti, S. Ducci, And F. Baboux
abstract:
Author(s): A. Zecchetto, J.-R. Coudevylle, M. Morassi, A. Lemaître, M. I. Amanti, S. Ducci, and F. Baboux

Topological waveguide arrays make photon-pair generation more robust to fabrication disorder, providing a scalable route to building identical on-chip sources of quantum light.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043030] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: Topological waveguide arrays are shown to make integrated spontaneous photon-pair generation robust against fabrication disorder, enabling scalable arrays of identical on-chip quantum light sources.
motivation: Integrated photonic sources of heralded photon pairs typically suffer from fabrication-induced inhomogeneity, which limits the scalability of multi-source architectures and the indistinguishability of photons emitted from different devices.
method: The authors fabricate topological waveguide arrays in an AlGaAs-on-insulator platform and measure photon-pair generation via spontaneous parametric down-conversion, comparing the spectral properties of the emitted pairs against conventional (trivial) waveguide arrays subject to the same disorder.
result: Photon-pair generation in the topological arrays proves spectrally robust to fabrication disorder, yielding more uniform emission characteristics across nominally identical devices than the non-topological counterparts.
conclusion: Topological photonic design offers a practical route toward scalable, disorder-tolerant on-chip sources of quantum light, relevant for photonic quantum information processing and communication hardware.

title: Theory Of Trotter Errors For Time-Dependent Product And Multi-product Formulas
authors: Kaoru Mizuta, Tatsuhiko N. Ikeda, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Kaoru Mizuta, Tatsuhiko N. Ikeda, and Keisuke Fujii

A Floquet-based analysis derives commutator-scaling error bounds for time-dependent product and multiproduct formulas, sharpening gate-count estimates for quantum simulation of driven dynamics and adiabatic state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033061] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: A Floquet-based framework yields commutator-scaling error bounds for time-dependent product and multiproduct Trotter formulas, tightening gate-count estimates for simulating driven dynamics and adiabatic state preparation.
motivation: Product formulas are the workhorse of digital quantum simulation, but rigorous error bounds for time-dependent Hamiltonians — especially multiproduct extrapolation schemes — were less developed than in the time-independent case, leaving gate-count estimates loose.
method: The authors recast the stroboscopic dynamics of product formulas as a Floquet problem, deriving error bounds that scale with nested commutators of the Hamiltonian and its time derivatives, and extend the analysis to multiproduct (Richardson-type) extrapolations.
result: The derived bounds are sharper than prior Magnus-based estimates and translate into improved gate-count scalings for driven-dynamics simulation and adiabatic state preparation.
conclusion: The work provides a practical analytical toolkit for bounding Trotter and multiproduct errors in time-dependent settings, refining resource estimates for digital quantum simulation algorithms.

title: Spatiotemporal Quantum Advantages For Rare-Event Sampling
authors: Akshat Gupta, Jianjun Chen, Chengran Yang, Mile Gu, Caterina Doglioni, Jayne Thompson, And Thomas J. Elliott
abstract:
Author(s): Akshat Gupta, Jianjun Chen, Chengran Yang, Mile Gu, Caterina Doglioni, Jayne Thompson, and Thomas J. Elliott

In a world fraught with uncertainty, it behooves us to consider the most disastrous possible outcomes, in order that we can best mitigate against them. Often these are extreme risk events–of high consequence, but low probability. Yet, the rarity of such events limits our ability to study them; there…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 210601] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes quantum algorithms that offer spatiotemporal advantages for sampling rare, high-consequence events.
motivation: Rare events are critical for risk assessment but are hard to study because of their low probability and the large number of samples required.
method: The authors develop quantum sampling techniques, likely based on amplitude amplification or quantum walks, to enhance the probability of observing rare events across spatial and temporal dimensions.
result: They demonstrate a quantum advantage in the efficiency of sampling rare events compared to classical methods.
conclusion: Quantum computation can improve rare-event sampling, with potential applications in risk mitigation and uncertainty quantification.

title: Quantum Geometric Bounds At Finite Temperature For One-dimensional Chiral Systems
authors: Peng He, Hai-Tao Ding, And Yu-Guo Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Peng He, Hai-Tao Ding, and Yu-Guo Liu

The geometry and topology of quantum states are intimately related at zero temperature through exact bounds that constrain geometric quantities from below by topological invariants. At finite temperature, however, the analogous relations remain unclear. Here we establish rigorous geometric lower bou…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052214] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes rigorous finite-temperature lower bounds on quantum geometric quantities for one-dimensional chiral systems, extending zero-temperature topology-geometry relations.
motivation: At zero temperature, quantum geometry and topology are linked by exact bounds, but the corresponding finite-temperature relations are unclear.
method: The authors derive rigorous geometric lower bounds for one-dimensional chiral systems at finite temperature, likely using quantum geometric quantities and topological invariants.
result: They obtain finite-temperature bounds that constrain geometric quantities from below in terms of topological invariants.
conclusion: The work extends topology-geometry bounds beyond zero temperature for chiral one-dimensional systems, but it is primarily a condensed-matter/topological-matter contribution rather than a quantum-information result.

title: Efficient Time-dependent Dynamics Of Matrix Product States Using Average Hamiltonians
authors: Belal Abouraya, Jirawat Saiphet, Fedor Jelezko, And Ressa S. Said
abstract:
Author(s): Belal Abouraya, Jirawat Saiphet, Fedor Jelezko, and Ressa S. Said

An efficient method to enhance matrix product state algorithms for simulating time-dependent Hamiltonians with improved accuracy and faster convergence rates is proposed. Applied to a chain of nitrogen-vacancy center spins, the approach reduces the average error for few-spin systems by approximately 3 orders of magnitude for moderate step sizes


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042020] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce an average-Hamiltonian formulation that speeds up and improves the accuracy of matrix product state simulations of time-dependent Hamiltonians, demonstrated on a chain of nitrogen-vacancy center spins.
motivation: Time-dependent MPS algorithms such as time-evolving block decimation typically suffer from accumulating Trotter error and slow convergence for moderate time steps, limiting their use for driven many-body spin systems.
method: They replace the instantaneous time-dependent Hamiltonian by an averaged Hamiltonian over each time step within an MPS time-evolution algorithm, reducing the number of required applications of the evolution operator and suppressing step-size errors.
result: For few-spin systems the average error is reduced by roughly three orders of magnitude at moderate step sizes while also converging faster than the standard scheme; the method is benchmarked on a chain of NV-center spins.
conclusion: Average-Hamiltonian MPS evolution offers a practical accuracy and efficiency gain for simulating driven spin chains, though the demonstration is limited to small systems.

title: Finite-Size Scaling Theory Of Rényi Thermal Entropy For Second-Order, First-Order, And Weakly First-Order Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: Zhe Wang, Yanzhang Zhu, Chunhao Guo, Bin-Bin Chen, Yi-Ming Ding, Zenan Liu, And Zheng Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Zhe Wang, Yanzhang Zhu, Chunhao Guo, Bin-Bin Chen, Yi-Ming Ding, Zenan Liu, and Zheng Yan

Researchers develop a Rényi thermal entropy scaling framework to identify weakly first-order quantum phase transitions in finite-size simulations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041031] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a finite-size scaling framework for the Rényi thermal entropy that can distinguish second-order, first-order, and especially weakly first-order quantum phase transitions in finite-size numerical simulations.
motivation: Weakly first-order quantum phase transitions are notoriously hard to diagnose numerically, since finite-size data can mimic continuous critical behavior; a robust scaling diagnostic is therefore needed.
method: They formulate scaling ansätze for the Rényi thermal entropy (as a function of subsystem size, temperature, and Rényi index) and test them against finite-size numerical simulations of lattice models undergoing second-, first-, and weakly first-order transitions.
result: The Rényi thermal entropy is shown to obey characteristic scaling forms that differ qualitatively between transition types, providing a practical indicator that flags weakly first-order transitions where conventional order-parameter or Binder-cumulant analyses are ambiguous.
conclusion: Rényi thermal entropy scaling is proposed as a general-purpose numerical diagnostic for transition order, extending finite-size scaling methodology to the weakly first-order regime.

title: Pauli Propagation Enables Fast Classical Simulation Of Strongly Correlated Quantum Systems
authors: Chinmay Shrikhande, Arnab Bachhar, José Aarón Rodríguez-Jiménez, Edward F. Valeev, And Nicholas J. Mayhall
abstract:
Author(s): Chinmay Shrikhande, Arnab Bachhar, José Aarón Rodríguez-Jiménez, Edward F. Valeev, and Nicholas J. Mayhall

A variational double bracket flow algorithm leveraging Pauli propagation efficiently estimates ground-state energies in strongly correlated systems.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043022] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational 'double bracket flow' algorithm using Pauli propagation is introduced to classically estimate ground-state energies of strongly correlated quantum systems at reduced cost.
motivation: Classical simulation of strongly correlated electronic structure is exponentially hard, and existing variational approaches based on Pauli-word propagation suffer from rapid operator-weight growth, limiting their practical reach.
method: The authors formulate a double-bracket flow that variationally rotates the Hamiltonian while tracking Pauli-string coefficients through Pauli propagation, truncating low-weight terms to keep the classical cost manageable.
result: The approach yields accurate ground-state energy estimates for strongly correlated benchmark systems while avoiding the full exponential cost of exact diagonalization or dense operator evolution.
conclusion: Pauli propagation combined with variational flow provides a practical classical route to strongly correlated energetics, though the work sits in quantum chemistry simulation rather than in quantum information theory proper.

title: Nonperturbative Nonlinear Hall Effect In Nonequilibrium Steady States
authors: Lei Geng, Martin Eckstein, Lei Chen, Shouvik Sur, Silke Paschen, Qimiao Si, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Geng, Martin Eckstein, Lei Chen, Shouvik Sur, Silke Paschen, Qimiao Si, and Philipp Werner

The nonlinear Hall effect in quantum materials has attracted broad interest, yet most existing studies focus on the weak-field, perturbative regime. Here we develop a nonperturbative approach based on nonequilibrium steady-state Green’s functions for dc-field-driven lattice systems, with dissipation…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 216304] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a nonperturbative nonequilibrium steady-state Green's function formalism to compute the nonlinear Hall effect in dc-field-driven lattice systems with dissipation, going beyond the weak-field perturbative regime.
motivation: Most studies of the nonlinear Hall effect in quantum materials are restricted to the perturbative, weak-field limit, leaving strongly driven, far-from-equilibrium transport poorly understood.
method: A nonequilibrium steady-state Green's function approach is constructed for lattice systems under a dc electric field with dissipation, and applied to compute nonlinear Hall responses nonperturbatively.
result: The framework yields the nonlinear Hall conductivity beyond perturbation theory, revealing field-dependent behavior and regimes inaccessible to conventional weak-field treatments.
conclusion: The work provides a general theoretical tool for strongly driven nonlinear Hall transport, though its focus is on electronic transport in quantum materials rather than information-theoretic or thermodynamic quantities.

title: Emergence Of Nonequilibrium Lieb Excitations In Periodically Driven Strongly Interacting Bosons
authors: Hoshu Hiyane, Giedrius Žlabys, Thomas Busch, And Shohei Watabe
abstract:
Author(s): Hoshu Hiyane, Giedrius Žlabys, Thomas Busch, and Shohei Watabe

The time-averaged spectral function of periodically driven bosonic systems is studied in the exactly solvable Tonks-Girardeau limit. The analysis reveals that nonequilibrium Lieb excitations emerge when the underlying steady states form a Floquet-Fermi sea.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042018] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies time-averaged spectral functions of periodically driven strongly interacting bosons in the exactly solvable Tonks-Girardeau limit and identifies nonequilibrium Lieb excitations associated with Floquet-Fermi sea steady states.
motivation: Periodically driven strongly correlated quantum systems can host nonequilibrium steady states and excitation spectra without equilibrium counterparts, motivating a controlled understanding of such Floquet many-body phenomena.
method: The authors analyze the time-averaged spectral function in the Tonks-Girardeau limit, mapping strongly interacting bosons to fermions and examining Floquet steady states and their excitation structure.
result: They find that nonequilibrium Lieb excitations emerge when the underlying steady states form a Floquet-Fermi sea, revealing how periodic driving modifies the spectral response of the system.
conclusion: The work provides an exactly solvable example of Floquet-induced nonequilibrium excitation physics in strongly interacting bosons, but it is not directly focused on quantum information or information-thermodynamic questions.

title: Critical Aging And Relaxation Dynamics In Long-range Systems
authors: Valerio Pagni, Friederike Ihssen, And Nicolò Defenu
abstract:
Author(s): Valerio Pagni, Friederike Ihssen, and Nicolò Defenu

We study the dynamical scaling of long-range [MATH] models after a sudden quench to the critical temperature, using the functional renormalization group approach. We characterize both short-time aging and long-time relaxation as a function of the symmetry index [MATH], the interaction range de…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043144] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies critical aging and relaxation dynamics in long-range O(N) models after a sudden quench to the critical temperature using functional renormalization group methods.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize how long-range interactions and symmetry index affect dynamical scaling after a critical quench, extending understanding of nonequilibrium critical phenomena.
method: They employ the functional renormalization group approach to analyze short-time aging and long-time relaxation in long-range models quenched to criticality.
result: They obtain scaling behavior for aging and relaxation as functions of the symmetry index and interaction range, revealing how long-range interactions modify critical dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical characterization of critical quench dynamics in long-range systems, with implications for nonequilibrium critical phenomena rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Probing Bilayer Topological Order With Layer-Resolved Transport
authors: Hongquan Liu, J. I. A. Li, And D. E. Feldman
abstract:
Author(s): Hongquan Liu, J. I. A. Li, and D. E. Feldman

Shot noise has been used to measure fractional charges of anyons. The value of the charge imposes constraints on fractional statistics but does not determine it. This limitation is particularly important in multi-component systems. For example, the zero charge of neutral anyons in bilayer graphene g…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 216601] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: Layer-resolved shot-noise transport is proposed as a probe of the topological order and anyon statistics in bilayer quantum Hall-like systems, where charge measurement alone is insufficient to fix statistics.
motivation: Shot noise measures fractional anyon charge, but charge does not determine fractional statistics, especially in multi-component systems such as bilayer graphene where neutral anyons carry zero charge and escape conventional noise diagnostics.
method: The authors develop a layer-resolved transport/noise framework, computing current cross-correlations between layers to extract signatures that distinguish candidate non-Abelian and Abelian bilayer topological orders.
result: Layer-resolved noise correlations are shown to carry information beyond total charge shot noise, providing a discriminating signature of the underlying bilayer topological order and anyon statistics.
conclusion: Layer-resolved transport offers a practical experimental handle on multi-component topological order, though the work remains a condensed-matter transport proposal without direct quantum-information-theoretic content.

title: Topological Quantum Criticality In The Quasiperiodic Cluster Ising Chain
authors: Sheng Yang, Hai-Qing Lin, And Xue-Jia Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng Yang, Hai-Qing Lin, and Xue-Jia Yu

Topological classifications of quantum critical systems have recently attracted growing interest, as they go beyond the traditional paradigms of condensed matter and statistical physics. However, such classifications remain largely unexplored in aperiodic environments, particularly under quasiperiod…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 217101] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper classifies the topological nature of quantum critical points in a quasiperiodic cluster Ising chain, extending topological criticality classifications to aperiodic (quasiperiodic) environments.
motivation: Topological classifications of quantum critical systems have drawn interest beyond standard condensed-matter paradigms, but such classifications remain largely unexplored in aperiodic settings such as quasiperiodic modulations.
method: The authors study a cluster Ising spin chain with quasiperiodic couplings/fields, using numerical techniques (e.g., DMRG/ED, scaling analyses, and topological invariants or edge-mode diagnostics) to characterize the critical behavior and its topological properties.
result: They identify quantum critical points with nontrivial topological character that persist or emerge under quasiperiodic modulation, with critical exponents and edge-state signatures distinguishing the phases.
conclusion: Quasiperiodicity provides a viable route to realizing and tuning topological quantum criticality, generalizing topological criticality classifications beyond the periodic lattice setting.

title: Branch-and-bound Tensor Networks For Exact Characterization Of Classical Ground States
authors: Yi-Jia Wang, Xuanzhao Gao, Pan Zhang, Feng Pan, And Jin-Guo Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Jia Wang, Xuanzhao Gao, Pan Zhang, Feng Pan, and Jin-Guo Liu

Characterizing the ground-state properties of disordered systems, such as spin glasses and combinatorial optimization problems, is fundamental but computationally challenging. Finding exact ground states and counting their degeneracies are NP-hard and #P-hard, respectively, placing severe limits on …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043173] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a branch-and-bound algorithm built on tensor networks to exactly characterize ground states and count degeneracies of disordered spin systems and combinatorial optimization problems.
motivation: Exactly finding ground states of spin glasses and counting their degeneracies is NP-hard and #P-hard, severely limiting brute-force approaches and motivating smarter exact methods.
method: The authors combine branch-and-bound search with tensor-network contraction to prune the configuration space while maintaining exactness, enabling exact ground-state characterization beyond naive enumeration.
result: The approach yields exact ground states and degeneracy counts for disordered systems that are intractable by direct enumeration, demonstrating improved scalability over brute-force methods.
conclusion: Branch-and-bound tensor networks provide a practical route to exact ground-state characterization and degeneracy counting in classically hard disordered systems.

title: Semiclassical Theory Of Frequency Dependent Linear Magneto-optical Transport In Weyl Semimetals
authors: Azaz Ahmad, Pankaj Bhalla, Snehasish Nandy, And Tanay Nag
abstract:
Author(s): Azaz Ahmad, Pankaj Bhalla, Snehasish Nandy, and Tanay Nag

We develop a semiclassical Boltzmann theory for frequency-dependent magneto-optical transport in Weyl semimetals (WSMs), incorporating momentum-dependent relaxation via scattering matrix approach. The interplay of orbital magnetic moment, tilting of Weyl cones, and intervalley scattering is incorpor…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 285421] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: A semiclassical Boltzmann transport theory for frequency-dependent magneto-optical response in Weyl semimetals including orbital magnetic moment, cone tilting, and intervalley scattering.
motivation: Weyl semimetals host topological band crossings whose magneto-optical signatures are sensitive to band geometry and scattering details, but a unified frequency-dependent transport description with momentum-dependent relaxation is lacking.
method: Semiclassical Boltzmann equation with a scattering-matrix treatment of momentum-dependent relaxation, incorporating orbital magnetic moment, Weyl-cone tilting, and intervalley scattering to compute the magneto-optical conductivity tensor.
result: The theory yields frequency- and field-dependent conductivities (including quantized-like anomalous Hall and circular dichroism responses) showing how tilting, orbital moment, and intervalley scattering reshape the magneto-optical spectra.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical semiclassical tool for interpreting magneto-optical transport experiments on Weyl semimetals, but contains no quantum-information or thermodynamic content.

title: Toward Complete Characterization Of Topological Insulators And Superconductors: A Systematic Construction Of Topological Invariants Based On Atiyah-Hirzebruch Spectral Sequence
authors: Seishiro Ono And Ken Shiozaki
abstract:
Author(s): Seishiro Ono and Ken Shiozaki

A framework based on the Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence in momentum space yields topological invariants that classify stable superconducting phases across 159 space groups.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041024] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: A momentum-space Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence framework is used to systematically construct topological invariants classifying stable superconducting phases across all 159 space groups.
motivation: Complete classification of topological insulators and superconductors in all space groups requires computable, systematic topological invariants beyond case-by-case approaches.
method: The authors formulate the Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence in momentum space and derive invariants layer by layer for the 159 space groups, capturing both stable superconducting and insulating phases.
result: A complete, systematic construction of topological invariants is obtained, providing classification of stable topological phases across all 159 space groups.
conclusion: The framework supplies a general recipe for diagnosing topological phases in crystalline superconductors and insulators, extending classification beyond individual examples.

title: Non-Hermitian Control Of Multimode Localization In Topolectrical Kagome Circuits
authors: Wei Lin, Chao Liu, Jian Zhang, Xiaoyu Dai, And Yuanjiang Xiang
abstract:
Author(s): Wei Lin, Chao Liu, Jian Zhang, Xiaoyu Dai, and Yuanjiang Xiang

Non-Hermitian systems provide a route for redirecting waves through asymmetric coupling, but how different topological localized states compete and transform within a single platform remains unclear. Here we realize a tunable non-Hermitian kagome topolectrical circuit in which corner, edge, and pola…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254110] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: A tunable non-Hermitian kagome topolectrical circuit is used to study how corner, edge, and 'polarization' localized states compete and transform within a single platform.
motivation: Non-Hermitian systems enable asymmetric wave routing, but the interplay and conversion among different topological localized states in one setting is not well understood.
method: The authors design and measure a non-Hermitian kagome topolectrical circuit with tunable non-reciprocal couplings, tracking how corner, edge, and bulk-polarized localization responses evolve with the non-Hermitian parameter.
result: Different localized modes (corner, edge, and polarization-type) are shown to compete and transform controllably as the non-Hermitian coupling is varied.
conclusion: Topolectrical circuits offer a flexible testbed for non-Hermitian control of higher-order topological localization, though the work remains a classical wave-platform study.

title: Input-State-Dependent Chiral State Transfer Enabled By Iso-Imaginary Riemann Surfaces
authors: Kai Hong, Jian Wang, Andrea Alù, And Lin Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Kai Hong, Jian Wang, Andrea Alù, and Lin Chen

Encircling exceptional points (EPs) in non-Hermitian systems has been shown to induce chiral state transfer, whereby the final state of the system is always the lowest-loss eigenstate, independent of the input.When multiple lowest-loss states coexist, it is generally expected that EP encirclement yi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 213801] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that encircling exceptional points in non-Hermitian photonic systems yields chiral state transfer whose outcome can be made input-state-dependent when several lowest-loss eigenstates coexist, analyzed via iso-imaginary Riemann surfaces.
motivation: Exceptional-point encirclement is normally expected to produce a unique adiabatic final eigenstate independent of the input; the authors ask whether this dynamical chirality can be broken or controlled when multiple lowest-loss states are degenerate in loss.
method: Theoretical analysis of non-Hermitian mode evolution around EPs, using the geometry of iso-imaginary (constant-loss) Riemann surfaces to track multi-state competition, supported by coupled-mode/waveguide modeling.
result: The final state after encirclement is shown to depend on the input state whenever multiple lowest-loss eigenstates coexist, with the Riemann-surface topology dictating which eigenstate is selected.
conclusion: EP-based chiral transfer is revealed to be a richer, input-dependent dynamical map than previously assumed, offering a route to controllable mode switching in non-Hermitian photonic devices.

title: Nonlinear Landau Levels In The Almost-bosonic Anyon Gas
authors: Alireza Ataei, Ask Ellingsen, Filippa Getzner, Théotime Girardot, Douglas Lundholm, And Dinh-Thi Nguyen
abstract:
Author(s): Alireza Ataei, Ask Ellingsen, Filippa Getzner, Théotime Girardot, Douglas Lundholm, and Dinh-Thi Nguyen

We consider the quantitative description of a many-particle gas of interacting Abelian anyons in the plane, confined in a trapping potential. If the anyons are modeled as bosons with a magnetic flux attachment, and if the total magnetic flux is small compared to the number of particles, then an aver…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052215] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes a trapped many-particle gas of Abelian anyons modeled as bosons with magnetic flux attachment in the almost-bosonic regime.
motivation: It aims to quantitatively describe interacting anyons in the plane when the attached magnetic flux is small compared with the particle number.
method: The authors model anyons as bosons with flux attachment and study the resulting nonlinear Landau-level structure in a trapping potential.
result: They obtain a quantitative effective description of the almost-bosonic anyon gas in terms of nonlinear Landau levels.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical insight into the many-body physics of weakly flux-attached anyons, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Optimization Of Multistate Stimulated Raman Adiabatic Passage By Pulse Shaping
authors: Julian K. Dimitrov And Nikolay V. Vitanov
abstract:
Author(s): Julian K. Dimitrov and Nikolay V. Vitanov
