We propose a pulse-shaping method for improving population transfer in multistate stimulated Raman adiabatic passage with nearest-neighbor couplings only. The method extends the quasiparallel-eigenenergy approach, previously used for two- and three-state systems, to multistate chains without introdu…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053108] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a pulse-shaping method to improve population transfer in multistate stimulated Raman adiabatic passage (STIRAP) chains with nearest-neighbor couplings.
motivation: Multistate STIRAP is useful for robust coherent population transfer, but achieving high fidelity in longer chains can be challenging without complex couplings.
method: The authors extend the quasiparallel-eigenenergy approach, previously applied to two- and three-state systems, to multistate STIRAP chains and optimize the pulse shapes accordingly.
result: The shaped pulses improve population transfer efficiency in nearest-neighbor-coupled multistate chains compared to conventional STIRAP protocols.
conclusion: Pulse shaping based on quasiparallel eigenenergies provides a practical route to enhanced multistate STIRAP, though the work is specialized quantum control rather than aligned with the specified research directions.

title: Digital Quantum Simulation Of The Holstein-Primakoff Transformation On Noisy Qubits
authors: Kelvin Yip, Alessandro Monteros, Sahel Ashhab, And Lin Tian
abstract:
Author(s): Kelvin Yip, Alessandro Monteros, Sahel Ashhab, and Lin Tian

Quantum simulation of many-body systems offers a powerful approach to exploring collective quantum dynamics beyond classical computational reach. Although spin and fermionic models have been extensively simulated on digital quantum computers, the simulation of bosonic systems on programmable quantum…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052431] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes and analyzes digital quantum simulation of the Holstein-Primakoff transformation for bosonic many-body dynamics on noisy qubits.
motivation: Bosonic many-body systems are challenging to simulate classically and less explored than spin or fermionic models on digital quantum computers.
method: The authors design a digital quantum simulation approach that maps bosonic degrees of freedom to qubits via the Holstein-Primakoff transformation and assess its performance under noise.
result: The abstract indicates a demonstration/analysis of bosonic dynamics on programmable quantum hardware, though specific quantitative outcomes are not available in the excerpt.
conclusion: This work extends digital quantum simulation techniques to bosonic systems, but it does not directly address the researcher's core interests in quantum information theory, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Telescopy With Realistic Anticorrelated Optical Fields As References
authors: Xuan Tang And Z. Y. Ou
abstract:
Author(s): Xuan Tang and Z. Y. Ou

First proposed by Gottesman et al. [
tldr: The paper analyzes quantum telescopy using realistic anticorrelated optical fields as references to enhance Hanbury Brown–Twiss stellar interferometry.
motivation: Quantum telescopy was proposed to improve astronomical interferometry by using spatially entangled single-photon references, potentially rivaling Michelson interferometry.
method: The authors study realistic anticorrelated optical fields as reference states in the quantum-enhanced HBT intensity interferometric scheme.
result: They show that quantum telescopy with realistic anticorrelated fields can approach the performance of Michelson interferometry.
conclusion: The work supports the feasibility of quantum telescopy with practical optical reference fields, though it is an applied quantum-optics/astronomy proposal rather than a quantum-information-theory contribution.

title: Quantum Advantage For Sensing Properties Of Classical Fields
authors: Jordan Cotler, Daine L. Danielson, And Ishaan Kannan
abstract:
Author(s): Jordan Cotler, Daine L. Danielson, and Ishaan Kannan

Researchers demonstrate a quantum sensing protocol that uses entanglement and squeezing to learn diverse classical signal properties with subvacuum precision.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041025] Published Fri Oct 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum sensing protocol that uses entanglement and squeezing to estimate properties of classical fields with subvacuum precision.
motivation: Quantum metrology seeks advantages over classical sensing by exploiting quantum correlations and nonclassical probe states.
method: The authors use entangled and squeezed quantum probes to interrogate classical fields and extract multiple signal properties from measurement outcomes.
result: The protocol achieves subvacuum precision for learning diverse classical signal properties, demonstrating a quantum advantage in sensing.
conclusion: Entanglement and squeezing can enhance estimation of classical field properties beyond standard vacuum-level precision, with implications for quantum sensing applications.

title: Theory Of Quantum-Enhanced Interferometry With General Markovian Light Sources
authors: Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Daniel Malz, Ana Asenjo-Garcia, And Rahul Trivedi
abstract:
Author(s): Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Daniel Malz, Ana Asenjo-Garcia, and Rahul Trivedi

A new framework for designing and evaluating quantum light sources clarifies where realistic devices can provide a quantum advantage in interferometry.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033069] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a theoretical framework for designing and evaluating quantum light sources for quantum-enhanced interferometry under general Markovian source models.
motivation: It aims to clarify when realistic quantum light sources can deliver a genuine quantum advantage in interferometric sensing rather than only in idealized settings.
method: The authors develop a general Markovian light-source framework and use it to analyze interferometric performance and identify conditions for quantum enhancement.
result: The framework characterizes regimes where realistic quantum light sources provide an advantage and offers a practical way to evaluate candidate source designs.
conclusion: The work provides guidance for assessing and designing quantum light sources for interferometry, emphasizing realistic device constraints.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithm For Nonlinear Fluid Dynamics With Bounded Quantum Advantage
authors: David Jennings, Kamil Korzekwa, Matteo Lostaglio, Richard Ashworth, Emanuele Marsili, And Stephen Rolston
abstract:
Author(s): David Jennings, Kamil Korzekwa, Matteo Lostaglio, Richard Ashworth, Emanuele Marsili, and Stephen Rolston

A detailed resource analysis identifies the fundamental bottlenecks and achievable speedups for nonlinear fluid simulations on a fault-tolerant quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033060] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: A resource analysis of an end-to-end fault-tolerant quantum algorithm for nonlinear fluid dynamics, identifying bottlenecks and bounded achievable quantum advantage.
motivation: To assess whether fault-tolerant quantum computers can provide meaningful speedups for nonlinear fluid simulations and to identify the fundamental resource bottlenecks.
method: The authors perform a detailed resource analysis of an end-to-end quantum algorithm for nonlinear fluid dynamics on a fault-tolerant quantum computer.
result: The analysis identifies key bottlenecks and establishes bounds on the achievable quantum advantage for this simulation task.
conclusion: The work clarifies the practical prospects and limitations of quantum algorithms for nonlinear fluid dynamics, showing that quantum advantage is bounded by resource constraints.

title: Gamma-Ray Pulsar Discovery Using A Lattice-Based Method
authors: Daniel Pook-Kolb, Dotan Gazith, Colin J. Clark, Erik Agrell, Barak Zackay, And Bruce Allen
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Pook-Kolb, Dotan Gazith, Colin J. Clark, Erik Agrell, Barak Zackay, and Bruce Allen

Researchers using a cryptography-based method have identified a previously unknown pulsar from sparse data.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 211201] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: A lattice-based, cryptography-inspired computational method is used to discover a previously unknown gamma-ray pulsar from sparse observational data.
motivation: Pulsar searches in gamma-ray data are hampered by sparsity and background noise, motivating more powerful signal-recovery algorithms borrowed from computational number theory.
method: The authors apply a lattice-based search technique (akin to methods used in lattice cryptography) to detect periodic signals in sparse photon data, identifying a new pulsar candidate.
result: The method successfully recovers a previously unknown gamma-ray pulsar, demonstrating the feasibility of lattice-based search algorithms in astrophysical data analysis.
conclusion: Lattice-based algorithms provide a promising alternative tool for periodicity searches in sparse data, though the work is an astrophysics application rather than a quantum information result.

title: Resonant Delay In A Stationary Quantum Clock: Lifting The Threshold Mask
authors: Paul C. W. Davies And Damien A. Easson
abstract:
Author(s): Paul C. W. Davies and Damien A. Easson

Quantum transit times have a long history of inequivalent definitions, including phase times, dwell times, and quantum-clock constructions. In this context we revisit the Salecker-Wigner-Peres stationary quantum clock as a phase-sensitive scattering observable, with clock time defined by the energy …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052216] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper revisits the Salecker-Wigner-Peres stationary quantum clock as a phase-sensitive scattering observable and analyzes resonant delay in quantum transit-time definitions.
motivation: Quantum transit times have multiple inequivalent definitions, and the authors aim to clarify the stationary quantum-clock approach by connecting clock time to scattering phase and energy sensitivity.
method: They treat the Salecker-Wigner-Peres clock as a scattering observable and examine how resonant delay and threshold effects influence the extracted clock time.
result: The analysis lifts a threshold mask on resonant delay, providing a clearer phase-sensitive characterization of the stationary quantum clock.
conclusion: The work contributes to foundational quantum time and transit-time debates but does not directly address quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Spin Textures And Eigenstate Evolution Of Isospectrally Patterned Lattices
authors: Peter Schmelcher
abstract:
Author(s): Peter Schmelcher

Isospectrally patterned lattices exhibit a composite band structure with a tunable ratio of localized versus delocalized eigenstates that is controlled by the underlying phase gradient. We show that the lattice Hamiltonian can be interpreted as that of a single spin, which, when exposed to a rotatin…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 295407] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: Isospectrally patterned lattices with a phase-gradient-tunable mixture of localized and delocalized eigenstates are reinterpreted as the Hamiltonian of a single spin driven by a rotating field, giving a geometric picture of eigenstate evolution.
motivation: Isospectral patterning offers a knob to control the ratio of localized versus delocalized states without changing the spectrum, but a transparent physical interpretation of the mechanism and of eigenstate dynamics is lacking.
method: The lattice Hamiltonian is mapped onto an effective single-spin problem subject to a rotating field, and the resulting spin textures are used to analyze the band structure and the time/parameter evolution of eigenstates.
result: The spin picture reproduces the composite band structure and explains how the phase gradient tunes localization versus delocalization through the corresponding spin textures.
conclusion: The spin-texture mapping provides an intuitive geometric framework for isospectrally patterned lattices, useful for designing lattices with tailored eigenstate localization.

title: Nonlinear Dynamics Of Rapidly Driven Systems
authors: Afshin Besharat And Alexander A. Penin
abstract:
Author(s): Afshin Besharat and Alexander A. Penin

We consider systems characterized by the presence of a rapidly oscillating force. A general method is presented for the construction of the effective action governing the large-scale nonlinear dynamics of such systems order by order in inverse powers of the oscillation frequency [MATH]. The explicit ex…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054213] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a systematic high-frequency expansion for the effective action that governs the large-scale nonlinear dynamics of systems subject to a rapidly oscillating force.
motivation: Rapidly driven systems appear across mechanics and physics, but a general, order-by-order scheme for deriving the slow effective dynamics beyond standard averaging is lacking.
method: An asymptotic expansion in inverse powers of the driving frequency is constructed for the effective action, with explicit expressions derived order by order and illustrated on concrete nonlinear models.
result: The procedure yields systematic corrections to the averaged (slow) dynamics, capturing driving-induced modifications of the nonlinear equations of motion at each order in 1/omega.
conclusion: The formalism provides a general and controllable tool for analyzing rapidly driven nonlinear systems, applicable well beyond the specific examples treated.

title: Multimode Equilibrium Approximations In Light-matter Systems From Weak To Strong Coupling
authors: Davis M. Welakuh, Vasil Rokaj, Michael Ruggenthaler, And Angel Rubio
abstract:
Author(s): Davis M. Welakuh, Vasil Rokaj, Michael Ruggenthaler, and Angel Rubio

In this work, we detail different approaches to treat multimode photonic environments within nonrelativistic quantum electrodynamics in the long-wavelength approximation efficiently. Specifically, we show that for equilibrium properties of coupled light-matter systems, we can approximately capture t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043176] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops efficient equilibrium approximations for multimode light-matter systems in nonrelativistic quantum electrodynamics across weak-to-strong coupling regimes.
motivation: Full multimode photonic treatments of coupled light-matter systems are computationally demanding, so practical approximations are needed for equilibrium properties.
method: The authors analyze and detail different approaches within long-wavelength nonrelativistic QED to approximately capture equilibrium behavior of multimode coupled light-matter systems.
result: The proposed approximations are shown to efficiently capture equilibrium properties from weak to strong light-matter coupling.
conclusion: This provides a practical theoretical framework for modeling multimode photonic environments in equilibrium light-matter systems.

title: Protocols For A Many-Body Phase Microscope: From Coherences And $d$-Wave Superconductivity To Green’s Functions
authors: Christof Weitenberg, Luca Asteria, Ola Carlsson, Annabelle Bohrdt, And Fabian Grusdt
abstract:
Author(s): Christof Weitenberg, Luca Asteria, Ola Carlsson, Annabelle Bohrdt, and Fabian Grusdt

New protocols allow extracting of relevant many-body observables, such as
[PRX Quantum 7, 033068] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces protocols for quantum gas microscopes to extract many-body observables such as d-wave superconducting order parameters, coherences, and Green's functions.
motivation: Quantum gas microscopes offer powerful access to strongly correlated quantum many-body systems, but extracting key observables like superconducting order parameters and Green's functions remains challenging.
method: The authors develop measurement protocols tailored to state-of-the-art quantum gas microscopes, using local control and detection to reconstruct coherences and correlation functions.
result: The protocols enable direct extraction of d-wave superconducting order parameters, spatial coherences, and Green's functions in quantum gas microscope experiments.
conclusion: These techniques provide a practical toolbox for characterizing many-body phases, including unconventional superconductivity, in cold-atom quantum simulators.

title: Experimental Neuromorphic Computing Based On Quantum Memristor
authors: Mirela Selimović, Iris Agresti, Michał Siemaszko, Joshua Morris, Borivoje Dakić, Riccardo Albiero, Andrea Crespi, Francesco Ceccarelli, Roberto Osellame, Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mirela Selimović, Iris Agresti, Michał Siemaszko, Joshua Morris, Borivoje Dakić, Riccardo Albiero, Andrea Crespi, Francesco Ceccarelli, Roberto Osellame, Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto, and Philip Walther

A photonic neuromorphic architecture leverages a quantum memristor to enable nonlinear, memory-dependent processing for complex learning tasks such as vowel recognition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033067] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a photonic quantum memristor enabling nonlinear, memory-dependent processing for neuromorphic computing tasks such as vowel recognition.
motivation: Neuromorphic computing requires hardware with nonlinear memory-dependent dynamics, and quantum memristors could provide quantum advantages for such learning tasks.
method: A quantum memristor is implemented using photonic integrated circuits, characterized for memristive behavior, and integrated into a neuromorphic architecture for vowel recognition.
result: The quantum memristor exhibits nonlinear memory-dependent conductance, enabling successful vowel recognition in the experimental photonic platform.
conclusion: Quantum memristors are viable for quantum neuromorphic computing and show promise for complex learning tasks.

title: Probing Fractional Quantum Hall States In Weakly Interacting Fermi Gases
authors: Viktor Bekassy, Mikael Fogelström, And Johannes Hofmann
abstract:
Author(s): Viktor Bekassy, Mikael Fogelström, and Johannes Hofmann

Quantum gases are used to simulate the physics of the lowest Landau level with neutral atoms, which in the simplest setup is achieved by rotating the gas at the confining harmonic trap frequency, a requirement that is difficult to meet in practice. However, it is known that lowest Landau level state…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 213402] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a scheme to realize and probe fractional quantum Hall states in weakly interacting ultracold Fermi gases without requiring rotation at the trap frequency.
motivation: Rotating quantum gases can emulate lowest-Landau-level physics with neutral atoms, but the standard requirement of rotating at the harmonic trap frequency is experimentally impractical, motivating alternative routes to access Laughlin-type states.
method: They analyze how lowest-Landau-level states emerge in weakly interacting Fermi gases under accessible trapping/rotation conditions, using theoretical modeling of the many-body state and its signatures.
result: They identify a practical parameter regime where fractional quantum Hall-like states can form and specify observables that can probe them in cold-atom experiments.
conclusion: The work provides a feasible cold-atom platform for simulating fractional quantum Hall physics, extending quantum-gas simulation beyond the strict rotation-frequency requirement.

title: Rectification At High Currents In Asymmetric Two-Dimensional Electron Structures: Electron Tesla Valve
authors: Daniil I. Sarypov, Dmitriy A. Pokhabov, Arthur G. Pogosov, Evgeny Yu. Zhdanov, Andrey A. Shevyrin, And Askhat K. Bakarov
abstract:
Author(s): Daniil I. Sarypov, Dmitriy A. Pokhabov, Arthur G. Pogosov, Evgeny Yu. Zhdanov, Andrey A. Shevyrin, and Askhat K. Bakarov

In solids, frequent electron-electron collisions can induce collective, fluidlike electron transport. While this regime offers a powerful framework for exploring many-body phenomena, there is still a lack in functional electronic device actively exploiting hydrodynamic behavior of electrons. Here, w…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 216306] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The authors demonstrate a room-temperature-style solid-state 'electron Tesla valve' in an asymmetric two-dimensional electron gas structure that rectifies current by exploiting hydrodynamic electron flow at high currents.
motivation: Electron-electron collisions in solids can produce fluidlike collective transport, but few functional devices actively exploit this hydrodynamic regime; the authors aim to build a rectifying device analogous to Tesla's macroscopic valve.
method: Asymmetric two-dimensional electron structures in a semiconductor heterostructure are fabricated and measured at high current bias, where electron hydrodynamics dominates, and the resulting current-voltage rectification is characterized.
result: The asymmetric geometry yields pronounced current rectification at high currents, consistent with hydrodynamic (viscous) electron transport rather than diffusive or ballistic behavior.
conclusion: Hydrodynamic electron flow provides a viable mechanism for functional electronic device operation, opening a route to fluidic-inspired electronics such as electron valves and rectifiers.

title: Quantum Control Of Chemical Bonding And Antibonding: Entanglement Of A Single Alkaline-earth-metal Long-range Dimer
authors: G. A. Bougas, U. D. Jentschura, And S. I. Mistakidis
abstract:
Author(s): G. A. Bougas, U. D. Jentschura, and S. I. Mistakidis

Two identical neutral atoms, one of which is in an excited internal state, exhibit suppressed and enhanced collective spontaneous emission when prepared in subradiant and superradiant Dicke states, respectively. A single atom pair initialized in such a highly entangled state interacts via long-range…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052816] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how entangled Dicke states of a single alkaline-earth-metal atom pair can control long-range interactions and chemical bonding versus antibonding behavior.
motivation: The work aims to connect collective spontaneous emission and entanglement in a long-range dimer to quantum control of chemical bonding, a topic outside the listed quantum-information, thermodynamics, network, and hybrid-platform priorities.
method: The authors theoretically analyze two identical neutral atoms, one internally excited, prepared in subradiant or superradiant Dicke states and interacting via long-range potentials.
result: Subradiant and superradiant Dicke states suppress or enhance collective emission and modify the effective bonding/antibonding behavior of the dimer.
conclusion: Entanglement and collective emission in alkaline-earth-metal dimers provide a route for quantum control of chemical bonding, but the contribution is primarily atomic/molecular physics rather than one of the researcher's four core directions.

title: Non-Abelian Quantum Turbulence In Spinor Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Michikazu Kobayashi And Masahito Ueda
abstract:
Author(s): Michikazu Kobayashi and Masahito Ueda

We numerically investigate statistically steady quantum turbulence in the cyclic phase of a spin-2 spinor Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) driven by large-scale energy injection via a divergence-free external velocity field. In the full non-Abelian cyclic system, the mass-current spectrum exhibits an …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053319] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper numerically studies statistically steady quantum turbulence in the cyclic phase of a spin-2 spinor Bose-Einstein condensate driven by large-scale energy injection.
motivation: The work aims to understand how non-Abelian defect structures and spin degrees of freedom affect turbulence and energy transfer in spinor Bose-Einstein condensates.
method: The authors perform numerical simulations of a spin-2 spinor BEC in the cyclic phase under a divergence-free external velocity field that injects energy at large scales, focusing on the resulting mass-current spectrum.
result: The full non-Abelian cyclic system exhibits a characteristic mass-current spectrum, revealing how non-Abelian order-parameter structure influences the turbulent cascade.
conclusion: Non-Abelian quantum turbulence in spinor BECs provides a distinct setting for studying energy transfer and defect-mediated dynamics beyond ordinary scalar quantum turbulence.

title: Linear And Nonlinear Optical Torque In Multilevel Atomic Systems Driven By Counter-rotating Orbital Angular Momentum Fields
authors: Dharma P. Permana, Mažena Mackoit Sinkevičienė, Viačeslav Kudriašov, Julius Ruseckas, Gediminas Juzeliūnas, And Hamid R. Hamedi
abstract:
Author(s): Dharma P. Permana, Mažena Mackoit Sinkevičienė, Viačeslav Kudriašov, Julius Ruseckas, Gediminas Juzeliūnas, and Hamid R. Hamedi

We investigate the generation of optical torque in coherently prepared multilevel atomic media driven by a vector vortex beam composed of two counter-rotating components carrying opposite orbital angular momenta, [MATH] and [MATH]. We consider a three-level [MATH] configuration and a four-level …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053720] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies linear and nonlinear optical torque generated in coherent multilevel atomic media driven by counter-rotating orbital-angular-momentum components of a vector vortex beam.
motivation: Optical torque from structured light carrying orbital angular momentum is of interest for controlling atomic media, but its behavior in multilevel coherent atomic systems driven by counter-rotating OAM fields is not fully understood.
method: The authors analyze three-level and four-level atomic configurations interacting with a vector vortex beam composed of two counter-rotating components carrying opposite OAM, deriving linear and nonlinear contributions to the optical torque.
result: They show how atomic coherence and multilevel structure influence the generation of optical torque, with distinct linear and nonlinear torque contributions arising from the counter-rotating OAM fields.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical description of optical torque in multilevel atomic media and highlights coherent control possibilities using counter-rotating OAM fields, but it is not directly aligned with the listed quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-systems priorities.

title: Adaptive Noise-mitigated Distributed Variational Quantum Sensing With Federated Learning
authors: Ratun Rahman, Atit Pokharel, Ashlyn D. Burch, And Dinh C. Nguyen
abstract:
Author(s): Ratun Rahman, Atit Pokharel, Ashlyn D. Burch, and Dinh C. Nguyen

Quantum sensor networks (QSNs) enable collaborative parameter estimation across distributed quantum sensors, improving sensing precision, spatial coverage, and robustness over standalone systems. However, practical QSNs are intrinsically heterogeneous and time-varying, as sensor nodes may experience…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052610] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an adaptive noise-mitigated distributed variational quantum sensing framework that uses federated learning to handle heterogeneous and time-varying quantum sensor networks.
motivation: Distributed quantum sensor networks can improve sensing precision and coverage, but practical deployments suffer from hardware heterogeneity, noise, and time-varying conditions that degrade estimation performance.
method: The authors combine variational quantum sensing with adaptive noise mitigation and federated learning so distributed sensor nodes can collaboratively train models without centralizing raw data.
result: The framework is presented as improving robustness and sensing performance under realistic noise and heterogeneity in quantum sensor networks, though the abstract does not provide detailed quantitative benchmarks.
conclusion: The work targets applied distributed quantum sensing using federated learning and noise mitigation, rather than core quantum information theory, thermodynamics, quantum networking, or hybrid quantum hardware.

title: Predissociation Dynamics Of Charged Long-range Rydberg Molecules
authors: Neethu Abraham, P. Giannakeas, And Matthew T. Eiles
abstract:
Author(s): Neethu Abraham, P. Giannakeas, and Matthew T. Eiles

We investigate predissociation in homonuclear ([MATH]) and heteronuclear ([MATH]) long-range Rydberg atom-ion molecules. Owing to their micron-scale bond lengths, these dissociate on timescales far removed from those of more tigh…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052814] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies predissociation dynamics of homonuclear and heteronuclear long-range Rydberg atom-ion molecules.
motivation: Long-range Rydberg molecules have micron-scale bond lengths and can dissociate on unusually long timescales, motivating a detailed understanding of their stability and decay mechanisms.
method: The authors develop a theoretical treatment of charged long-range Rydberg molecules and analyze their predissociation dynamics for homonuclear and heteronuclear cases.
result: They characterize predissociation pathways and timescales for these Rydberg atom-ion molecules, distinguishing behaviors between homonuclear and heteronuclear species.
conclusion: The results provide insight into the lifetime and dynamical stability of long-range Rydberg molecules, relevant to ultracold molecular physics and Rydberg-mediated interactions.

title: Optical Spectroscopy Of Bose-Einstein Condensates At Finite Temperature
authors: R. M. F. Andersen, L. N. Stokholm, I. Zebergs, N. R. Neubert, A. S. Chatterley, N. Kjærgaard, And J. J. Arlt
abstract:
Author(s): R. M. F. Andersen, L. N. Stokholm, I. Zebergs, N. R. Neubert, A. S. Chatterley, N. Kjærgaard, and J. J. Arlt

We report on optical spectroscopic measurements of ultracold and partially condensed [MATH] gases, which show distinct spectral features due to the thermal and Bose-condensed components in the frequency domain. These features are detected in situ by using a dark-field configuration with …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053317] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: In-situ dark-field optical spectroscopy resolves distinct spectral signatures of the thermal and Bose-condensed components in partially condensed ultracold gases.
motivation: Finite-temperature ultracold gases contain coexisting thermal and condensed fractions, and a frequency-domain probe that distinguishes them in situ would give a direct, non-destructive window on condensate fraction and thermodynamics.
method: Dark-field optical spectroscopic measurements are performed on ultracold, partially condensed gases, and the recorded spectra are interpreted in terms of the distinct contributions from thermal and Bose-condensed atoms.
result: The spectra exhibit separate, identifiable features attributable to the thermal and condensed components, allowing the two fractions to be distinguished in the frequency domain without destructive imaging.
conclusion: Optical spectroscopy provides a viable in-situ diagnostic of condensate fraction and finite-temperature behaviour in ultracold gases, complementing conventional time-of-flight and density measurements.

title: Quantum Theory Of Molecular Orientation
authors: Victor V. Albert, Eric Kubischta, Mikhail Lemeshko, And Lee R. Liu
abstract:

We formulate a quantum phase space for rotational and nuclear-spin states of rigid molecules. For each nuclear spin isomer, we rederive the isomer's admissible angular momentum states from molecular geometry and nuclear-spin data, introduce its angular position states using quantization theory, and …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053318] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper formulates a quantum phase-space framework for rotational and nuclear-spin states of rigid molecules, including nuclear spin isomers.
motivation: It aims to describe molecular orientation and derive admissible angular momentum states from molecular geometry and nuclear-spin data.
method: The authors use quantization theory to construct angular position states and rederive angular momentum state spaces for each nuclear spin isomer.
result: They obtain a phase-space description of molecular rotational and nuclear-spin states organized by spin isomer.
conclusion: This is a specialized molecular quantum mechanics framework that does not directly address the researcher's core interests in quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Second-harmonic Stabilization Of A Bulk Photonic Resonator
authors: Lindell M. Williams, Grant M. Brodnik, And Scott B. Papp
abstract:
Author(s): Lindell M. Williams, Grant M. Brodnik, and Scott B. Papp

Photonic resonators provide compact frequency references for laser stabilization and precision metrology. Their frequency stability, however, is fundamentally limited by the environmental sensitivity of the resonator material. We explore second-harmonic (SH) stabilization in photonic resonators, whi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053513] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates second-harmonic stabilization as a means of improving the frequency stability of bulk photonic resonators used as compact laser frequency references.
motivation: Photonic resonators offer compact alternatives to traditional frequency references for laser stabilization and precision metrology, but their stability is limited by the environmental sensitivity of the resonator material.
method: The authors explore second-harmonic stabilization in bulk photonic resonators, presumably comparing the drift of the second-harmonic signal against the fundamental to cancel common-mode environmental perturbations.
result: The study characterizes how SH-based locking schemes affect resonator frequency stability relative to conventional stabilization approaches, quantifying the achievable reduction in environmental sensitivity.
conclusion: Second-harmonic stabilization may provide a practical route to more robust compact photonic frequency references, though the work remains within classical precision metrology rather than quantum information science.

title: Anomalous Scaling And Channel-selective Sensitivity Of Nonlinear Higher-order Exceptional Points Engineered By Artificial Gauge Fields
authors: Run-Cheng Li, Ke-Wen Xiao, And Wen-Yuan Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Run-Cheng Li, Ke-Wen Xiao, and Wen-Yuan Wang

Nonlinear non-Hermitian systems offer a promising route to overcome the stringent dimensional constraints of linear higher-order exceptional points (EPs), yet their robustness against external perturbations and their fundamental noise limits remain critical open questions. Here we investigate a mini…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053514] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies higher-order exceptional points in nonlinear non-Hermitian systems engineered via artificial gauge fields, analyzing their anomalous scaling and channel-selective sensitivity to perturbations.
motivation: Linear higher-order exceptional points are dimensionally constrained, and nonlinear non-Hermitian systems are proposed as a route around this, but their robustness against external perturbations and fundamental noise limits remain open questions.
method: A minimal nonlinear non-Hermitian model with artificial gauge fields is analyzed to characterize the scaling of eigenfrequency splitting and the perturbation response near higher-order exceptional points.
result: Anomalous scaling laws and channel-selective sensitivity to perturbations are identified, revealing how nonlinearity modifies the response of higher-order exceptional points relative to the linear case.
conclusion: Nonlinear higher-order exceptional points offer enhanced but channel-dependent sensing capability, with implications for the noise limits of EP-based sensing schemes.

title: Strain-induced Spin Reorientation Transition And Associated Anomalies Of Magnetization Dynamics In Epitaxial ${\mathrm{Y}}_{3}{\mathrm{Fe}}_{5}{\mathrm{O}}_{12}$ Films
authors: Nikolay A. Pertsev
abstract:
Author(s): Nikolay A. Pertsev

Ferrimagnetic insulator yttrium iron garnet (YIG) is distinguished by very low magnetic damping, which makes it favorable for experimental investigations of spin dynamics and suitable for various device applications. This paper presents a theoretical study of the effects of substrate-induced strains…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254414] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of how substrate-induced strain in epitaxial YIG films drives a spin reorientation transition and modifies magnetization dynamics and damping.
motivation: Yttrium iron garnet has very low magnetic damping, making it attractive for spin-dynamics studies and magnonic devices, but strain from lattice mismatch with substrates can strongly alter its magnetic anisotropy and dynamics.
method: Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert-type theoretical analysis of the magnetic free energy of epitaxial YIG films including substrate-induced strain, used to compute equilibrium spin orientations and the associated ferromagnetic resonance / magnetization dynamics.
result: Strain is shown to induce a spin reorientation transition as a function of film thickness and strain, accompanied by anomalies in the magnetization dynamics such as changes in resonance frequency and damping behavior near the transition.
conclusion: Strain engineering provides a route to control magnetic anisotropy and dynamic response in YIG films, which is relevant for magnonic device design but has no direct bearing on quantum information, information thermodynamics, or quantum network/hybrid-qubit hardware.

title: Probing Spinon Interactions In The Spin-1 Bilinear-biquadratic Chain
authors: Yonatan Lin, Oleg A. Starykh, And Anna Keselman
abstract:
Author(s): Yonatan Lin, Oleg A. Starykh, and Anna Keselman

We study the dynamical spin and nematic correlations in the bilinear-biquadratic spin-1 chain in the critical phase hosting deconfined spinons. We demonstrate how spinon interactions can be directly probed in the presence of a magnetic field or a single-ion anisotropy. Using a hydrodynamic treatment…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274432] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies dynamical spin and nematic correlations in the critical phase of a spin-1 bilinear-biquadratic chain to show how deconfined spinon interactions can be probed via magnetic field or single-ion anisotropy.
motivation: The authors aim to identify observable signatures of spinon interactions in a deconfined critical spin-chain phase, where such interactions are usually difficult to access directly.
method: They use a hydrodynamic treatment of the low-energy spinon excitations and compute dynamical spin and nematic correlation functions in the presence of a magnetic field or single-ion anisotropy.
result: The analysis demonstrates that spinon interactions leave characteristic signatures in the dynamical correlations, providing a route to probe them experimentally through field or anisotropy tuning.
conclusion: The work establishes dynamical spin and nematic correlations as practical probes of spinon interactions in the spin-1 bilinear-biquadratic chain.

title: Universal Transport Properties Of Continuous Quantum Gases
authors: Zi-Yang Liu, Xiangguo Yin, Yunbo Zhang, Shizhong Zhang, And Xi-Wen Guan
abstract:
Author(s): Zi-Yang Liu, Xiangguo Yin, Yunbo Zhang, Shizhong Zhang, and Xi-Wen Guan

The Drude weight characterizes ballistic transport in quantum many-body systems. Although analytical calculations of Drude weights have been extensively studied in integrable models, their direct connections to finite-temperature macroscopic state functions remain unestablished, especially for conti…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 285117] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies universal Drude weights and ballistic transport in continuous quantum gases, connecting them to finite-temperature macroscopic state functions.
motivation: Analytical Drude-weight calculations are well developed for integrable models, but their direct link to finite-temperature macroscopic thermodynamics remains unclear, especially for continuous quantum gases.
method: The authors derive universal transport properties for continuous quantum gases, likely using integrability-based or thermodynamic Bethe ansatz techniques to relate Drude weights to state functions.
result: They establish connections between Drude weights and macroscopic thermodynamic quantities, providing universal transport formulas for continuous quantum gases at finite temperature.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of ballistic transport in quantum many-body systems, but it is primarily a condensed-matter/quantum-gas transport study rather than a quantum-information or information-thermodynamics contribution.

title: Raman Optical Activity And Helicity-dependent Phonon Splitting In Chiral CoSi
authors: Yuki Suganuma, Gakuto Kusuno, Kohei Miyazaki, Hikaru Watanabe, Rikuto Oiwa, Ryotaro Arita, Satoshi Iwasaki, Yoshiki Yasuoka, Yusuke Kousaka, Yoshihiko Togawa, And Takuya Satoh
abstract:
Author(s): Yuki Suganuma, Gakuto Kusuno, Kohei Miyazaki, Hikaru Watanabe, Rikuto Oiwa, Ryotaro Arita, Satoshi Iwasaki, Yoshiki Yasuoka, Yusuke Kousaka, Yoshihiko Togawa, and Takuya Satoh

Circularly polarized Raman scattering in solids provides access to two distinct phenomena: Raman optical activity (ROA), an intensity difference between circular polarization channels, and helicity-dependent frequency splitting of chiral phonons. We observe both in the chiral topological semimetal C…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254305] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: Circularly polarized Raman scattering is used to observe both Raman optical activity and helicity-dependent chiral phonon splitting in the chiral topological semimetal CoSi.
motivation: Chiral crystals can exhibit two distinct circular-polarization phenomena—an intensity asymmetry between polarization channels (ROA) and a helicity-dependent frequency splitting of chiral phonons—but both are rarely observed together in a single material.
method: Polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy with circularly polarized light on single crystals of the chiral topological semimetal CoSi, supported by first-principles calculations of phonon spectra and Raman tensor analysis.
result: Both Raman optical activity and a helicity-dependent splitting of chiral phonon modes are observed in CoSi, with the splitting attributed to the underlying structural chirality of the crystal.
conclusion: CoSi provides a platform in which optical activity and chiral phonon splitting coexist, offering a spectroscopic handle on chirality-driven lattice dynamics in topological chiral semimetals.

title: Possible Existence Of Classical Spin-liquid-like Behavior In The Antiferromagnetic ${J}_{1}\text{–}{J}_{2}\text{–}{J}_{3}$ Spin-1/2 Ising Model On The Kagome Lattice: Effective Field Theory Analysis
authors: E. Jurčišinová, M. Jurčišin, And R. Remecký
abstract:
Author(s): E. Jurčišinová, M. Jurčišin, and R. Remecký

The three-site cluster effective-field theory approximation is used for the investigation of the phase diagram and magnetic properties of the geometrically frustrated classical antiferromagnetic [MATH] spin-[MATH] Ising model on the kagome lattice with three different…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054125] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: A three-site cluster effective-field-theory study of the phase diagram and magnetic properties of the geometrically frustrated classical J1–J2–J3 spin-1/2 Ising antiferromagnet on the kagome lattice, suggesting classical spin-liquid-like behavior.
motivation: Geometrically frustrated magnets on the kagome lattice are of longstanding interest because frustration can suppress conventional order and host exotic spin-liquid-like states; the authors aim to characterize how the J1, J2 and J3 couplings shape the phase diagram.
method: The classical spin-1/2 Ising model with nearest-, next-nearest- and third-neighbor antiferromagnetic couplings is treated within a three-site cluster effective-field theory approximation to compute the phase diagram and magnetic properties.
result: The effective-field-theory analysis yields the phase diagram as a function of the three coupling ratios and identifies regimes exhibiting classical spin-liquid-like behavior arising from frustration.
conclusion: The work suggests that purely classical frustration on the kagome lattice can mimic some spin-liquid phenomenology, providing a classical baseline against which quantum spin-liquid candidates may be compared.

title: Random Theory For A Guiding Center Gas: Semiclassical Stochastic Dynamics In Phase Space And non-Hermitian Many-body Problem
authors: Hiroshi Kuratsuji, Satoshi Tsuchida, And Takahiro Uetoko
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroshi Kuratsuji, Satoshi Tsuchida, and Takahiro Uetoko

We study a random theory of semiclassical guiding center motion for a many-electron system in a strong magnetic field. We consider the many-body aspect of an assembly of guiding center coordinates, which we call a “guiding center gas”, that characterize the lowest Landau level. This system is descri…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054123] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a random semiclassical theory for a many-electron guiding-center gas in a strong magnetic field, connecting stochastic phase-space dynamics to a non-Hermitian many-body problem.
motivation: It aims to capture many-body aspects of an assembly of guiding-center coordinates characterizing the lowest Landau level.
method: The authors formulate a random theory of semiclassical guiding-center motion and analyze the resulting stochastic dynamics in phase space within a non-Hermitian many-body framework.
result: The work derives a stochastic semiclassical description for the guiding-center gas and relates it to non-Hermitian many-body dynamics.
conclusion: The framework may offer a route to understanding lowest-Landau-level many-body physics through random and non-Hermitian semiclassical dynamics, but it is not directly aligned with the specified quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-systems interests.

title: Integrability-breaking Phase Transitions In Stadiumlike Billiards
authors: Anne Kétri P. Da Fonseca And Edson D. Leonel
abstract:
Author(s): Anne Kétri P. da Fonseca and Edson D. Leonel

We investigate integrability-breaking transitions in two classes of stadiumlike billiards with parabolic boundaries. While focusing boundaries generate a mixed phase space in which regular islands coexist with a chaotic sea, dispersing boundaries produce a fully chaotic phase space for any finite bo…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054210] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies integrability-breaking transitions in two classes of stadiumlike billiards with parabolic boundaries, contrasting mixed phase space (focusing boundaries) with fully chaotic phase space (dispersing boundaries).
motivation: Stadium billiards are paradigmatic models for the transition from integrable to chaotic dynamics, and understanding how boundary geometry controls the emergence of mixed versus fully chaotic phase space is a long-standing question in nonlinear dynamics.
method: Classical dynamical-systems analysis of billiard trajectories with parabolic focusing and dispersing boundaries, using phase-space portraits, Poincaré sections, and characterization of regular islands, chaotic seas, and the transition to full chaos as a function of the boundary deformation parameter.
result: Focusing (parabolic) boundaries yield a mixed phase space with coexisting regular islands and a chaotic sea, whereas dispersing boundaries produce fully chaotic dynamics for any finite deformation.
conclusion: Boundary curvature class determines whether the integrability-breaking transition is gradual (mixed) or immediate (hard chaos), clarifying the geometric origin of chaos in stadiumlike billiards.

title: Vorticity Induced By Nonfrontal Collisions Of Quantum Droplets
authors: J. E. Alba-Arroyo, Santiago F. Caballero-Benitez, And R. Jáuregui
abstract:
Author(s): J. E. Alba-Arroyo, Santiago F. Caballero-Benitez, and R. Jáuregui

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042023] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: A phase diagram for vortex nucleation (vortex rings, twin vortices, twisted single vortices) in off-axis collisions of incompressible binary quantum droplets is computed and shown to be experimentally accessible.
motivation: Quantum droplets are self-bound ultracold-atom liquids whose nonfrontal collisions offer a controlled setting for studying superfluidity, vortex generation, and nonlinear soliton-like dynamics.
method: Numerical simulations of the extended Gross-Pitaevskii equations for a binary droplet mixture in the incompressible regime, scanning impact parameter and kinetic energy to map the collision outcomes.
result: The study produces a phase diagram separating elastic/merged outcomes from vortex-ring, twin-vortex, and twisted single-vortex nucleation regimes, with parameters within reach of current experiments.
conclusion: Off-axis quantum droplet collisions provide a practical platform for deterministic vortex generation and for testing hydrodynamic analogies in quantum fluids.

title: Nonequilibrium Probes Of Quantum Geometry In Gapless Systems
authors: Bastien Lapierre, Per Moosavi, And Blagoje Oblak
