Much of our understanding of gapless quantum matter stems from low-energy descriptions using conformal field theory. This is especially true in [MATH] dimensions, where such theories have an infinite-dimensional parameter space induced by their conformal symmetry. We reveal the underlying quantum geo…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043177] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates nonequilibrium probes of quantum geometry in gapless quantum systems, using conformal field theory descriptions.
motivation: Much of the understanding of gapless quantum matter relies on low-energy conformal field theory, especially in certain dimensions where conformal symmetry gives an infinite-dimensional parameter space.
method: The authors use conformal field theory and nonequilibrium probes to reveal underlying quantum geometry in gapless systems.
result: They reveal underlying quantum geometric structure in gapless systems via nonequilibrium probes.
conclusion: The work provides new insight into quantum geometry in gapless quantum matter, but it falls outside the specified quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems directions.

title: Quantum Eigenvalue Transformations For Arbitrary Matrices
authors: Xabier Gutiérrez, Lorenzo Laneve, And Mikel Sanz
abstract:
Author(s): Xabier Gutiérrez, Lorenzo Laneve, and Mikel Sanz

A block encoding is called
[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042017] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends block encodings and generalized quantum signal processing to implement polynomial eigenvalue transformations of arbitrary square matrices, including non-diagonalizable ones via Jordan blocks.
motivation: Quantum signal processing and block encodings are powerful tools for quantum algorithms, but existing eigenvalue-transformation frameworks typically target Hermitian or normal matrices; extending them to arbitrary matrices is important for broader matrix-function applications.
method: The authors introduce a strengthened block-encoding notion and show that any block encoding can be upgraded using O(log) ancillary qubits, enabling generalized quantum signal processing to realize degree-n polynomials of arbitrary square matrices.
result: The construction implements polynomial transformations acting on the Jordan blocks of non-diagonalizable matrices, thereby generalizing quantum eigenvalue transformations beyond the usual Hermitian/normal setting.
conclusion: This work broadens the scope of quantum signal processing and block-encoding-based algorithms to arbitrary matrices, with potential applications to quantum linear algebra and matrix-function simulation.

title: Extracting The Pairing Gap From Van Hove Singularities In Rf Spectra Of The Fermi-Hubbard Model
authors: Chuping Li, Kaichao Zhang, Junru Wu, Yuxuan Wu, Dingli Yuan, Pengyi Chen, Lin Sun, And Qijin Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Chuping Li, Kaichao Zhang, Junru Wu, Yuxuan Wu, Dingli Yuan, Pengyi Chen, Lin Sun, and Qijin Chen

We show that van Hove singularities in radio-frequency spectra of the three-dimensional (3D) attractive Fermi-Hubbard model provide a robust route to extracting the pairing gap. Four types of singularities are classified, and their spectral positions are shown to depend solely on the pairing gap $\m…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043153] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that van Hove singularities in radio-frequency spectra of the 3D attractive Fermi-Hubbard model can be used to extract the pairing gap.
motivation: Identifying robust spectroscopic signatures of pairing in strongly correlated Fermi systems is important for interpreting ultracold-atom and condensed-matter experiments.
method: The authors classify four types of van Hove singularities in RF spectra of the 3D attractive Fermi-Hubbard model and analyze how their spectral positions depend on the pairing gap.
result: The singularity positions are found to depend solely on the pairing gap, providing a clean route to extracting it from RF spectroscopy.
conclusion: Van Hove singularities in RF spectra offer a robust diagnostic of pairing in the Fermi-Hubbard model, with potential relevance to cold-atom experiments.

title: Realization Of Repulsive Polarons In The Strongly Correlated Regime
authors: R. Henke, J. Levinsen, M. M. Parish, J. Boronat, G. E. Astrakharchik, H. Moritz, And C. R. Cabrera
abstract:
Author(s): R. Henke, J. Levinsen, M. M. Parish, J. Boronat, G. E. Astrakharchik, H. Moritz, and C. R. Cabrera

A stable repulsive Bose polaron is realized in a two-dimensional quantum gas by encoding impurities and their surrounding quantum medium in different vibrational states, allowing for the investigation of quasiparticle properties in the strongly interacting regime.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041040] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally realizes a stable repulsive Bose polaron in a two-dimensional quantum gas by encoding impurities and the medium in different vibrational states, enabling study of quasiparticle properties in the strongly correlated regime.
motivation: Repulsive polarons are challenging to stabilize because they are often short-lived, limiting access to strongly correlated quasiparticle physics in ultracold quantum gases.
method: The authors use a two-dimensional Bose gas with impurities prepared in distinct vibrational states, which suppresses loss and allows controlled investigation of repulsive polaron formation and properties.
result: A stable repulsive Bose polaron is observed in the strongly interacting regime, enabling measurement of quasiparticle characteristics that were previously difficult to access.
conclusion: This work provides a clean platform for studying strongly correlated impurity physics in quantum gases, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems for quantum information processing.

title: Emergent Gauge Flux In Mixed ${\mathrm{QED}}_{3}$ With Flavor Chemical Potential: Implications For Magnetized U(1) Dirac Spin Liquids
authors: Chuang Chen, Urban F. P. Seifert, Kexin Feng, Oleg A. Starykh, Leon Balents, And Zi Yang Meng
abstract:
Author(s): Chuang Chen, Urban F. P. Seifert, Kexin Feng, Oleg A. Starykh, Leon Balents, and Zi Yang Meng

Quantum Monte Carlo simulations reveal that a Zeeman field drives Dirac spin liquids into a chiral flux phase, forming relativistic spinon Landau levels and gapless photon excitations of the emergent gauge field theory.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041029] Published Fri Oct 30, 2026.
tldr: Quantum Monte Carlo simulations show that a Zeeman field can drive mixed QED3 Dirac spin liquids into a chiral flux phase with relativistic spinon Landau levels and gapless emergent photons.
motivation: The paper studies magnetized U(1) Dirac spin liquids and the fate of emergent gauge fields under flavor chemical potential, aiming to understand field-induced phases in frustrated quantum magnets.
method: The authors use quantum Monte Carlo simulations of a lattice model for mixed QED3 with flavor chemical potential and analyze the resulting emergent gauge flux and excitation spectra.
result: They find a field-driven chiral flux phase characterized by relativistic spinon Landau levels and gapless photon excitations of the emergent gauge theory.
conclusion: The work clarifies how magnetic fields can stabilize chiral flux ordering in U(1) Dirac spin liquids, with implications for magnetized spin-liquid candidate materials.

title: Topological Phase Transitions And Their Thermodynamic Fate In Arbitrary-$S$ Classical Pyrochlore Spin Ice
authors: Sena Watanabe, Yukitoshi Motome, And Haruki Watanabe
abstract:
Author(s): Sena Watanabe, Yukitoshi Motome, and Haruki Watanabe

A theoretical framework for arbitrary-spin pyrochlore spin ice reveals that
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041016] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: A general theoretical framework for arbitrary-spin classical pyrochlore spin ice shows that S=3/2 magnets alone exhibit an abrupt transition between two distinct spin-liquid states that survives thermal fluctuations, while all other transitions melt into crossovers.
motivation: Spin ice hosts topological defects (monopoles) and spin-liquid behaviour, but how the nature of these phases and their transitions depends on the local spin magnitude S was unclear; existing work focused mostly on the classical S→∞ and effective doublet limits.
method: The authors formulate a general theoretical treatment of pyrochlore spin ice for arbitrary spin length S, using classical spin models with exchange and dipolar couplings, and analyze the phase behaviour and its evolution under thermal fluctuations.
result: They find that for S=3/2 a sharp transition between two distinct spin-liquid regimes occurs and remains robust against thermal fluctuations, whereas for all other values of S the putative transitions are washed out into smooth crossovers.
conclusion: The paper establishes which spin-liquid phases and phase transitions can genuinely persist at finite temperature in classical pyrochlore spin ice, singling out the S=3/2 case as special.

title: Spin-Valley Relaxation Of Rydberg Excitons
authors: V. Jindal, K. Mourzidis, M. Semina, D. Lagarde, A. Balocchi, P. Renucci, T. Boulier, T. Taniguchi, K. Watanabe, M. Glazov, And X. Marie
abstract:
Author(s): V. Jindal, K. Mourzidis, M. Semina, D. Lagarde, A. Balocchi, P. Renucci, T. Boulier, T. Taniguchi, K. Watanabe, M. Glazov, and X. Marie

Rydberg excitons, characterized by large spatial extension and reduced electron-hole overlap, must have a spin-valley dynamics different from that of ground state excitons. Here, we report a direct measurement of spin relaxation of Rydberg excitons in high-quality [MATH] monolayer usin…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 216403] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper directly measures spin-valley relaxation dynamics of Rydberg excitons in high-quality monolayer MoS2 using time-resolved spectroscopy.
motivation: Rydberg excitons have large spatial extent and small electron-hole overlap, so their spin-valley dynamics should differ markedly from ground-state excitons, but this had not been measured directly.
method: Time-resolved (polarization-resolved) optical spectroscopy on high-quality monolayer MoS2 samples, with an accompanying theoretical analysis of spin-valley relaxation channels for Rydberg exciton states.
result: Spin relaxation times of Rydberg excitons are measured and shown to differ from those of ground-state excitons, revealing the role of state-dependent exchange interaction and valley depolarization mechanisms.
conclusion: Rydberg excitons exhibit a distinct spin-valley relaxation behavior, establishing them as a tunable platform for valleytronic studies in monolayer semiconductors.

title: Odd-Parity Magnons In The Haldane-Hubbard Model From Topological Exciton Condensation
authors: Rintaro Eto And Johannes Knolle
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto and Johannes Knolle

Collective excitations in condensed matter can carry nontrivial topology and provide information about quantum phases beyond their ground-state properties. At the same time, the recent emergence of altermagnetism and related nonrelativistic spin-split electronic states raises the question of how unc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 216703] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically studies odd-parity magnon collective excitations emerging from topological exciton condensation in the Haldane-Hubbard model, with connections to altermagnetism and nonrelativistic spin-split electronic states.
motivation: Collective excitations can carry nontrivial topology and reveal physics beyond ground-state properties, and recent interest in altermagnetism raises questions about spin-split electronic states and their collective modes.
method: The authors analyze the Haldane-Hubbard model and topological exciton condensation to derive the magnon spectrum and identify odd-parity topological magnon modes.
result: They find that topological exciton condensation leads to odd-parity magnons in the Haldane-Hubbard model, linking excitonic topology to spin-wave excitations.
conclusion: The work establishes a route to topological magnon excitations from exciton condensation and highlights connections to altermagnetism and spin-split electronic states.

title: Signature Of Field-induced Spin Relaxation In The Paramagnetic Regime Of The Frustrated Triangular Antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{NdZnAl}}_{11}{\mathrm{O}}_{19}$
authors: Manshi Rani, Dheeraj Ranaut, Manh Duc Le, Mohamed Aouane, G. B. G. Stenning, And K. Mukherjee
abstract:
Author(s): Manshi Rani, Dheeraj Ranaut, Manh Duc Le, Mohamed Aouane, G. B. G. Stenning, and K. Mukherjee

This study explores the influence of positional disorder on magnetic behavior, focusing on the presence of orphan spins that are effectively decoupled from the collective spin dynamics. Here, the authors investigate the positional disorder and its impact on crystal electric field (CEF) excitations using inelastic neutron scattering measurements. Interestingly, a field-induced spin relaxation associated with the orphan spins, with an energy barrier corresponding to the CEF gap is revealed through ac susceptibility measurements.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254413] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: Inelastic neutron scattering and ac susceptibility are used to show that positional disorder in the frustrated triangular antiferromagnet NdZnAl11O19 produces orphan spins whose field-induced relaxation is governed by a crystal-electric-field energy gap.
motivation: Positional disorder in frustrated magnets can generate decoupled 'orphan' spins that alter collective magnetic behavior, but how such disorder affects crystal-field excitations and spin dynamics is poorly understood.
method: Inelastic neutron scattering is used to probe crystal-electric-field excitations and positional disorder in NdZnAl11O19, complemented by ac susceptibility measurements to track field-induced spin relaxation.
result: A field-induced spin relaxation process associated with the orphan spins is observed, with an activation energy barrier matching the crystal-electric-field gap.
conclusion: The work links positional disorder, orphan spins, and crystal-field physics in a frustrated triangular antiferromagnet, offering a magneto-structural picture of the paramagnetic regime.

title: Two-dimensional Twisted Ferromagnetic Domain Wall As A Spin-wave Diffraction Grating
authors: Ehsan Faridi, Se Kwon Kim, And Giovanni Vignale
abstract:
Author(s): Ehsan Faridi, Se Kwon Kim, and Giovanni Vignale

We present a theoretical study of spin-wave scattering by a twisted domain wall (DW) in a two-dimensional ferromagnet with easy-axis anisotropy. While the twisted DW generates an effective gauge field for spin waves, leading to a deflection of their trajectories, our main focus is on a distinct effe…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274425] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study showing that a twisted ferromagnetic domain wall in a two-dimensional easy-axis ferromagnet acts as a diffraction grating for spin waves, producing distinct scattering patterns beyond the gauge-field deflection.
motivation: Twisted domain walls generate effective gauge fields that deflect spin-wave trajectories, but the authors aim to identify and characterize a separate, structurally induced scattering effect useful for controlling spin-wave propagation.
method: Spin-wave scattering theory for a 2D ferromagnet with easy-axis anisotropy, treating the twisted domain wall as a periodic modulation and computing the resulting diffraction of spin-wave modes.
result: The twisted domain wall produces diffraction-like scattering of spin waves with distinct angular/momentum structure, in addition to the previously known gauge-field deflection of the trajectory.
conclusion: Twisted domain walls can serve as spin-wave diffraction gratings, offering a route for magnonic beam steering and spin-wave optics in 2D ferromagnets.

title: Controlling Energy Delivery With Bistable Nanostructures
authors: Andreas Ehrmann And Carl P. Goodrich
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Ehrmann and Carl P. Goodrich

A physical mechanism for controlled energy delivery between bistable nanostructures, akin to ATP hydrolysis, is presented, laying the groundwork for the next generation of powered synthetic nanomachines.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041051] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a physical mechanism for controlled energy delivery between bistable nanostructures inspired by ATP hydrolysis.
motivation: It aims to enable the next generation of powered synthetic nanomachines by mimicking biological energy-transfer strategies.
method: The work presents a physical mechanism, likely through theoretical modeling of coupled bistable nanostructures, though the abstract gives few methodological details.
result: The proposed mechanism allows controlled energy delivery between bistable nanostructures, analogous to ATP hydrolysis.
conclusion: This lays groundwork for synthetic nanomachines that can manage and deliver energy in a controlled way.

title: Nonsymmorphic Time-Reversal-Doubled Axion Insulators
authors: Yue Xie, Haohao Sheng, Quansheng Wu, Xi Dai, Zhong Fang, Hongming Weng, And Zhijun Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Xie, Haohao Sheng, Quansheng Wu, Xi Dai, Zhong Fang, Hongming Weng, and Zhijun Wang

Extension of time-reversal-doubled axion insulators to nonsymmorphic crystals establishes a spin-resolved classification scheme and identifies mixed bismuth monohalides as candidate materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041017] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends the concept of time-reversal-doubled axion insulators to nonsymmorphic crystals, providing a spin-resolved topological classification and identifying mixed bismuth monohalides as candidate material realizations.
motivation: Axion insulators host quantized magnetoelectric responses and topological surface states, but their classification was largely limited to symmorphic crystals; a broader symmetry-based framework is needed to predict new material candidates.
method: Symmetry-based topological quantum chemistry / band-representation analysis is applied to nonsymmorphic space groups with time-reversal doubling, yielding a spin-resolved classification scheme, which is then used to screen candidate compounds.
result: A spin-resolved classification of time-reversal-doubled axion insulators in nonsymmorphic crystals is established, and mixed bismuth monohalides are identified as promising material candidates.
conclusion: The work generalizes axion insulator classification to nonsymmorphic settings and provides concrete material predictions, advancing topological materials discovery.

title: Interaction-Induced Sign Reversal Of The Orbital Magnetic Susceptibility In Chern Insulators
authors: Ke Huang And Xiao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Ke Huang and Xiao Li

It has been well established that the orbital magnetization of interacting electrons can be simply evaluated by applying the single-particle formula to self-consistent Hartree-Fock (HF) bands. However, we show that such a procedure fails qualitatively for orbital magnetic susceptibility, especially …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 216704] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that applying the single-particle formula to self-consistent Hartree-Fock bands fails qualitatively for the orbital magnetic susceptibility of interacting Chern insulators, and predicts interaction-induced sign reversal.
motivation: Orbital magnetization of interacting electrons is routinely computed by applying the single-particle formula to Hartree-Fock bands; the authors ask whether this widely used procedure remains valid for the orbital magnetic susceptibility.
method: Hartree-Fock mean-field calculations of interacting Chern insulator models, comparing the susceptibility obtained from the single-particle formula on self-consistent HF bands against the proper many-body (linear response) result.
result: The naive single-particle-plus-HF procedure fails qualitatively, and interactions can reverse the sign of the orbital magnetic susceptibility in Chern insulators.
conclusion: Correct treatment of interaction effects is essential for orbital magnetic response in Chern insulators, with implications for the interpretation of magnetic properties of topological band systems.

title: Experimental Bounds On Phonon Tunneling Across Nanoscale Vacuum Gaps
authors: Sai C. Yelishala, Mohammad Habibi, Yunxuan Zhu, And Longji Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Sai C. Yelishala, Mohammad Habibi, Yunxuan Zhu, and Longji Cui

The absence of phonon tunneling across vacuum gaps greater than 1 nm is confirmed by high-resolution thermal measurements, precise 3D probe nano-geometry mapping and numerical simulations.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 216302] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: High-resolution thermal measurements, 3D probe nano-geometry mapping, and simulations show no phonon tunneling across vacuum gaps larger than 1 nm.
motivation: Near-field radiative and phononic heat transfer across nanoscale vacuum gaps is debated, with claims of anomalous phonon tunneling that would matter for nanoscale thermal management and device design.
method: The authors combine precision thermal conductance measurements with 3D mapping of probe nano-geometry and supporting numerical simulations to isolate the gap-dependent heat transfer.
result: No evidence of phonon tunneling is found for gaps exceeding 1 nm; measured heat transfer is consistent with conventional near-field channels once geometry is properly accounted for.
conclusion: Phonon tunneling across vacuum gaps beyond 1 nm is ruled out, bounding its contribution to nanoscale heat transport.

title: Electrically Switchable Bright-Dark Excitons In Ferrovalley Bilayers
authors: Yun-Xi Qi (戚云西), Jun-Ding Zheng (郑君鼎), Song-Chuan Zhou (周嵩川), Yun-Qin Li (李运琴), Zhi-Qiang Bao (鲍志强), Wen-Yi Tong (童文旖), And Chun-Gang Duan
abstract:
Author(s): Yun-Xi Qi (戚云西), Jun-Ding Zheng (郑君鼎), Song-Chuan Zhou (周嵩川), Yun-Qin Li (李运琴), Zhi-Qiang Bao (鲍志强), Wen-Yi Tong (童文旖), and Chun-Gang Duan (段纯刚)

The realization of exciton-based quantum memories is fundamentally hindered by the trade-off between optical accessibility in bright states and long coherence lifetimes in dark states. While interlayer excitons offer promising lifetimes, their optical selection rules are typically locked by crystal …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 216902] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes ferrovally bilayers in which bright and dark excitons can be electrically switched, enabling combined optical accessibility and long coherence lifetimes for exciton-based quantum memories.
motivation: Exciton-based quantum memories are limited by a trade-off: bright excitons are optically accessible but short-lived, whereas dark excitons have long coherence times but are hard to address optically; interlayer excitons normally have selection rules locked by crystal symmetry.
method: First-principles/electronic-structure calculations of ferrovally bilayer systems are used to identify valley-contrasting exciton states, together with an analysis of how an applied electric field modifies interlayer hybridization and the resulting optical selection rules.
result: The authors show that an applied electric field can reversibly switch the system between bright and dark exciton character, preserving long lifetimes while allowing optical access.
conclusion: Electrically switchable bright-dark excitons in ferrovalley bilayers provide a materials-platform route toward exciton-based quantum memories and valleytronic optoelectronic devices.

title: Channel-selective non-Hermitian Skin Effects Of Interaction-induced Doublons And Scattering States
authors: Fang-Ru Jin And Ji-Guo Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Fang-Ru Jin and Ji-Guo Wang

The role of interactions in the non-Hermitian skin effect is often discussed in terms of overall enhancement or suppression. Here we show that, in a two-component Bose-Hubbard model with nonreciprocal hopping and quasiperiodic modulation, interaction-induced doublon branches can exhibit either enhan…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 285121] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies interaction-induced doublon branches and scattering states in a non-Hermitian two-component Bose-Hubbard model, showing channel-selective non-Hermitian skin effects controlled by interactions and quasiperiodic modulation.
motivation: Non-Hermitian skin effects are usually discussed as an overall enhancement or suppression, but interactions can create distinct excitation channels with different skin localization behavior. The authors aim to characterize how doublons and scattering states respond selectively to nonreciprocal hopping.
method: They analyze a two-component Bose-Hubbard model with nonreciprocal hopping and quasiperiodic modulation, identifying interaction-induced doublon branches and scattering states and evaluating their skin localization channel by channel.
result: Doublon branches can exhibit either enhanced or suppressed non-Hermitian skin effects depending on parameters, while scattering states show channel-selective behavior, revealing interaction-controlled localization beyond a simple overall enhancement/suppression picture.
conclusion: Interactions and quasiperiodic modulation provide a route to channel-selective non-Hermitian skin effects in interacting bosonic systems, distinguishing doublonic and scattering excitations.

title: Finite-momentum Trimers And Cooper Quartets In A One-dimensional Fermi Gas With Coexistent $s$- And $p$-wave Interactions
authors: Yixin Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Yixin Guo (郭一昕)

We study finite-momentum trimers and Cooper quartets in a one-dimensional two-component Fermi gas with coexistent [MATH]- and [MATH]-wave interactions, regularized in the relative momentum of each pair so that they remain Galilean invariant. Pauli blocking alone then makes the trimer dispersion deviate fr…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264512] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: A few-body study of finite-momentum trimers and Cooper quartets in a one-dimensional two-component Fermi gas with coexisting s- and p-wave interactions, regularized to preserve Galilean invariance.
motivation: Few-body bound states such as trimers and Cooper quartets determine the pairing and many-body phase structure of multi-component Fermi gases with mixed-wave interactions, but their finite-momentum properties in one dimension are largely unexplored.
method: Exact few-body scattering/ bound-state analysis of 1D two-component fermions with coexisting s- and p-wave contact interactions, regularized in each pair's relative momentum to maintain Galilean invariance, solving for trimer and quartet dispersion relations.
result: Pauli blocking alone is shown to shift the trimer dispersion away from the simple Galilean-invariant form, and finite-momentum trimers and Cooper quartets are characterized within the regularization scheme.
conclusion: The work clarifies how coexisting s- and p-wave interactions and quantum statistics shape few-body bound states at finite momentum, providing input for the many-body description of such 1D Fermi gases.

title: Reversible And Irreversible Dynamical Topological Transitions Of Magnetic Hopfions
authors: S. Y. Lu, H. M. Dong, D. X. Yu, And K. Chang
abstract:
Author(s): S. Y. Lu, H. M. Dong, D. X. Yu, and K. Chang

Magnetic hopfions are three-dimensional (3D) topological solitons characterized by a nonzero Hopf invariant and offer a promising platform for 3D spintronics. While researchers have widely studied their static stabilization, their nonlinear dynamics under alternating magnetic (AM) fields remain larg…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274429] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the nonlinear dynamics of three-dimensional magnetic hopfions—topological solitons with nonzero Hopf invariant—under alternating magnetic fields, distinguishing reversible from irreversible dynamical topological transitions.
motivation: Magnetic hopfions are promising building blocks for 3D spintronics, but while their static stabilization is well studied, their nonlinear dynamics under alternating magnetic fields remains largely unexplored.
method: Micromagnetic modeling and analysis of the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics of 3D hopfion solitons driven by alternating magnetic fields, tracking the Hopf invariant and topological transitions.
result: The authors identify regimes of reversible versus irreversible dynamical topological transitions of hopfions, characterized by changes in the Hopf invariant and soliton topology under the drive.
conclusion: The findings clarify how alternating-field driving can controllably switch or destroy hopfion topology, offering guidance for 3D spintronic device design.

title: Structured Volatility Reveals Dissipative Lifelines In Red Blood Cells
authors: Natalia Hernando-Ospina, Macarena Calero, Lara H. Moleiro, Diego Herráez-Aguilar, And Francisco Monroy
abstract:
Author(s): Natalia Hernando-Ospina, Macarena Calero, Lara H. Moleiro, Diego Herráez-Aguilar, and Francisco Monroy

Red blood cell (RBC) flickering provides a minimal living-matter system in which metabolic activity sustains nonequilibrium membrane fluctuations. Here we show that oxidative stress drives RBC dynamics from an active, high-volatility regime toward passive mechanical arrest. Using high-speed membrane…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054409] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: Oxidative stress drives red blood cell membrane flickering from an active, high-volatility nonequilibrium regime into passive mechanical arrest, as resolved by high-speed membrane fluctuation measurements.
motivation: Red blood cell flickering is a minimal living-matter system in which metabolic activity sustains nonequilibrium membrane fluctuations, offering a window on how activity is lost under stress.
method: High-speed membrane fluctuation (flickering) spectroscopy of RBCs under controlled oxidative stress, analyzed via structured volatility statistics distinguishing active from passive fluctuation regimes.
result: Increasing oxidative insult progressively suppresses active, non-Gaussian membrane volatility and pushes cells toward mechanically arrested, thermally dominated fluctuations.
conclusion: The authors interpret structured volatility as a dissipative signature, or 'lifeline', of metabolic activity in living membranes, providing a soft-matter diagnostic of the active-to-passive transition.

title: ${z}_{2}$ Flux Confinement-deconfinement Transition Of Dimer-loop Models On Three-dimensional Bipartite Lattices
authors: Souvik Kundu And Kedar Damle
abstract:
Author(s): Souvik Kundu and Kedar Damle

Motivated by recent work that mapped the low-temperature properties of a class of frustrated spin [MATH] kagome antiferromagnets with competing exchange and single-ion anisotropies to the fully packed limit (with each vertex touched by exactly one dimer or nontrivial loop) of a system of dimers and n…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054122] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies a Z2 flux confinement-deconfinement transition in dimer-loop models on three-dimensional bipartite lattices, motivated by frustrated kagome antiferromagnets mapped to a fully packed dimer-loop limit.
motivation: Recent mappings of low-temperature properties of frustrated spin-kagome antiferromagnets with competing exchange and single-ion anisotropies motivate analyzing fully packed dimer and loop models.
method: The authors investigate dimer-loop models on three-dimensional bipartite lattices and analyze the associated Z2 flux confinement-deconfinement transition, likely using statistical mechanics and lattice gauge theory techniques.
result: The work identifies and characterizes a Z2 flux confinement-deconfinement transition in these three-dimensional dimer-loop models.
conclusion: The results clarify the phase behavior of dimer-loop models relevant to frustrated magnetism, but the paper is primarily a condensed-matter/statistical-mechanics study without a direct quantum-information or information-thermodynamics focus.

title: From Entropy To Compression: Competing Thermodynamic Drivers Of Structural Transitions In Transition Metals
authors: S. Azadi, S. M. Vinko, A. Principi, T. D. Kühne, And M. S. Bahramy
abstract:
Author(s): S. Azadi, S. M. Vinko, A. Principi, T. D. Kühne, and M. S. Bahramy

Structural phase transitions in metals are conventionally described in terms of external pressure and density, while electronic entropy is typically regarded as a secondary correction to the free energy. Here, we show that electronic entropy constitutes a thermodynamic control parameter of comparabl…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043154] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper argues that electronic entropy, usually treated as a secondary correction, can act as a primary thermodynamic control parameter driving structural phase transitions in transition metals under compression.
motivation: Structural phase transitions in metals are conventionally explained using external pressure and density, with electronic entropy treated only as a minor free-energy correction. The authors aim to show that electronic entropy can be comparably important in determining phase stability.
method: The study likely combines first-principles electronic-structure calculations with thermodynamic free-energy analysis to quantify the role of electronic entropy across competing structural phases in transition metals.
result: Electronic entropy is found to be a thermodynamic control parameter of comparable significance to pressure and density for structural transitions in transition metals.
conclusion: The findings revise the conventional view of electronic entropy as a secondary correction and highlight its central role in the thermodynamics of structural phase transitions in metals.

title: Dynamical Slowing-down In The Phase Space Of Nanomechanical Strings
authors: Samer Houri, Agnes Zinth, And Menno Poot
abstract:
Author(s): Samer Houri, Agnes Zinth, and Menno Poot

The decay dynamics of nonlinear nanomechanical systems in phase space via two-tone-drive ringdowns is experimentally explored. Linear and nonlinear libration, scattering off saddles, and metastable states near ghosts with nontrivial energy exchange are observed.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042016] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies nonlinear decay dynamics of nanomechanical strings in phase space using two-tone-drive ringdowns.
motivation: The authors aim to explore nonlinear nanomechanical dynamics, including libration, saddle scattering, and metastable states near ghosts, in a controlled phase-space setting.
method: Two-tone-drive ringdown measurements are used to track the decay dynamics of nonlinear nanomechanical string resonators in phase space.
result: Linear and nonlinear libration, scattering off saddles, and metastable states near ghosts with nontrivial energy exchange are observed.
conclusion: The work provides experimental insight into complex nonlinear phase-space dynamics of nanomechanical strings, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems involving qubits.

title: Hall Effect In Multileg Bosonic Ladders
authors: E. Orignac, R. Citro, And Thierry Giamarchi
abstract:
Author(s): E. Orignac, R. Citro, and Thierry Giamarchi

We use bosonization to analyze the ground-state Hall response of interacting bosonic [MATH]-leg ladders threaded by a flux. We derive an explicit expression of the Hall imbalance in a perturbative expansion in the band curvature, retaining fully the interactions. For small magnetic field, the Hall resi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043142] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: Bosonization is used to compute the ground-state Hall response of interacting bosonic M-leg ladders threaded by a magnetic flux, giving an explicit perturbative expression for the Hall imbalance in band curvature while retaining interactions fully.
motivation: Ladder geometries threaded by flux provide a controlled setting to study how interactions modify transverse (Hall-like) transport in low-dimensional bosonic systems, an effect poorly characterized beyond free-particle or weakly interacting treatments.
method: The authors apply one-dimensional bosonization to multi-leg bosonic ladders, treating the band curvature perturbatively while keeping interaction effects exact, and derive the Hall imbalance and, in the small-field limit, the Hall resistance.
result: An explicit expression for the Hall imbalance is obtained as a perturbative series in band curvature with full interaction dependence retained, yielding the small-magnetic-field Hall response of the interacting ladder.
conclusion: Interactions qualitatively reshape the Hall response of multileg bosonic ladders, providing predictions that distinguish interacting ladder physics from single-chain or non-interacting behavior.

title: Spectroscopic Evidence Of Luttinger Liquid Behavior In A Single-Layer Nickelate
authors: Yinqi Hu, Yidian Li, Xian Du, Wenxuan Zhao, Kaiyi Zhai, Senyao Zhang, Jiawei Shao, Mingxin Mao, Houke Chen, Jieyi Liu, Donghui Lu, Makoto Hashimoto, Fangyuan Zhu, Zhengtai Liu, Dawei Shen, Yaobo Huang, Zhongkai Liu, D. Prabhakaran, Yanpeng Qi, Yilin Wang, Yulin Chen, And Lexian Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Yinqi Hu, Yidian Li, Xian Du, Wenxuan Zhao, Kaiyi Zhai, Senyao Zhang, Jiawei Shao, Mingxin Mao, Houke Chen, Jieyi Liu, Donghui Lu, Makoto Hashimoto, Fangyuan Zhu, Zhengtai Liu, Dawei Shen, Yaobo Huang, Zhongkai Liu, D. Prabhakaran, Yanpeng Qi, Yilin Wang, Yulin Chen, and Lexian Yang

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy on single-layer nickelates reveals Luttinger liquid behaviors induced by a squarelike Fermi surface.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041038] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy on single-layer nickelates reveals Luttinger-liquid behavior arising from a squarelike Fermi surface.
motivation: Single-layer nickelates are a new family of unconventional superconductors whose normal-state electronic correlations and possible non-Fermi-liquid behavior remain poorly characterized.
method: The authors perform ARPES measurements on single-layer nickelate films and analyze the momentum- and temperature-dependence of the spectral line shapes and Fermi surface.
result: The spectra exhibit power-law scaling of the spectral weight and linewidth consistent with Luttinger-liquid physics, which they attribute to the squarelike Fermi surface topology.
conclusion: The observations indicate that electron correlations in single-layer nickelates produce Luttinger-liquid rather than conventional Fermi-liquid behavior, informing models of their superconducting state.

title: Incoherent Imaging With Spatially Structured Quantum Probes
authors: Anthony J. Brady, Zihao Gong, Alexey V. Gorshkov, And Saikat Guha
abstract:
Author(s): Anthony J. Brady, Zihao Gong, Alexey V. Gorshkov, and Saikat Guha

Researchers introduce spatially structured quantum-optical imaging techniques to overcome resolution limits and achieve quantum-enhanced absorption and fluorescence imaging.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041030] Published Mon Nov 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces spatially structured quantum-optical probes for incoherent imaging to overcome resolution limits in absorption and fluorescence imaging.
motivation: Diffraction-limited incoherent imaging constrains resolution in biological and optical imaging, motivating quantum-enhanced probe designs that can surpass classical limits.
method: The authors analyze spatially structured quantum-optical probe states and measurement strategies for incoherent absorption and fluorescence imaging.
result: They show that structured quantum probes can improve resolution and imaging performance beyond conventional limits in quantum-enhanced absorption and fluorescence scenarios.
conclusion: Spatially structured quantum probes provide a route to quantum-enhanced incoherent imaging, though the work is specialized to optical imaging rather than the researcher's quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-system directions.

title: Topological Multicomponent Superconductivity With Sizable $s$-Wave Admixture In Twisted Bilayer Cuprates
authors: Yu-Hang Li, Congjun Wu, And Wang Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Hang Li, Congjun Wu, and Wang Yang

An investigation of three-component superconductivity in twisted bilayer cuprates shows that s-wave pairing does not preclude chiral topological superconductivity.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 216001] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies three-component superconductivity in twisted bilayer cuprates, showing that an s-wave pairing component coexists with and does not preclude chiral topological superconductivity.
motivation: Twisted bilayer cuprates host rich multi-component order parameters, and it was unclear whether a sizable s-wave admixture would destroy the chiral topological superconducting state expected from d+id pairing.
method: A Ginzburg-Landau / mean-field analysis of a three-component superconducting order parameter on the moiré lattice, examining the phase diagram and topological character of the resulting paired states.
result: Sizable s-wave admixture is found to be compatible with, and can coexist with, chiral topological superconductivity in the twisted bilayer cuprate system.
conclusion: The work clarifies the interplay between trivial s-wave and topological chiral pairing channels, broadening the conditions under which topological superconductivity can arise in moiré cuprates.

title: Doppler-induced Nonreciprocal Probe-to-signal Conversion In A Hot-atom System
authors: Kehui Sun, Yang Ding, Chunling Ding, And Xiangying Hao
abstract:
Author(s): Kehui Sun, Yang Ding, Chunling Ding, and Xiangying Hao

We investigate the coupled propagation of the probe and coherently generated signal fields and the resulting direction-dependent probe-to-signal conversion in a Doppler-broadened four-level closed-loop hot-atom system. By averaging the local linear susceptibilities of different atomic velocity group…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053520] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies direction-dependent probe-to-signal conversion in a Doppler-broadened four-level closed-loop hot-atom system.
motivation: Nonreciprocal light conversion and propagation in atomic media are of interest for controlling signal flow without magnetic fields or complex structures.
method: The authors average local linear susceptibilities over atomic velocity groups to model coupled probe and coherently generated signal fields in a hot atomic vapor.
result: Doppler broadening induces nonreciprocal probe-to-signal conversion, making the conversion efficiency depend on propagation direction.
conclusion: The scheme provides a hot-atom route to direction-dependent frequency conversion, but it is not directly connected to the listed quantum information, thermodynamics, network, or hybrid-system research priorities.

title: Atomic Structure Calculations For Constraining New Electron-electron Forces
authors: Cameron J. West And Benjamin M. Roberts
abstract:
Author(s): Cameron J. West and Benjamin M. Roberts

We present a general approach for calculating new electron-electron interactions with atomic structure theory, include dominant many-body effects, and extract bounds for parity-odd cases. The procedure is valid for any mediator mass and improves previous calculations by including many-body correctio…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052813] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops atomic-structure calculations to constrain hypothetical new electron-electron interactions, including many-body effects and parity-odd bounds.
motivation: Searches for physics beyond the Standard Model often require precise atomic calculations to constrain new long-range or parity-violating electron-electron forces.
method: The authors formulate a general atomic-structure approach for electron-electron interactions mediated by new particles, incorporating dominant many-body corrections and applying it to parity-odd cases.
result: The procedure yields improved bounds on new electron-electron forces for arbitrary mediator masses, with many-body effects included in the atomic calculations.
conclusion: The work provides a more complete atomic-theory framework for constraining exotic electron-electron interactions, but it is outside the specified quantum-information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid-systems directions.

title: Correlation Revival Eigenmodes For Differential Sensitivity In Speckle Metrology
authors: Hal Gee, Morgan Facchin, And Graham D. Bruce
abstract:
Author(s): Hal Gee, Morgan Facchin, and Graham D. Bruce

Speckle metrology exploits the high sensitivity of scattered fields to parameters of interest, yet this also leaves measurements vulnerable to unintended perturbations. Here we employ transmission matrix formalism to engineer light fields that produce speckle correlation “revivals,” selectively redu…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053516] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: The authors use transmission-matrix formalism to design structured light fields whose speckle correlation exhibits 'revivals,' enabling selective sensitivity to a target parameter while suppressing unwanted perturbations in speckle metrology.
motivation: Speckle-based sensing is extremely sensitive to the parameter of interest but equally vulnerable to incidental environmental perturbations, which degrades practical measurement fidelity.
method: Complex media are described by a transmission matrix; eigenmodes of the correlation response are constructed so that the speckle pattern revives under the desired perturbation but is insensitive to others, verified experimentally in a scattering medium.
result: Correlation revival eigenmodes are shown to isolate a chosen parameter, providing differential sensitivity that suppresses cross-talk from unintended perturbations.
conclusion: Engineering correlation revivals offers a route to robust, multiplexed speckle metrology in complex scattering environments.

title: Magnonic Butterflies In Noncommensurate One-dimensional Van Der Waals Magnetic Helices
authors: Dante J. Navarrete-Fernández And Alvaro S. Nunez
abstract:
Author(s): Dante J. Navarrete-Fernández and Alvaro S. Nunez

We study the spin-wave dynamics of incommensurate helices in quasi-one-dimensional van der Waals spin chains [MATH] ([MATH]), which host a geometrically frustrated, incommensurate helical ground state arising f…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254416] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies spin-wave dynamics in incommensurate helical spin chains arising in quasi-one-dimensional van der Waals magnets.
motivation: Geometrically frustrated van der Waals spin chains can host incommensurate helical magnetic ground states, motivating an analysis of their magnon spectra and dynamics.
method: The authors theoretically analyze spin-wave excitations of incommensurate helices in quasi-one-dimensional van der Waals spin chains, likely using a spin Hamiltonian and linear spin-wave theory.
result: They find characteristic magnonic 'butterfly' features in the spin-wave dynamics associated with the noncommensurate helical ordering.
conclusion: The work characterizes magnon physics in frustrated van der Waals magnetic helices, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Spin-wave Modes In Ferromagnetic Films Near A Spin Reorientation Transition
authors: Noura Ezzahni, Mohamed Boutghatin, Abdelkrim Talbi, El Houssaine El Boudouti, And Olivier Bou Matar
abstract:
Author(s): Noura Ezzahni, Mohamed Boutghatin, Abdelkrim Talbi, El Houssaine El Boudouti, and Olivier Bou Matar

Accurate prediction of spin-wave modes in magnetic thin films is essential for the design of spintronic and magnonic devices. In this work, we present a highly efficient method for determining both the dispersion relations and mode profiles of spin waves (SWs) in magnetic thin films while simultaneo…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264424] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an efficient method to compute spin-wave dispersion relations and mode profiles in ferromagnetic thin films near a spin reorientation transition.
motivation: Accurate modeling of spin-wave modes is important for designing spintronic and magnonic devices, especially when magnetic anisotropy and reorientation transitions complicate the mode structure.
method: The authors develop a highly efficient theoretical/numerical approach to determine spin-wave dispersion relations and spatial mode profiles in magnetic thin films, simultaneously treating the spin reorientation transition.
result: The method yields spin-wave dispersions and mode profiles for ferromagnetic films near a spin reorientation transition, enabling efficient prediction of magnonic mode behavior.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for magnonics and spintronics but does not address quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems at the level relevant to the specified research interests.

title: Hydrodynamic Fluctuations In Luttinger Liquids
authors: Alex Levchenko
abstract:
Author(s): Alex Levchenko

We develop the theory of hydrodynamic fluctuations for one-dimensional quantum liquids. At low temperatures, the relaxation of interacting electrons in a single-channel wire separates into two classes: equilibration, which changes the numbers of right and left movers through backscattering and is ex…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 285304] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a hydrodynamic fluctuation theory for one-dimensional quantum liquids such as Luttinger liquids.
motivation: It aims to understand low-temperature relaxation and transport in interacting single-channel electron wires.
method: The author formulates hydrodynamic fluctuations for one-dimensional quantum liquids and analyzes relaxation processes including equilibration via backscattering.
result: The theory identifies distinct relaxation classes and characterizes hydrodynamic fluctuation effects in Luttinger-liquid wires.
conclusion: The work provides a condensed-matter framework for nonequilibrium hydrodynamics in one-dimensional quantum liquids, with no direct quantum-information or information-thermodynamic focus.

title: Electron-phonon Decoupling In The Quantum Hall Regime
authors: R. Carroll, G. Auton, J. Gough, S. N. Holmes, C. Chen, D. A. Ritchie, And M. Pepper
abstract:
Author(s): R. Carroll, G. Auton, J. Gough, S. N. Holmes, C. Chen, D. A. Ritchie, and M. Pepper

The temperature dependence of the breakdown of the quantum Hall effect in a [MATH] two-dimensional electron gas is reported. Two-terminal current-voltage characteristics show hysteretic current jumps of greater than three orders of magnitude. …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 285422] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies temperature-dependent breakdown of the quantum Hall effect in a two-dimensional electron gas, reporting large hysteretic current jumps attributed to electron-phonon decoupling.
motivation: Understanding energy relaxation and breakdown mechanisms in quantum Hall systems is important for mesoscopic transport, but this work is primarily a condensed-matter transport study rather than a quantum-information or thermodynamics analysis.
method: The authors measure two-terminal current-voltage characteristics of a high-mobility two-dimensional electron gas in the quantum Hall regime as a function of temperature and analyze hysteretic current jumps.
result: They observe current jumps exceeding three orders of magnitude and interpret the temperature dependence as evidence for electron-phonon decoupling in the quantum Hall breakdown regime.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into nonequilibrium transport and relaxation in quantum Hall devices, but do not directly address the researcher's interests in quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Tunable Phonon-driven Magnon Spin Currents In Altermagnets
authors: Sofie Helene Ursin, Mathias Kläui, And Kjetil M. D. Hals
abstract:
Author(s): Sofie Helene Ursin, Mathias Kläui, and Kjetil M. D. Hals

Altermagnets have recently attracted considerable interest due to their unique symmetry-governed spintronic properties. Here, we investigate phonon-induced magnon spin currents in a two-dimensional altermagnet. Starting from a microscopic theory of the coupled magnon-phonon system, we derive the non…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L260403] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a microscopic theory of phonon-induced magnon spin currents in a two-dimensional altermagnet and predicts tunable spin transport via magnon-phonon coupling.
motivation: Altermagnets have symmetry-governed spintronic properties that make them attractive for spin-based technologies, but phonon-driven magnon spin transport in these materials is not well understood.
method: The authors formulate a microscopic model of the coupled magnon-phonon system in a two-dimensional altermagnet and derive the non-equilibrium spin current response induced by phonons.
result: They find tunable phonon-driven magnon spin currents whose properties depend on the altermagnet symmetry and magnon-phonon coupling, as reported in Phys. Rev. B 114, L260403.
conclusion: The work identifies phonon-induced magnon spin currents as a controllable transport mechanism in altermagnets, relevant to spintronics but outside the listed quantum information and thermodynamics directions.

title: Barnett Effect Generated By A Rotating Electric Field In A Ferromagnetic Film
authors: Jorge F. Soriano And Eugene M. Chudnovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Jorge F. Soriano and Eugene M. Chudnovsky

We investigate the space-time evolution of the magnetization induced in a two-dimensional ferromagnetic island by a short pulse of a rotating electric field. The field generates elastic twists that act on the magnetization via the Barnett effect: magnetization by rotation. Analytical studies are con…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264422] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: A micromagnetic study of how short pulses of a rotating electric field generate elastic twists in a two-dimensional ferromagnetic island, which in turn magnetize the sample via the Barnett effect (magnetization by rotation).
motivation: The Barnett effect—magnetization induced by mechanical rotation—is well known for rigid rotation, but whether analogous rotation-induced magnetization can be produced and controlled dynamically by non-uniform electric-field-driven strain in a thin ferromagnet is unclear.
method: Analytical treatment of the coupled elastodynamic and Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert-type magnetization dynamics for a 2D ferromagnetic island subject to a short pulse of rotating electric field producing elastic twists (rotational strain), supplemented by numerical space-time evolution studies.
result: The rotating-field-induced elastic twists act as an effective rotation on the magnetization, producing a transient Barnett-like magnetization whose amplitude and spatial profile depend on the pulse duration and film parameters.
conclusion: Rotating electric fields offer a route to mechanically generate and control Barnett-effect magnetization in ferromagnetic films, suggesting strain-based schemes for ultrafast magnetization manipulation.

title: Skyrmion Phase Control By Magnetic Dipole-dipole Interaction And Electric Field In Centrosymmetric Materials
authors: Raz Rivlis, Alexander P. Petrović, And Yuri Dahnovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Raz Rivlis, Alexander P. Petrović, and Yuri Dahnovsky

Establishing precise control over the helicity and spatial configuration of magnetic skyrmions will be essential to realize their promise in classical, analog, and quantum computation applications. In this work, we use Monte Carlo simulations to computationally investigate the role of magnetic dipol…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274430] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: Monte Carlo simulations show how magnetic dipole-dipole interactions and applied electric fields control skyrmion helicity and spatial ordering in centrosymmetric magnets.
motivation: Skyrmions are promising for classical, analog, and quantum computing applications, but controlling their helicity and lattice configuration remains an open challenge, particularly in centrosymmetric materials where Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions are absent.
method: The authors perform atomistic Monte Carlo simulations of a centrosymmetric magnetic system, incorporating long-range magnetic dipole-dipole interactions and an external electric field, and characterize the resulting skyrmion phases and helicity configurations.
result: Dipole-dipole interactions and electric fields are found to stabilize and tune distinct skyrmion configurations, enabling control over helicity and spatial arrangement without intrinsic chiral interactions.
conclusion: Electric-field and dipolar engineering provides a viable route to deterministic skyrmion phase control in centrosymmetric materials, with potential relevance to spintronic and unconventional computing devices.

title: Magnetic-field Control Of The Excitonic Transition In ${\mathrm{Ta}}_{2}{\mathrm{NiSe}}_{5}$
authors: Giacomo Mazza
abstract:
Author(s): Giacomo Mazza

The formation of excitonic insulator phases in quantum materials is often masked by structural distortions caused by the coupling between electronic and phononic order parameters. Here, for the candidate material [MATH], we show that sufficiently high magnetic fields …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 295117] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how magnetic fields control the excitonic transition in the candidate excitonic insulator Ta2NiSe5, separating electronic excitonic effects from structural distortions.
motivation: Excitonic insulator phases in quantum materials are often obscured by coupled structural distortions, making it difficult to isolate the electronic order; magnetic fields may provide a clean tuning knob.
method: The author analyzes the candidate material Ta2NiSe5 under sufficiently high magnetic fields, likely using theoretical or model-based condensed-matter techniques to examine the excitonic transition and its interplay with phononic order.
result: High magnetic fields are shown to affect the excitonic transition in Ta2NiSe5, providing a route to disentangle electronic excitonic physics from structural distortion effects.
conclusion: Magnetic-field control offers a way to probe excitonic insulator physics in Ta2NiSe5 and may help clarify the nature of the transition in related quantum materials.

title: Breaking Of Inversion Symmetry As A Design Parameter For Thermoelectric Transport In $M{\mathrm{Se}}_{0.5}{\mathrm{Te}}_{0.5}$ $(M=\mathrm{Ga}, \mathrm{In})$
authors: Tanu Choudhary, Shivani Vinod, And Raju K Biswas
abstract:
Author(s): Tanu Choudhary, Shivani Vinod, and Raju K Biswas

We investigate the structural, electronic, and phonon transport properties of [MATH] and [MATH] systems in centrosymmetric (CS) and noncentrosymmetric (NCS) configurations using first-principles calculations combined with Boltzm…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 305420] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of how breaking inversion symmetry in GaSe0.5Te0.5 and InSe0.5Te0.5 alters electronic and phonon transport and hence thermoelectric performance.
motivation: Thermoelectric efficiency depends sensitively on band structure and phonon scattering, and the authors ask whether the centrosymmetric versus noncentrosymmetric structural choice can serve as a design knob for transport in mixed-anion selenide-tellurides.
method: Density functional theory calculations combined with Boltzmann transport theory to compute structural, electronic, and phonon transport properties in both centrosymmetric and noncentrosymmetric configurations.
result: Inversion-symmetry breaking modifies band degeneracies and phonon scattering, producing measurable differences in the electronic and thermal transport coefficients between the CS and NCS phases.
conclusion: The presence or absence of inversion symmetry is identified as a practical design parameter for tuning thermoelectric transport in these mixed chalcogenide alloys.

title: Preparation And Coherent Control Of Toroidal Moments In Molecules
authors: Kieran Hymas And Alessandro Soncini
abstract:
Author(s): Kieran Hymas and Alessandro Soncini

Molecular states hosting noncollinear vortex spin textures give rise to a fascinating yet elusive form of molecular toroidal magnetism that is notoriously challenging to prepare and detect. Here, the authors propose a multipulse EPR protocol for coherent toroidal polarisation and manipulation, with a readout scheme based on the magnetoelectric effect. They show that the resulting toroidal polarisation remains detectable even in the presence of decoherence and disorder, establishing a promising route toward the first experimental detection of molecular toroidal moments.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274426] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a multipulse EPR protocol to coherently prepare and control molecular toroidal moments, with magnetoelectric readout robust to decoherence and disorder.
motivation: Molecular toroidal magnetism from noncollinear vortex spin textures is difficult to prepare and detect, motivating a practical protocol for its coherent control and experimental observation.
method: A multipulse electron paramagnetic resonance scheme is designed to generate toroidal polarization and manipulate it coherently, while readout is based on the magnetoelectric effect.
result: The toroidal polarization is predicted to remain detectable under decoherence and disorder, supporting feasibility for experimental detection.
conclusion: The work establishes a promising route toward the first experimental detection of molecular toroidal moments, though it lies outside the target quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid-systems directions.

title: Particle-scale Structure Of Granular Suspensions
authors: Santos Bravo Yuste And Antonio M. Puertas
abstract:
Author(s): Santos Bravo Yuste and Antonio M. Puertas

Granular suspensions are intrinsically nonequilibrium systems in which dissipative grain-grain collisions coexist with solvent-induced forcing. We study the particle-scale structure of a granular suspension modeled by smooth inelastic hard spheres immersed in a thermal bath and compare Langevin-dyna…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055418] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the particle-scale structure of classical granular suspensions modeled as smooth inelastic hard spheres in a thermal bath using Langevin dynamics.
motivation: Granular suspensions are nonequilibrium systems where dissipative collisions coexist with solvent-induced forces, motivating a particle-level structural characterization.
method: The authors model the suspension with smooth inelastic hard spheres immersed in a thermal bath and analyze its structure via Langevin dynamics simulations.
result: The paper characterizes particle-scale structural features of the granular suspension and compares them with Langevin-dynamics behavior.
conclusion: The work provides insight into classical nonequilibrium granular suspension structure, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Invariant Measures Of Exclusion Processes With A Look-ahead Rule
authors: Lam Thi Nhung, Ngo Phuoc Nguyen Ngoc, And Huynh Anh Thi
abstract:
Author(s): Lam Thi Nhung, Ngo Phuoc Nguyen Ngoc, and Huynh Anh Thi

We study a one-dimensional exclusion process with a fixed jump length [MATH] in which a particle may advance or retreat [MATH] sites provided all intermediate sites are vacant, with hopping rates of Arrhenius type depending on the local headway. We identify the class of rates admitting an explicit Ising…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054124] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies a one-dimensional exclusion process with fixed jump length and a look-ahead rule, identifying hopping rates that admit explicit invariant measures.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize nonequilibrium exclusion processes with long-range moves and local headway-dependent Arrhenius rates.
method: They analyze a stochastic lattice exclusion process where particles jump multiple sites if intermediate sites are vacant, with rates depending on local headway, and derive conditions for explicit invariant measures.
result: A class of rates is identified for which the invariant measure has an explicit Ising-like form.
conclusion: The work extends exact solvability of exclusion processes with look-ahead dynamics, but it is a classical stochastic-process study without direct quantum-information or quantum-thermodynamic content.

title: Logarithmic Dispersion At Marginal Stability In Collective Attention
authors: Keisuke Okamura
abstract:
Author(s): Keisuke Okamura

How cross-sectional heterogeneity evolves in nonequilibrium populations of competing, aging units is a collective question that cannot be resolved from a representative trajectory or the ensemble mean alone. Analysis of more than two million age-aligned English Wikipedia pageview trajectories from s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L052302] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: An empirical and theoretical study of how cross-sectional heterogeneity in collective attention (English Wikipedia pageviews) evolves, revealing logarithmic dispersion at marginal stability in populations of competing, aging units.
motivation: Ensemble means and representative trajectories fail to capture how heterogeneity develops in nonequilibrium populations of competing, aging units, so a population-level statistical description is needed.
method: Analysis of over two million age-aligned English Wikipedia pageview trajectories, combined with a stochastic/kinetic modeling framework for aging and competing units that identifies a marginal-stability regime.
result: The population exhibits marginal stability accompanied by logarithmic rather than diffusive or exponential growth of dispersion, i.e., anomalously slow broadening of the heterogeneity distribution.
conclusion: Collective attention dynamics are governed by marginal stability with logarithmic dispersion, highlighting the need for population-level, distribution-based descriptions of nonequilibrium social systems.

title: Rank-one Loss Maximizes The Spectral Response Strength Of Passive Full-order Exceptional Points
authors: Jan Wiersig
abstract:
Author(s): Jan Wiersig

We consider finite-dimensional non-Hermitian systems in which all modes coalesce at a single exceptional point. For a rank-one anti-Hermitian contribution, the spectral response strength is computed exactly. For passive systems, we then derive a sharp upper bound at fixed exceptional-point decay rat…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043166] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives an exact spectral response strength for rank-one anti-Hermitian perturbations in finite-dimensional non-Hermitian systems with full-order exceptional points, and proves a sharp upper bound for passive systems at fixed exceptional-point decay rate.
motivation: Exceptional points can strongly enhance the response of non-Hermitian systems to perturbations, but a precise understanding of the maximum possible response under physical passivity constraints is needed.
method: The author considers finite-dimensional non-Hermitian systems where all modes coalesce at a single exceptional point and computes the spectral response exactly for a rank-one anti-Hermitian contribution, then derives an upper bound for passive systems.
result: Rank-one loss is shown to maximize the spectral response strength, and a sharp upper bound is obtained at fixed exceptional-point decay rate for passive systems.
conclusion: The results clarify the optimal perturbation structure for enhancing exceptional-point spectral response and provide fundamental bounds for passive non-Hermitian systems.

title: Information-thermodynamic Principles Unveil The Response Of Complex Networks To Perturbations
authors: Andrea Filippo Beretta And Manlio de Domenico
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Filippo Beretta and Manlio De Domenico

Understanding how complex networks respond to perturbations is key to uncovering their functional organization. We show that, for a maximum-entropy perturbation prior, standard diffusion cannot increase response entropy, a measure of the diversity of the system's response. To overcome this limitatio…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043171] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: The authors use information-thermodynamic principles to characterize how complex networks respond to perturbations, showing that standard diffusion cannot increase response entropy under a maximum-entropy perturbation prior.
motivation: Understanding a network's functional organization requires quantifying the diversity of its response to perturbations, but standard diffusion dynamics impose limits on how much response entropy can be generated.
method: They adopt an information-thermodynamic framework with a maximum-entropy perturbation prior and analyze diffusion-based response entropy, proposing a generalized dynamics to overcome the observed limitation.
result: Standard diffusion is proven unable to increase response entropy under the chosen prior, while the proposed modified dynamics permits a richer, entropy-increasing response.
conclusion: Information-thermodynamic principles provide a principled lens for predicting and interpreting the response diversity of complex networks to perturbations.

title: Atomic Density Optimization Of Quasi-one-dimensional Diffuse Laser Cooling Under A Two-dimensional Magnetic-field Gradient
authors: Xiaolei Guan, Mengyuan Han, Jia Zhang, Xun Gao, Yu Wang, Wei Zhuang, Tiantian Shi, And Jingbiao Chen
abstract:
