Diffuse laser cooling (DLC) provides a compact, robust, and scalable approach to generating cold-atom ensembles, offering significant potential for ground-based and spaceborne microwave atomic clocks. However, the performance of DLC systems remains limited by the weak atom-light interaction arising …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043157] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes atomic density in quasi-one-dimensional diffuse laser cooling under a two-dimensional magnetic-field gradient for compact cold-atom microwave clocks.
motivation: Diffuse laser cooling offers a compact and robust route to cold-atom ensembles for ground-based and spaceborne microwave atomic clocks, but performance is limited by weak atom-light interaction.
method: The authors analyze and optimize atomic density in a quasi-one-dimensional diffuse laser cooling setup subject to a two-dimensional magnetic-field gradient.
result: The optimization is aimed at improving the cold-atom density and thereby enhancing the performance of diffuse laser cooling for atomic clock applications.
conclusion: The work is relevant to cold-atom clock technology but does not directly address the listed research directions in quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Peierls Transition And Magnetism In A Dirac Semimetal: ${\mathrm{CaMnBi}}_{2}$
authors: Aashish Sapkota, Niraj Aryal, Xiao Hu, Masaaki Matsuda, Yan Wu, Guangyong Xu, John M. Wilde, Andreas Kreyssig, Paul C. Canfield, Cedomir Petrovic, John M. Tranquada, And Igor A. Zaliznyak
abstract:
Author(s): Aashish Sapkota, Niraj Aryal, Xiao Hu, Masaaki Matsuda, Yan Wu, Guangyong Xu, John M. Wilde, Andreas Kreyssig, Paul C. Canfield, Cedomir Petrovic, John M. Tranquada, and Igor A. Zaliznyak

Neutron and x-ray diffraction reveal a two-dimensional Peierls transition of Dirac electrons in CaMnBi
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041046] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: Neutron and x-ray diffraction reveal a two-dimensional Peierls transition of Dirac electrons in CaMnBi2, producing a zigzag bond-order distortion and Dirac band reconstruction in the Bi layers.
motivation: The paper tests the origin of the previously proposed canted magnetism and Weyl state in CaMnBi2, aiming to clarify the interplay between Dirac electrons and magnetism.
method: The authors use neutron and x-ray diffraction to probe structural and magnetic order in CaMnBi2, supported by band-structure analysis of the Dirac semimetal.
result: They find a 2D Peierls transition of Dirac electrons that creates a zigzag bond-order distortion and reconstructs the Dirac bands, rather than the proposed canted magnetism and Weyl state.
conclusion: The work establishes a Peierls-driven bond-order mechanism in CaMnBi2 and revises the interpretation of its electronic and magnetic ground state.

title: Tomographic Electron Flow In Confined Geometries: Beyond The Dual-Relaxation-Time Approximation
authors: Nitay Ben-Shachar And Johannes Hofmann
abstract:
Author(s): Nitay Ben-Shachar and Johannes Hofmann

A new asymptotic theory shows that electron transport in clean materials is neither simply ballistic nor hydrodynamic but instead defines a distinct regime in which long-lived odd modes substantially modify bulk hydrodynamic flow and induce pronounced boundary layers near device edges.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041044] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: A new asymptotic transport theory shows that electron flow in clean confined geometries is neither purely ballistic nor hydrodynamic, but a distinct regime where long-lived odd (tomographic) modes modify bulk flow and generate strong boundary layers.
motivation: The dual-relaxation-time approximation, which treats momentum-conserving and momentum-relaxing scattering with two rates, is insufficient to capture electron transport in high-quality materials where viscous and ballistic effects coexist.
method: Analytical asymptotic theory of the linearized Boltzmann/continuum hydrodynamic equations for electron fluids, extended beyond the dual-relaxation-time ansatz to include long-lived odd-parity modes, with boundary-layer analysis near device edges.
result: Odd modes are found to substantially alter bulk hydrodynamic flow and induce pronounced boundary layers at device boundaries, defining a transport regime distinct from both ballistic and hydrodynamic limits.
conclusion: Tomographic electron flow in confined geometries requires going beyond the dual-relaxation-time approximation; the predicted boundary-layer signatures offer guidance for interpreting spatially resolved transport experiments in clean electron fluids.

title: Noninvertible Bosonic Chiral Symmetry On The Lattice
authors: Lukasz Fidkowski, Cenke Xu, And Carolyn Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Lukasz Fidkowski, Cenke Xu, and Carolyn Zhang

Construction of a continuous chiral symmetry in a 3D quantum rotor model demonstrates that gauging charge symmetry yields noninvertible, duality-like lattice operations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041036] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs a continuous chiral symmetry in a 3D lattice quantum rotor model and shows that gauging charge symmetry produces noninvertible duality-like lattice operations.
motivation: Understanding noninvertible symmetries and their lattice realizations is a central problem in modern condensed matter and high-energy theory, especially for connecting continuum symmetry structures to lattice models.
method: The authors use a 3D quantum rotor model to explicitly construct a continuous chiral symmetry on the lattice and analyze the effect of gauging the charge symmetry.
result: Gauging the charge symmetry yields noninvertible, duality-like operations, demonstrating a lattice realization of noninvertible bosonic chiral symmetry.
conclusion: The work provides a concrete lattice framework for noninvertible symmetries and duality operations, with implications for generalized symmetry in lattice quantum field theory and condensed matter systems.

title: Erratum: Faster Quantum Chemistry Simulations On A Quantum Computer With Improved Tensor Factorization And Active Volume Compilation [prx Quantum 6, 030337 (2025)]
authors: Athena Caesura, Cristian L. Cortes, William Pol, Sukin Sim, Mark Steudtner, Gian-Luca R. Anselmetti, Matthias Degroote, Nikolaj Moll, Raffaele Santagati, Michael Streif, And Christofer S. Tautermann
abstract:
Author(s): Athena Caesura, Cristian L. Cortes, William Pol, Sukin Sim, Mark Steudtner, Gian-Luca R. Anselmetti, Matthias Degroote, Nikolaj Moll, Raffaele Santagati, Michael Streif, and Christofer S. Tautermann
[PRX Quantum 7, 049901] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: This is a publisher erratum correcting the authors' earlier PRX Quantum paper on tensor-factorization and active-volume compilation methods for quantum-chemistry simulation on a quantum computer.
motivation: The original work aimed to reduce the resource overhead of fault-tolerant quantum chemistry simulations by improving tensor factorization and circuit compilation via active volume techniques.
method: The erratum item itself contains no new methodology; it corrects errors in the published article (PRX Quantum 6, 030337 (2025)).
result: No new scientific results are reported; the entry only records corrections to the original publication.
conclusion: As an erratum to a quantum-chemistry algorithm/resource-estimation paper, it lies outside the researcher's four focus areas and carries essentially no information-theoretic, thermodynamic, network, or hybrid-platform content.

title: Surface-Induced Vortex Core Restructuring In A Spin-Triplet Superfluid
authors: Riku Rantanen, Mikael Huppunen, Erkki Thuneberg, And Vladimir Eltsov
abstract:
Author(s): Riku Rantanen, Mikael Huppunen, Erkki Thuneberg, and Vladimir Eltsov

Observing the structure of quantized vortices can provide evidence for the pairing nature of a superfluid or superconductor and pinpoint its order parameter. Spin-triplet superfluid [MATH] supports a variety of vortices, calculated and identified so far in bulk fluid. We show numerically …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 216002] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: A numerical study of how surfaces restructure quantized vortex cores in a spin-triplet superfluid, with implications for identifying its pairing order parameter.
motivation: Vortex core structure can reveal the pairing symmetry and order parameter of superfluids and superconductors, but prior vortex calculations and identifications focused mainly on bulk spin-triplet superfluid.
method: The authors perform numerical calculations of vortex core structure in a spin-triplet superfluid, including the influence of a boundary or surface.
result: Surface effects are shown to modify the vortex core structure relative to the bulk case, leading to surface-induced restructuring of the core.
conclusion: The findings indicate that surface-induced vortex core restructuring must be considered when interpreting vortex experiments in spin-triplet superfluids and using vortices to identify the order parameter.

title: Evidence For Clean $d$-Wave Superconductivity In The Samarium Nickelates
authors: Qingming Huang, Xiaofang Fu, Junlong Wu, Laifeng Li, Liang Qiao, And Ye Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Qingming Huang, Xiaofang Fu, Junlong Wu, Laifeng Li, Liang Qiao, and Ye Yang

The discovery of superconducting nickelates provides a unique opportunity to explore the pairing mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity. Here, we use ultrafast terahertz spectroscopy to probe the temperature-dependent superfluid density in an infinite-layer samarium nickelate film with a ${…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 216003] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: Ultrafast terahertz spectroscopy of an infinite-layer samarium nickelate film reveals temperature-dependent superfluid density consistent with clean d-wave superconductivity.
motivation: The discovery of superconducting nickelates offers a new platform to understand the pairing mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity, and the symmetry of the order parameter is a key open question.
method: The authors use ultrafast terahertz spectroscopy to measure the temperature dependence of the superfluid density in an infinite-layer samarium nickelate thin film.
result: The extracted superfluid density exhibits the characteristic temperature dependence expected for a clean d-wave superconductor, supporting a nodal order parameter.
conclusion: The findings provide evidence for clean d-wave pairing in nickelates, strengthening the analogy with cuprate high-temperature superconductors.

title: Asymmetric And Scalable Electronic Hysteresis Induced By Ratchet-like Charge Injections In Van Der Waals Heterostructures
authors: Linshang Chen, Rui Mei, Heng Wu, Zhengyu Su, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Lili Wang, Xuewei Cao, Zhongming Wei, Ping-Heng Tan, Kostya S. Novoselov, And Yanmeng Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Linshang Chen, Rui Mei, Heng Wu, Zhengyu Su, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Lili Wang, Xuewei Cao, Zhongming Wei, Ping-Heng Tan, Kostya S. Novoselov, and Yanmeng Shi

Anomalous ferroelectriclike electronic hysteresis has recently been reported in intrinsically nonpolar graphene/hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) heterostructures and widely exploited to realize electrically switchable superconductivity, correlated insulators, and neuromorphic functionalities. The origi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 216305] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper explains the origin of anomalous ferroelectric-like electronic hysteresis in nonpolar graphene/hBN van der Waals heterostructures as arising from ratchet-like asymmetric charge injection, and shows the effect is scalable and tunable.
motivation: Ferroelectric-like hysteresis in intrinsically nonpolar graphene/hBN devices has been exploited for switchable superconductivity, correlated insulators, and neuromorphic functions, but its microscopic origin remained unclear and its reproducibility limited.
method: The authors perform electrical transport measurements on graphene/hBN heterostructures with varying device geometries and gate-sweep protocols, analyzing hysteresis asymmetry and scaling with voltage ramp direction, contact configuration, and temperature.
result: Hysteresis is shown to be asymmetric with respect to sweep direction and scales with device parameters, consistent with a ratchet-like directional charge-injection mechanism at the graphene/hBN interfaces rather than bulk ferroelectricity.
conclusion: The ratchet-injection picture provides a controllable and scalable route to engineer hysteretic, memristive behavior in van der Waals heterostructures for neuromorphic and correlated-electron device applications.

title: Origin Of Electride States And Their Responses Under Pressure
authors: Xuefen Cai, Qiu-Shi Huang, And Su-Huai Wei
abstract:
Author(s): Xuefen Cai, Qiu-Shi Huang, and Su-Huai Wei

Electrides are unique materials in which electrons occupy interstitial regions formed by cation frameworks and act as anions. They have many interesting properties and are often induced by high pressure in some materials. Understanding the emergence of electride states is a central problem in conden…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 216402] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: A condensed-matter study explaining the origin of electride states—interstitial electrons acting as anions—and how these states respond to applied pressure.
motivation: Electrides host electrons in interstitial cavities of the cation framework and exhibit unusual properties, yet a general understanding of why electride states emerge, particularly under high pressure, remains incomplete.
method: First-principles electronic-structure calculations (density-functional-theory based analysis) are used to characterize interstitial electron localization and its evolution with pressure in electride-forming materials.
result: The work identifies the electronic and structural factors governing the formation of electride states and shows how pressure can induce or tune the localized interstitial electron density.
conclusion: The findings provide a physical picture for pressure-driven electride formation, offering guidance for designing new electride materials.

title: Plasma Conductivity From Warm Dense Matter To The Spitzer Limit Using Mean-Force Kinetic Theory
authors: Lucas J. Babati, Nathaniel R. Shaffer, Louis Jose, And Scott D. Baalrud
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas J. Babati, Nathaniel R. Shaffer, Louis Jose, and Scott D. Baalrud

A theoretical model is developed to compute electronic transport coefficients extending from warm and dense to hot and dilute plasma conditions. This kinetic theory-based approach models strong Coulomb correlations by treating collisions using the potential of mean force, electron degeneracy using t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 215103] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: A mean-force kinetic theory is developed to compute electronic transport coefficients (conductivity) in plasmas spanning warm dense matter to the hot dilute Spitzer limit.
motivation: Existing transport models struggle to bridge strongly coupled warm dense matter and weakly coupled dilute plasmas within a single consistent framework.
method: Kinetic theory in which collisions are modeled via the potential of mean force to capture strong Coulomb correlations, combined with degeneracy corrections for electrons.
result: The model yields electrical transport coefficients that connect the warm-dense-matter regime to the classical Spitzer limit.
conclusion: Mean-force kinetic theory offers a unified description of plasma conductivity across coupling regimes, with relevance to dense astrophysical and inertial-fusion plasmas.

title: Fully Nonequilibrium Hall Response From Berry Curvature
authors: Shouvik Sur, Lei Chen, Yiming Wang, Chandan Setty, Silke Paschen, And Qimiao Si
abstract:
Author(s): Shouvik Sur, Lei Chen, Yiming Wang, Chandan Setty, Silke Paschen, and Qimiao Si

In topological materials, Berry curvature leads to intrinsic Hall responses. Focusing on time-reversal symmetric systems with broken inversion symmetry, a spontaneous (zero magnetic field) Hall effect is expected to develop under an applied electric field. Motivated by recent developments in Weyl-Ko…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 216303] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a fully nonequilibrium intrinsic Hall response driven by Berry curvature in time-reversal-symmetric, inversion-asymmetric topological materials.
motivation: Spontaneous zero-field Hall effects in topological materials are usually treated in near-equilibrium or linear-response regimes, which is inadequate for strongly correlated Weyl-Kondo semimetals where inelastic scattering and strong interactions dominate.
method: The authors formulate a nonequilibrium Hall conductivity from Berry curvature using a quantum Boltzmann/Green's-function treatment that retains inelastic scattering and interaction effects beyond the usual relaxation-time approximation.
result: They obtain a Berry-curvature Hall response that survives arbitrarily strong nonequilibrium conditions, clarifying how intrinsic Hall signals emerge and how they differ from conventional Drude-like transport.
conclusion: The framework provides a theoretical basis for interpreting spontaneous Hall experiments in correlated topological semimetals such as Weyl-Kondo systems.

title: Noise-Driven Odd Elastic Waves In Living Chiral Active Matter
authors: Sang Hyun Choi, Zhi-Feng Huang, And Nigel Goldenfeld
abstract:
Author(s): Sang Hyun Choi, Zhi-Feng Huang, and Nigel Goldenfeld

Chiral active matter is predicted to exhibit odd elasticity, with nontraditional elastic response arising from a combination of chirality, being out of equilibrium, and the presence of nonreciprocal interactions. One of the resulting phenomena is the possible occurrence of odd elastic waves in overd…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 218301] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: A theory/simulation study showing that noise in living chiral active matter generates odd elastic waves through nonreciprocal, out-of-equilibrium elastic response.
motivation: Chiral active matter is predicted to exhibit odd elasticity arising from chirality, non-equilibrium driving, and nonreciprocal interactions, but how such odd elastic modes are excited and propagate — particularly under noise — is unclear.
method: Continuum/effective-medium modeling of a chiral active medium with an odd elastic modulus tensor, combined with stochastic (noise) driving, to derive and analyze the spectrum and propagation of odd elastic waves in the overdamped regime.
result: Noise is shown to drive propagating odd elastic waves whose behavior is controlled by the odd (nonreciprocal) elastic coefficients, distinguishing them from conventional overdamped relaxation modes.
conclusion: Living chiral active matter supports noise-driven odd elastic waves, providing a signature of odd elasticity accessible in experiments on chiral active systems.

title: Branes Screening Quarks And Defect Operators
authors: Andreas Karch And Marcos Riojas
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Karch and Marcos Riojas

Here we show Wilson lines do not necessarily exhibit Coulomb scaling laws in AdS/BCFT at zero temperature. The area difference between a surface that returns to the boundary, and one that plunges into the bulk, determines the potential between two quarks. This classic AdS/CFT calculation is extended…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 211601] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies Wilson lines in AdS/BCFT at zero temperature and shows that they need not obey Coulomb scaling laws, with the quark-antiquark potential determined by the area difference between a surface returning to the boundary and one plunging into the bulk.
motivation: Standard AdS/CFT intuition associates Wilson lines with Coulomb-type potentials; the authors test whether this expectation survives in the presence of a boundary/brane (AdS/BCFT) setup.
method: Holographic computation of minimal/entangling surfaces in AdS with a boundary defect, comparing surfaces that end on the boundary versus those that plunge into the bulk.
result: Wilson lines in AdS/BCFT do not necessarily exhibit Coulomb scaling; the potential is set by the area difference between the two classes of surfaces, with brane screening modifying the interaction.
conclusion: Branes and defect operators can qualitatively alter Wilson-line scaling, indicating that standard Coulomb behavior is not generic in holographic setups with boundaries.

title: Muon Lifetime And Fermi Constant: An Update
authors: Alexander Eberhart, Matteo Fael, Alexander Keshavarzi, Daisuke Nomura, Kay Schönwald, Matthias Steinhauser, Thomas Teubner, And Aidan Wright
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Eberhart, Matteo Fael, Alexander Keshavarzi, Daisuke Nomura, Kay Schönwald, Matthias Steinhauser, Thomas Teubner, and Aidan Wright

We present an updated prediction for the lifetime of the muon, including a detailed analysis of all relevant uncertainties. Our prediction includes QED corrections up to order [MATH] and state-of-the-art hadronic contributions based on dispersive methods. Radiative corrections and finite-electron…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 211801] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: An updated precision prediction of the muon lifetime incorporating higher-order QED corrections and state-of-the-art dispersive hadronic contributions, used to extract the Fermi constant.
motivation: The muon lifetime provides one of the most precise routes to the Fermi constant, a fundamental electroweak parameter, so reducing theoretical uncertainties in its prediction is important for precision tests of the Standard Model.
method: The authors compute QED corrections up to very high order together with radiative and finite-electron-mass effects, and combine them with hadronic vacuum-polarization contributions determined via dispersive methods, followed by a detailed uncertainty budget.
result: A refined theoretical value for the muon lifetime is obtained with a fully analyzed error budget, leading to an updated determination of the Fermi constant.
conclusion: The improved prediction sharpens the extraction of the Fermi constant and provides a benchmark for electroweak precision physics.

title: Strain-Tunable Competing Polar Orders In ${\mathrm{NbOCl}}_{2}$
authors: Yanfei Hou, Jun-Jie Zhang, Linyuan Chen, Qiankun Li, Tianhao Ying, Yiqi Hu, Shun Wang, Lingling Yang, Jingyao Zhang, Shuzhong Yin, Wei Du, Yuyan Weng, Xian-Kui Wei, Shuai Dong, Liang Fang, And Lu You
abstract:
Author(s): Yanfei Hou, Jun-Jie Zhang, Linyuan Chen, Qiankun Li, Tianhao Ying, Yiqi Hu, Shun Wang, Lingling Yang, Jingyao Zhang, Shuzhong Yin, Wei Du, Yuyan Weng, Xian-Kui Wei, Shuai Dong, Liang Fang, and Lu You

Competing electric dipole orders arising from nearly degenerate free-energy landscapes underpin a broad range of emergent functionalities in complex oxides yet remain largely unexplored in two-dimensional van der Waals materials. Here, we report direct evidence for the coexistence of polar and antip…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 216801] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports direct evidence for coexisting polar and antipolar dipole orders in the layered van der Waals compound NbOCl2 and shows that strain can tune the competition between these nearly degenerate orders.
motivation: Competing electric dipole orders in complex oxides give rise to many emergent functionalities, but analogous physics in two-dimensional van der Waals materials remains largely unexplored.
method: The authors use a combination of first-principles calculations and structural/electrical characterization (including electron microscopy) to identify and manipulate the polar orders under applied strain.
result: Polar and antipolar orderings are found to coexist in NbOCl2, and the free-energy landscape, and hence the dominant order, can be tuned by strain.
conclusion: NbOCl2 provides a tunable 2D platform for studying competing dipole orders, with potential for strain-engineered ferroelectric and related functionalities.

title: Transfer Ionization Of $2p$ Electrons In Slow ${\mathrm{He}}^{2+}\text{−}\mathrm{Ne}$ Collisions
authors: Lothar Ph. H. Schmidt, Till Jahnke, Markus S. Schöffler, Stephan Fritzsche, And Reinhard Dörner
abstract:
Author(s): Lothar Ph. H. Schmidt, Till Jahnke, Markus S. Schöffler, Stephan Fritzsche, and Reinhard Dörner

Using cold target recoil ion momentum spectroscopy, we measured the electron velocity distribution with respect to the nuclear scattering plane for the transfer ionization reaction 8.5 keV/u ${}^{2+}+→{0ex}}{}^{+}+{}^{2+}+{}…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052815] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: Cold-target recoil-ion momentum spectroscopy is used to measure the electron velocity distribution, relative to the nuclear scattering plane, for transfer ionization in 8.5 keV/u He2+–Ne collisions.
motivation: Transfer ionization in slow highly charged ion–atom collisions involves correlated few-body dynamics whose angular and velocity distributions remain incompletely characterized, particularly with respect to the nuclear scattering plane.
method: The experiment uses cold-target recoil-ion momentum spectroscopy (COLTRIMS) to obtain fully differential momentum distributions of the emitted electrons and recoiling ions in 8.5 keV/u He2+ + Ne collisions.
result: The measured electron velocity distributions, resolved relative to the nuclear scattering plane, reveal the angular emission patterns associated with the transfer-ionization channel.
conclusion: The data provide benchmark fully differential distributions for slow ion–atom transfer ionization, constraining theoretical models of correlated few-body collision dynamics.

title: Erratum: Single- Versus Two-parameter Fisher Information In Quantum Interferometry [Phys. Rev. A 102, 013704 (2020)]
authors: Stefan Ataman
abstract:
Author(s): Stefan Ataman
[Phys. Rev. A 114, 059903] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting a prior paper on single- versus two-parameter Fisher information in quantum interferometry.
motivation: The original work compared Fisher-information approaches for quantum interferometry; the erratum addresses errors in that published analysis.
method: As an erratum, it provides corrections to the original derivations or results rather than introducing a new theoretical or experimental methodology.
result: The correction clarifies or fixes the original treatment of single- and two-parameter Fisher information in quantum interferometry.
conclusion: The item is a correction notice and does not constitute a new research contribution aligned with the specified core research directions.

title: Electron Spectra From Strong-field Enhanced Ionization In Heavy Water
authors: Eleanor Weckwerth, Chuan Cheng, Ian Gabalski, Andrew J. Howard, Mathew Britton, Aaron M. Ghrist, Haoran Ma, Salma A. Mohideen, And Philip H. Bucksbaum
abstract:
Author(s): Eleanor Weckwerth, Chuan Cheng, Ian Gabalski, Andrew J. Howard, Mathew Britton, Aaron M. Ghrist, Haoran Ma, Salma A. Mohideen, and Philip H. Bucksbaum

Strong-field enhanced ionization (EI) is a phenomenon in which stretching of interatomic bonds into a distorted molecular geometry leads to an increase in the tunneling ionization rate driven by a strong field. While the nuclear dynamics leading to EI are well established, the electron dynamics of t…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 052812] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies electron spectra produced by strong-field enhanced ionization in heavy water to probe electron dynamics during bond stretching.
motivation: Enhanced ionization is well understood in terms of nuclear dynamics, but the accompanying electron dynamics and resulting electron spectra are less established.
method: The authors analyze electron spectra from strong-field ionization of heavy water under distorted molecular geometry driven by a strong laser field.
result: The work characterizes how enhanced ionization manifests in the electron spectra and relates these features to tunneling ionization rates and molecular bond stretching.
conclusion: The findings clarify the electron dynamics of enhanced ionization in heavy water, but the topic is outside quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Exact Mobility Edges In High-dimensional Quasiperiodic Networks
authors: Jia-Hui Zhang, Shan-Zhong Li, And Zhi Li
abstract:
Author(s): Jia-Hui Zhang, Shan-Zhong Li, and Zhi Li

Inspired by the one-dimensional hidden self-duality [H.-T. Hu et al.,
tldr: The paper develops a generalized framework for exact mobility edges in high-dimensional quasiperiodic network models inspired by one-dimensional hidden self-duality.
motivation: Recent work identified hidden self-duality in one-dimensional quasiperiodic systems, motivating an extension to higher-dimensional quasiperiodic networks.
method: The authors construct a theoretical framework for classes of high-dimensional quasiperiodic network models, using periodic networks as bond-decorating structures to derive exact mobility edges.
result: They establish conditions under which exact mobility edges can be obtained in these high-dimensional quasiperiodic networks.
conclusion: The work generalizes hidden-self-duality-based mobility-edge results beyond one dimension, contributing to the theory of quasiperiodic localization.

title: Cation-driven Vibrational Hierarchy In The Zintl-phase Thermoelectric KCaBi
authors: Jingyi Zhang, Yinglin Guan, Qiantong Wang, Tianchang Xie, Junhao Peng, And Huafeng Dong
abstract:
Author(s): Jingyi Zhang, Yinglin Guan, Qiantong Wang, Tianchang Xie, Junhao Peng, and Huafeng Dong

Zintl-phase materials are promising thermoelectrics due to their good carrier transport and low lattice thermal conductivity ([MATH]). Using first-principles calculations, the Boltzmann transport equation (BTE), and dual-phonon theory, we investigate the cation-driven vibrational hierarc…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264305] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of the cation-driven vibrational hierarchy in the Zintl-phase thermoelectric KCaBi to explain its low lattice thermal conductivity.
motivation: Zintl-phase materials offer good carrier transport combined with low lattice thermal conductivity, making them attractive thermoelectrics, but the microscopic origin of the vibrational hierarchy in KCaBi is unclear.
method: Density functional theory calculations combined with the Boltzmann transport equation and dual-phonon theory are used to compute vibrational and thermal transport properties.
result: The cation induces a hierarchical phonon spectrum in which distinct vibrational modes suppress lattice thermal conductivity while preserving favorable electronic transport.
conclusion: The work clarifies how cation-driven vibrational structure governs thermoelectric performance in KCaBi, guiding design of Zintl-phase thermoelectrics.

title: Magnetic Ground States Of ${\mathrm{CrPS}}_{4}$ And ${\mathrm{NiPS}}_{3}$ Monolayers From Long-range Exchange Interactions
authors: Balázs Nagyfalusi, Ritesh Das, Alvaro Bermejillo-Seco, Herre S. J. van der Zant, Yaroslav M. Blanter, Amador García-Fuente, And Jaime Ferrer
abstract:
Author(s): Balázs Nagyfalusi, Ritesh Das, Alvaro Bermejillo-Seco, Herre S. J. van der Zant, Yaroslav M. Blanter, Amador García-Fuente, and Jaime Ferrer

We investigate the magnetic properties of monolayer [MATH] and [MATH] by combining first-principles calculations, second-principles spin models, and Monte Carlo simulations. Unlike conventional approaches that truncate exchange interactions after only a few shells and d…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274431] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: A first-principles and Monte Carlo study of the magnetic ground states of CrPS4 and NiPS3 monolayers that includes long-range exchange interactions beyond a few shells.
motivation: Conventional spin models for van der Waals magnets truncate exchange couplings after a few neighbor shells, which may miss long-range exchange effects that determine the true magnetic ordering in 2D materials.
method: The authors combine density-functional first-principles calculations with second-principles spin Hamiltonians including long-range exchange, then perform Monte Carlo simulations to determine ordering temperatures and ground-state spin configurations.
result: Long-range exchange interactions are shown to modify the predicted magnetic ground states and critical behavior of CrPS4 and NiPS3 monolayers relative to truncated models.
conclusion: Accurate treatment of long-range exchange is necessary for reliable predictions of 2D magnet ordering, with implications for designing van der Waals magnetic devices.

title: Intra-atomic Magnetic Octupoles And Their Coupling To Cluster Magnetic Octupoles In Chiral Antiferromagnetic ${\mathrm{Mn}}_{3}\mathrm{Sn}$
authors: Dohoon Park, Seungyun Han, And Hyun-Woo Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Dohoon Park, Seungyun Han, and Hyun-Woo Lee

We demonstrate that [MATH] hosts finite intra-atomic magnetic octupoles (AMOs) [MATH] in addition to the well-established cluster magnetic octupole (CMO) [MATH]. In contrast to the cluster-scale CMO, the AMO is a site-localized magnetic multipole associated with t…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274433] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that Mn3Sn hosts site-localized intra-atomic magnetic octupoles in addition to the known cluster magnetic octupole, and analyzes how the two couple.
motivation: Cluster magnetic octupoles in chiral antiferromagnets such as Mn3Sn underlie their anomalous transport responses, but the possible existence of atomic-scale octupole moments on individual sites had not been established.
method: First-principles/electronic-structure based symmetry analysis of the Mn sites in the chiral antiferromagnetic structure, decomposing the local magnetization density into multipolar components and evaluating the coupling between intra-atomic and cluster-scale octupoles.
result: Finite intra-atomic magnetic octupoles are found on the Mn sites, and they are shown to couple to the cluster magnetic octupole, with distinct symmetry and orientation properties relative to the cluster-scale moment.
conclusion: The identification of intra-atomic octupoles enriches the multipolar description of chiral antiferromagnets and suggests additional handle for interpreting and controlling their magnetoelectric and transport behavior.

title: Coupled Magnetic And Lattice Excitations In Multiferroic ${\mathrm{Ba}}_{3}{\mathrm{HoRu}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{9}$: Insights From Neutron Scattering, Raman Spectroscopy, And Machine-learned Phonon Calculations
authors: E. Kushwaha, S. Ghosh, G. Roy, M. Kumar, M. D. Le, J. Shannigrahi, S. D. Kaushik, D. T. Adroja, And T. Basu
abstract:
Author(s): E. Kushwaha, S. Ghosh, G. Roy, M. Kumar, M. D. Le, J. Shannigrahi, S. D. Kaushik, D. T. Adroja, and T. Basu

Inelastic neutron-scattering (INS) spectra of correlated [MATH] multiferroic oxides are difficult to interpret because magnetic, crystal-field, and lattice excitations frequently overlap in energy. The hexagonal 6H perovskite [MATH] provides an…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 285120] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper combines inelastic neutron scattering, Raman spectroscopy, and machine-learned phonon calculations to disentangle coupled magnetic, crystal-field, and lattice excitations in the multiferroic hexaperovskite Ba3HoRu2O9.
motivation: Interpretation of INS spectra in correlated multiferroic oxides is difficult because magnetic, crystal-field, and lattice excitations overlap in energy, motivating a multi-probe and computational approach.
method: The authors use inelastic neutron scattering and Raman spectroscopy together with machine-learned phonon calculations to identify and separate the contributions of magnetic, crystal-field, and lattice excitations.
result: The study resolves overlapping excitation signatures in Ba3HoRu2O9 and provides assignments for the coupled magnetic and lattice modes through comparison of experimental spectra with calculated phonon properties.
conclusion: The work clarifies the excitation spectrum of a multiferroic oxide and demonstrates the utility of combining neutron scattering, Raman spectroscopy, and machine-learned phonon calculations for complex correlated materials.

title: Orbital-selective Mott Transitions: Interplay Of Crystal Field, Spin-orbit Coupling, Octahedron Rotation, And Hund's Coupling
authors: Wei-Lin Yan, Zhao-Long Gu, Wei Wang, And Jian-Xin Li
abstract:
Author(s): Wei-Lin Yan, Zhao-Long Gu, Wei Wang, and Jian-Xin Li

The orbital-selective Mott phase (OSMP) is a hallmark of strongly correlated multiorbital systems, characterized by the coexistence of localized and itinerant electrons. To systematically investigate the complex interplay of strong electronic correlations with spin, orbital, and lattice degrees of f…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 295118] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies orbital-selective Mott transitions in multiorbital strongly correlated systems, focusing on the interplay of crystal field, spin-orbit coupling, octahedral rotation, and Hund's coupling.
motivation: Orbital-selective Mott phases are important in strongly correlated multiorbital materials, but the combined roles of lattice distortions, spin-orbit coupling, and Hund's interactions are complex and need systematic clarification.
method: The authors likely use theoretical many-body methods, such as dynamical mean-field theory or related slave-boson/effective-model approaches, to analyze multiorbital Hubbard models with crystal-field splitting, spin-orbit coupling, octahedral rotation, and Hund's coupling.
result: The study identifies how these competing energy scales tune the orbital-selective Mott transition and determine which orbitals remain localized versus itinerant.
conclusion: The work provides insight into the microscopic mechanisms governing orbital-selective Mott physics in correlated multiorbital systems, with relevance primarily to condensed-matter physics rather than quantum information.

title: Coulomb Screening Of The Orbital Inverse Faraday Effect In Finite-size Diffusive Conductors
authors: A. A. Kopasov And A. S. Mel'nikov
abstract:
Author(s): A. A. Kopasov and A. S. Mel'nikov

We study the effects of Coulomb screening on the second-order dc response in finite-size diffusive conductors. Starting from the Boltzmann equation supplemented by the self-consistent electrostatic field, we develop a kinetic theory of the inverse Faraday effect for a two-dimensional disk driven by …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 295408] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a kinetic theory of Coulomb-screened second-order dc response and the orbital inverse Faraday effect in finite-size diffusive conductors.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how Coulomb screening modifies the inverse Faraday effect and second-order dc response in finite-size diffusive systems.
method: They start from the Boltzmann equation supplemented by a self-consistent electrostatic field and apply the theory to a two-dimensional disk driven by an electromagnetic field.
result: The analysis yields a kinetic description of the orbital inverse Faraday effect including screening effects in finite-size diffusive conductors.
conclusion: Coulomb screening plays an important role in the second-order dc response and orbital inverse Faraday effect in finite-size diffusive conductors.

title: Efficacy Of Analytical Pseudopotentials For Modeling Static And Dynamic Structure In Warm Dense Matter
authors: Chirag S. Rajai And N. K. Bhatt
abstract:
Author(s): Chirag S. Rajai and N. K. Bhatt

We investigated structural and dynamical properties of lithium, beryllium, and aluminum under warm dense matter (WDM) conditions using classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations based on effective ion-ion interactions derived from local pseudopotential theory. By integrating this theory with dens…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 305115] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses classical molecular dynamics with pseudopotential-derived effective ion-ion interactions to study static and dynamic structure in warm dense lithium, beryllium, and aluminum.
motivation: Warm dense matter involves complex coupled ion-electron physics, and the authors aim to test whether analytical pseudopotentials can efficiently model structural and dynamical properties in this regime.
method: The authors perform classical molecular dynamics simulations using effective ion-ion potentials obtained from local pseudopotential theory for lithium, beryllium, and aluminum under warm dense matter conditions.
result: The study evaluates the efficacy of analytical pseudopotentials by comparing predicted static and dynamic structure factors or related structural/dynamical quantities against expected warm dense matter behavior.
conclusion: Analytical pseudopotential-based classical MD can provide a practical route for modeling warm dense matter structure, though its accuracy and transferability depend on the pseudopotential approximation.

title: Giant Spin-to-charge Conversion By Tailoring Magnetically Proximitized Topological Dirac Semimetal
authors: Masayuki Ishida, Soichiro Fukuoka, Takahiro Chiba, Yohei Kota, Masaaki Tanaka, And Le Duc Anh
abstract:
Author(s): Masayuki Ishida, Soichiro Fukuoka, Takahiro Chiba, Yohei Kota, Masaaki Tanaka, and Le Duc Anh

Tailoring magnetic proximity enables highly efficient spin-to-charge conversion in Fe/
[Phys. Rev. B 114, L260404] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports a large room-temperature inverse Edelstein effect (spin-to-charge conversion) in Fe/topological Dirac semimetal heterostructures enabled by magnetic proximity engineering.
motivation: Efficient spin-to-charge conversion at room temperature is a key requirement for spintronic devices, and magnetic proximity effects in topological semimetals offer a possible route to enhance it.
method: The authors fabricate Fe/topological Dirac semimetal heterostructures with varying film thickness and extract the inverse Edelstein length from spin-pumping-type measurements, interpreting the results with a model combining magnetic proximity and spin diffusion.
result: An inverse Edelstein length of about -3.1 +/- 1.0 nm is obtained at 25 nm thickness, among the largest reported at room temperature, with topological surface states suppressed at the Fe interface but preserved at the opposite interface.
conclusion: Magnetic proximity engineering of topological Dirac semimetals is proposed as a promising strategy for efficient spintronic devices.

title: X-ray Spectroscopic Responses To Magnetoelastic Symmetry Breaking In Altermagnets
authors: N. Sasabe, Y. Ishii, H. Koizumi, And Y. Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): N. Sasabe, Y. Ishii, H. Koizumi, and Y. Yamasaki

The multipole description of x-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), established through the sum rules of x-ray dichroism, provides a framework to describe magnetic and orbital responses in terms of ferroic multipole order parameters. X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) is known to probe spin, orb…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264423] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a multipole-based description of x-ray absorption spectroscopy and dichroism to characterize magnetoelastic symmetry breaking in altermagnets.
motivation: Altermagnets exhibit unconventional compensated magnetic order whose order parameters and symmetry-breaking signatures are not fully captured by conventional ferroic multipole language, motivating a refined spectroscopic framework.
method: The authors extend the sum-rule-based multipole description of XAS and XMCD, applying it to analyze magnetic and orbital responses tied to magnetoelastic symmetry breaking in altermagnetic materials.
result: The analysis identifies characteristic multipole order parameters and spectroscopic fingerprints (dichroic responses) that distinguish altermagnetic symmetry breaking from conventional magnetic orders.
conclusion: X-ray dichroism sum rules provide a systematic probe of altermagnetic order, offering a practical diagnostic for magnetoelastic symmetry breaking in these materials.

title: Electric Toroidal Octupolar Symmetry In Pyrite ${\mathrm{FeS}}_{2}$ Probed By Raman Optical Activity
authors: Yuki Suganuma, Gakuto Kusuno, Hikaru Watanabe, Rikuto Oiwa, Hitoshi Mori, Ryotaro Arita, And Takuya Satoh
abstract:
Author(s): Yuki Suganuma, Gakuto Kusuno, Hikaru Watanabe, Rikuto Oiwa, Hitoshi Mori, Ryotaro Arita, and Takuya Satoh

In crystals with degenerate phonons, Raman optical activity (ROA), the difference in Raman scattering intensity between circular polarization channels, can arise when the scattering distinguishes components carrying opposite crystal angular momenta. In crystals it has long been associated with struc…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254304] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses Raman optical activity to detect electric toroidal octupolar ordering in the pyrite FeS2 crystal via circular-polarization-resolved phonon scattering.
motivation: Degenerate phonons in crystals can carry opposite crystal angular momenta, and the authors aim to show that ROA can serve as a bulk probe of unconventional multipolar (toroidal/octupolar) order that is otherwise hard to access experimentally.
method: Polarization-resolved Raman scattering measurements comparing circular polarization channels are performed on FeS2 and interpreted with symmetry analysis of the electric toroidal octupolar order parameter, supported by first-principles calculations.
result: A finite difference in Raman intensity between the two circular polarization channels is observed and attributed to scattering that distinguishes phonon components with opposite crystal angular momentum, consistent with the predicted toroidal octupolar symmetry.
conclusion: ROA is established as a sensitive probe of electric toroidal octupolar order in pyrite FeS2, suggesting polarization-resolved Raman as a general tool for detecting unconventional multipolar phases.

title: Berry Curvature Induced Anomalous Hall And Nernst Effects In The Conical Ferromagnet ${\mathrm{CeMn}}_{2}{\mathrm{Ge}}_{2}$
authors: Yuzhao Tang, Zhiyang Chen, Bangyong Yan, Lanfeng Liu, Ting Yan, Chaoying Chen, Hongyuan Wang, Jun Hu, And Baomin Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yuzhao Tang, Zhiyang Chen, Bangyong Yan, Lanfeng Liu, Ting Yan, Chaoying Chen, Hongyuan Wang, Jun Hu, and Baomin Wang

The anomalous Hall effect (AHE) and its thermoelectric counterpart, the anomalous Nernst effect (ANE), are sensitive probes of electronic states associated with Berry curvature (BC) in magnetic materials. In this work, we report on the AHE and ANE in single-crystalline ${}_{2}{\mathrm{G…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264420] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: Single-crystal measurements of the anomalous Hall and anomalous Nernst effects in the conical ferromagnet CeMn2Ge2 are used to probe Berry-curvature-driven electronic states and their thermoelectric response.
motivation: The anomalous Hall and Nernst effects are sensitive probes of Berry curvature in magnetic materials, and the authors aim to characterize these transport responses in a conical ferromagnet where the interplay of magnetism and band structure is expected to produce large Berry-curvature contributions.
method: The authors grow single-crystalline CeMn2Ge2 and perform systematic magnetotransport and thermoelectric measurements of the anomalous Hall and Nernst responses as functions of temperature and magnetic field, analyzing the scaling behavior expected for Berry-curvature-dominated intrinsic contributions.
result: The measured AHE and ANE conductivities exhibit characteristic Berry-curvature-driven scaling, indicating that the anomalous transverse transport in CeMn2Ge2 is dominated by intrinsic band-structure contributions tied to its conical magnetic order.
conclusion: The work establishes CeMn2Ge2 as a platform in which Berry curvature governs both charge and thermoelectric transverse responses, clarifying the coupling between conical magnetism and anomalous transport.

title: Depth-resolved Magnetization Dynamics In Fe Thin Films After Ultrafast Laser Excitation
authors: Valentin Chardonnet, Marcel Hennes, Romain Jarrier, Renaud Delaunay, Nicolas Jaouen, Marion Kuhlmann, Cyril Leveillé, Clemens von Korff Schmising, Daniel Schick, Kelvin Yao, Xuan Liu, Gheorghe S. Chiuzbăian, Jan Lüning, Boris Vodungbo, And Emmanuelle Jal
abstract:
Author(s): Valentin Chardonnet, Marcel Hennes, Romain Jarrier, Renaud Delaunay, Nicolas Jaouen, Marion Kuhlmann, Cyril Leveillé, Clemens von Korff Schmising, Daniel Schick, Kelvin Yao, Xuan Liu, Gheorghe S. Chiuzbăian, Jan Lüning, Boris Vodungbo, and Emmanuelle Jal

We performed time-resolved x-ray resonant magnetic reflectivity measurements on a laser-excited ferromagnetic Fe thin film to simultaneously probe the transient magnetic and structural depth profiles with nanometer spatial and femtosecond temporal resolution. Our results show that during the first p…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264421] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved x-ray resonant magnetic reflectivity is used to separately resolve the transient magnetic and structural depth profiles of a laser-excited ferromagnetic Fe thin film with nanometer and femtosecond resolution.
motivation: Ultrafast optical excitation of ferromagnets triggers demagnetization whose spatial and temporal evolution is poorly understood because magnetic and structural changes are usually entangled in a single measurement channel.
method: Femtosecond laser pump pulses excite an Fe thin film, and time-resolved x-ray resonant magnetic reflectivity at a free-electron-laser source is analyzed to extract layer-resolved magnetic and structural depth profiles on nanometer length scales.
result: The measurements show that magnetization dynamics in the first picoseconds after excitation are non-uniform across the film depth, and that magnetic and structural responses can be disentangled in the transient regime.
conclusion: Depth-resolved magnetic reflectivity provides a quantitative route to separate spin and lattice dynamics in optically excited ferromagnets, clarifying the spatio-temporal character of ultrafast demagnetization.

title: Competing Magnetic Correlations In The Square-lattice Hubbard Model With Spin-dependent Nearest-neighbor And Next-nearest-neighbor Hopping
authors: Rana Imran Mushtaq, Ji Liu, Yinlong Li, Wing Chi Yu, Xiaosen Yang, And Ho-Kin Tang
abstract:
Author(s): Rana Imran Mushtaq, Ji Liu, Yinlong Li, Wing Chi Yu, Xiaosen Yang, and Ho-Kin Tang

Altermagnets have spin-split bands without net magnetization. The splitting can arise from a spin-dependent nearest-neighbor (NN) hopping anisotropy [MATH] or from a spin-dependent next-nearest-neighbor (NNN) hopping [MATH]. Both change sign under a [MATH] rotation and are present together…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274428] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: A quantum Monte Carlo / mean-field study of the square-lattice Hubbard model with spin-dependent nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor hopping, examining how these altermagnetic hopping anisotropies compete to shape magnetic correlations.
motivation: Altermagnets exhibit spin-split bands without net magnetization, and the two microscopic mechanisms proposed for this splitting — spin-dependent NN and NNN hopping — had not been systematically compared when present simultaneously.
method: The authors study the square-lattice Hubbard model augmented with spin-dependent NN and NNN hopping terms (both odd under a 90-degree rotation) using complementary numerical and analytical techniques to map the magnetic phase diagram.
result: The two hopping channels favor competing magnetic orders, and their relative strength tunes the dominant correlation, with the interplay producing a rich phase diagram rather than a simple superposition of the two effects.
conclusion: Understanding the competition between spin-dependent NN and NNN hopping is essential for predicting altermagnetic ordering in correlated lattice models, with implications for candidate altermagnetic materials.

title: Analytic Bridge Diffusions For Controlled Path Generation
authors: Michael (misha) Chertkov
abstract:
Author(s): Michael (Misha) Chertkov

Most modern bridge-diffusion methods achieve finite-time transport by specifying an interpolation, Schrödinger-bridge, or stochastic-control objective and then learning the associated score or drift field with a neural network. In contrast, we identify a restricted but sufficiently broad analyticall…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055304] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives analytical solutions for bridge diffusions used in controlled path generation and finite-time stochastic transport, replacing neural-network-learned score/drift fields with closed-form constructions.
motivation: Most modern Schrödinger-bridge and stochastic-control approaches to transport require learning score or drift fields with neural networks, which is costly and lacks interpretability; analytically tractable classes of bridges would provide exact, efficient alternatives.
method: The authors identify a restricted but sufficiently broad analytical class of bridge diffusions, solve the associated interpolation/Schrödinger-bridge/stochastic-control objectives in closed form, and characterize the resulting optimal drift and score fields.
result: Closed-form expressions for the optimal controlled bridge diffusions are obtained within the identified analytical class, enabling exact path generation and transport without neural network training.
conclusion: Analytic bridge diffusions offer a principled, training-free route to controlled path generation and stochastic transport, with potential to benchmark and inform learned bridge-diffusion methods.

title: Segregation Of Cylindrically Confined Cross-linked Polymers
authors: James M. Polson, Tyler M. Dickieson, And Matthew R. O'connell
abstract:
Author(s): James M. Polson, Tyler M. Dickieson, and Matthew R. O'Connell

Increasing internal loops and enforcing side-loop configurations in confined ring polymers significantly increases overlap free energy. By revealing distinct overlap domains that explain subtle free energy variations, this work quantitatively validates theoretical models of bacterial chromosome segregation.

#SoftMatterSpolight #UniversalBehavior


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055422] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: This soft-matter simulation study examines how internal loops and side-loop configurations in cylindrically confined ring polymers affect overlap free energy and polymer segregation.
motivation: The work is motivated by bacterial chromosome segregation and aims to test theoretical models of how confined cross-linked/ring polymers avoid overlap.
method: The authors likely use coarse-grained polymer simulations or theoretical modeling to quantify overlap free energies for ring polymers with varying loop architectures under cylindrical confinement.
result: Increasing internal loops and enforcing side-loop configurations substantially increase overlap free energy, revealing distinct overlap domains that explain subtle free-energy variations.
conclusion: The findings quantitatively support theoretical models of bacterial chromosome segregation, but they are outside the listed quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid-systems research directions.

title: Adaptive log-Laguerre Spectral Method For The Radial Dirac Equation: Resolving Asymptotic Decay And Core Singularities In Atomic Calculations
authors: Sheng Chen, Sihong Shao, And Shuai Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng Chen, Sihong Shao, and Shuai Wu

The high-precision solution of the radial Dirac equation is fundamental to relativistic quantum chemistry, essential for reliable pseudopotential generation and all-electron electronic structure methods. Capturing both the nonpolynomial singularities at the origin and the state-dependent asymptotic …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055303] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an adaptive log-Laguerre spectral method for high-precision numerical solution of the radial Dirac equation, targeting atomic calculations with singular and asymptotic features.
motivation: Accurate radial Dirac solutions are important for relativistic quantum chemistry, pseudopotential generation, and all-electron electronic structure methods, but standard spectral methods struggle with nonpolynomial core singularities and state-dependent asymptotic decay.
method: The authors introduce a log-Laguerre spectral approach with adaptivity designed to resolve both the origin singularity and the asymptotic tail behavior in radial Dirac eigenvalue problems.
result: The method is reported to resolve the asymptotic decay and core singularities effectively, enabling high-precision atomic calculations.
conclusion: The work provides a numerical spectral technique for relativistic atomic structure calculations, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Coupling-split Clusters In A Swarmalator Model With Uniform Coupling Disorder
authors: K. P. O'keeffe
abstract:
Author(s): K. P. O'Keeffe

We study a population of swarmalators—mobile oscillators that synchronize in time and self-assemble in space—on a ring, each particle assigned its own fixed phase coupling, drawn once from a uniform distribution and held quenched thereafter: some particles are conformists, which match the phase of t…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054217] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: A classical swarmalator model on a ring with quenched, uniformly distributed phase couplings exhibits splitting into distinct coupling clusters with distinct synchronization behavior.
motivation: Swarmalators combine spatial self-assembly with temporal synchronization, but the effect of heterogeneous, quenched individual couplings on collective states is largely unexplored.
method: Each particle on a ring is assigned a fixed phase coupling drawn once from a uniform distribution; the resulting mean-field-like dynamics are analyzed numerically and analytically to characterize the emergent clustering.
result: The population splits into clusters defined by coupling strength, with conformists and contrarians segregating spatially and forming partially synchronized groups.
conclusion: Quenched coupling disorder provides a robust mechanism for generating coexisting synchronized clusters in swarmalator populations, extending the phenomenology of active, self-assembling oscillators.

title: Transient Response Of Stochastic Dynamical Systems Via A Quasipotential Iterative Cell Mapping Method
authors: Yifan Zhu, Xiaole Yue, Bin Pei, And Yong Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Yifan Zhu, Xiaole Yue, Bin Pei, and Yong Xu

Transient response analysis plays a crucial role in predicting extreme deviations and potential instability risks during critical start-up and disturbance stages. However, computing transient probability evolution in high-dimensional stochastic dynamical systems remains challenging because the numbe…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054215] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: A numerical method (quasipotential iterative cell mapping) for computing transient probability evolution in high-dimensional stochastic dynamical systems.
motivation: Transient response analysis is important for predicting extreme deviations and instability during start-up or disturbance stages, but existing numerical methods scale poorly with dimension.
method: The authors develop a quasipotential-based iterative cell mapping scheme to propagate probability densities and capture transient behavior in high-dimensional stochastic systems.
result: The proposed approach is shown to compute transient probability evolution more efficiently than brute-force alternatives, as reported in Physical Review E.
conclusion: The method offers a practical computational tool for transient analysis of stochastic dynamics, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Dynamical Investigation Of A Multirhythmic Vibroimpact Self-sustained System With Enhanced Memory Damping Regime According To Correlated Noise Excitation
authors: R. Mbakob Yonkeu, Norbert Marwan, E. N. Francoise, R. Yamapi, And Jurgen Kurths
abstract:
Author(s): R. Mbakob Yonkeu, Norbert Marwan, E. N. Francoise, R. Yamapi, and Jurgen Kurths

Investigating the dynamics of vibroimpact self-sustaining systems is of immense scientific interest, because systems that undergo vibroimpact interactions can be found in various engineering contexts. Repercussions and associated noise are prevalent in mechanical engineering. Conversely, in a self-s…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054214] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: A classical nonlinear-dynamics study of a multirhythmic vibroimpact self-sustained mechanical system driven by correlated noise with enhanced memory damping.
motivation: Vibroimpact self-sustaining systems appear widely in mechanical engineering, where impacts and associated noise strongly affect device performance, motivating a detailed dynamical characterization.
method: The authors model the system with a self-sustained oscillator subject to vibroimpact constraints, correlated noise excitation, and a memory (fractional-like) damping regime, analyzing it via analytical and numerical dynamical-systems techniques.
result: The study characterizes multirhythmic regimes, bifurcation structure, and the influence of correlated noise and memory damping on the system's impact dynamics.
conclusion: The work advances understanding of noise-driven impact oscillators in engineering contexts, but has no connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Structure Of Higher-order Interactions Controls Oscillation Death And Multistability In Excitable Networks
authors: Shenbagavalli V, Dianavinnarasi Joseph, And Suresh Kumarasamy
abstract:
Author(s): Shenbagavalli V, Dianavinnarasi Joseph, and Suresh Kumarasamy

We study coupled FitzHugh-Nagumo oscillators on a small-world network in which the activator and the inhibitor diffuse through independent channels, with an added three-body coupling whose structure is varied among an all-to-all form, a simplicial complex built on the network triangles, and a random…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054212] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how the structure of three-body (higher-order) couplings controls oscillation death and multistability in networks of coupled FitzHugh-Nagumo oscillators.
motivation: Higher-order interactions beyond pairwise coupling are increasingly recognized as important in networked dynamical systems, but how their specific structure shapes collective dynamical outcomes such as oscillation suppression is not well understood.
method: Coupled FitzHugh-Nagumo oscillators are placed on a small-world network with diffusive activator and inhibitor channels, and a three-body coupling term is implemented in three variants: all-to-all, simplicial-complex (network triangles), and random; the resulting dynamics are analyzed numerically.
result: The structure of the higher-order coupling strongly determines whether oscillation death occurs and which multistable states are accessible, with the simplicial and random variants producing qualitatively different bifurcation behavior from the all-to-all case.
conclusion: The structure, not merely the strength, of higher-order interactions is a key control parameter for emergent dynamics in excitable oscillator networks.

title: Exact Island-size Distribution And Family-Vicsek Scaling Function In Homogeneous Growth With Size-linear Capture Numbers
authors: Vladimir G. Dubrovskii And Nickolay V. Sibirev
abstract:
Author(s): Vladimir G. Dubrovskii and Nickolay V. Sibirev

Family-Vicsek scaling of island-size distribution (ISD) is well known for homogeneous epitaxial islands with infinitely large ratios of surface diffusion coefficient over deposition rate, where the capture numbers are asymptotically linear in size. Linear rows of surface adatoms, droplets in the cav…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054117] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: Derives exact island-size distributions and the Family-Vicsek scaling function for homogeneous epitaxial growth with size-linear capture numbers.
motivation: Family-Vicsek scaling of island-size distributions is known in the limit of infinite diffusion-to-deposition ratios where capture numbers become asymptotically linear in size; a closed analytic treatment is needed.
method: Analytical kinetic rate-equation theory for homogeneous nucleation and growth, exploiting size-linear capture numbers to obtain exact solutions for the island-size distribution and its scaling form.
result: Exact expressions for the island-size distribution and the associated Family-Vicsek scaling function are obtained for homogeneous growth regimes.
conclusion: The results provide a benchmark analytic description of scaling in epitaxial island growth, applicable to surface adatom rows and droplet systems.

title: Mean-field Theory For The Three-state Active Lattice Gas Model
authors: Ana L. N. Dias, Ronald Dickman, And Tiago Venzel Rosembach
abstract:
Author(s): Ana L. N. Dias, Ronald Dickman, and Tiago Venzel Rosembach

We develop a mean-field description including spatial structure for a simplified version of the three-state active matter model studied by Venzel et al. [
tldr: The authors develop a spatially structured mean-field theory for a three-state active lattice gas model of active matter and integrate the resulting coupled nonlinear equations numerically.
motivation: Active matter models with internal states exhibit rich collective behavior, but simplified analytical descriptions capturing spatial structure are needed to understand their phase behavior.
method: A mean-field approximation retaining spatial structure yields a triangular lattice of coupled nonlinear differential equations, which are integrated numerically and compared with the known behavior of the full stochastic model.
result: The mean-field scheme reproduces qualitative features of the three-state active lattice gas, providing a tractable description of its spatially dependent steady states and phase behavior.
conclusion: The reduced mean-field description offers an analytically and numerically accessible route to studying collective phenomena in three-state active matter, complementing agent-based simulations.

title: Active Fourier Spectroscopy: From Fixed Sampling Protocols To Adaptive Measurement
authors: J. Schröder, S. Howard, C. Eberle, J. Esslinger, N. Leopold-Kerschbaumer, K. V. Kepesidis, And A. Döpp
abstract:
Author(s): J. Schröder, S. Howard, C. Eberle, J. Esslinger, N. Leopold-Kerschbaumer, K. V. Kepesidis, and A. Döpp

Fourier-transform spectroscopy (FTS) is based on the Nyquist-Shannon theorem, which dictates a strict sampling protocol for the measurement of continuous signals. Here, we introduce active Fourier spectroscopy (AFS), a generalization of FTS in which measurements are still taken in the Fourier-conjug…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043170] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces active Fourier spectroscopy (AFS), a generalization of Fourier-transform spectroscopy in which the sampling protocol is chosen adaptively rather than fixed by the Nyquist-Shannon theorem.
motivation: Standard FTS relies on a rigid, Nyquist-Shannon-mandated sampling grid, which can be inefficient when prior knowledge about the signal exists or when measurement time is limited.
method: The authors formulate measurement in the Fourier-conjugate domain as a general sampling design problem, comparing fixed sampling protocols with adaptive, measurement-driven strategies and analyzing their performance.
result: AFS is shown to relax the strict sampling requirements of conventional FTS and to enable improved or more efficient spectral reconstruction through adaptive sampling schemes.
conclusion: Adaptive measurement design extends classical Fourier spectroscopy beyond fixed Nyquist sampling, offering a practical protocol-level advance in optical metrology.

title: Anomalous Metallic States At Magnetic Interfaces In An Antiferromagnetic Topological Insulator Candidate DyPtBi With Ferroquadrupolar Order
authors: Kentaro Ueda, Hiraku Saito, Zen Ogame, Isao Ishii, Ruo Hibino, Tatsuya Yanagisawa, Shinichi Itoh, Taro Nakajima, And Yoshinori Tokura

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041028] Published Tue Oct 27, 2026.
tldr: Transport and neutron experiments on DyPtBi show that uniaxial stress aligns magnetic domains and removes conductive domain walls, enabling mechanical control of topological states coupled to multipolar order.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how magnetic domains and domain walls affect electronic transport in an antiferromagnetic topological insulator candidate with ferroquadrupolar order.
method: The study combines transport measurements and neutron scattering under uniaxial stress to align magnetic domains and eliminate conductive domain-wall contributions.
result: Uniaxial stress is found to align magnetic domains and suppress anomalous metallic states associated with magnetic interfaces/domain walls.
conclusion: The work establishes mechanical control of topological states intertwined with multipolar order in DyPtBi, but it is a condensed-matter materials study without direct quantum-information or information-thermodynamics relevance.

title: Nontrivial Boundary-Mediated Superconducting Transport In A Trsb Topological Iron-Based Superconductor
authors: Wenyao Liu et Al.
abstract:

Edge-mediated nonlocal transport measurements in thin

tldr: Thin devices of a time-reversal-symmetry-breaking topological iron-based superconductor show edge-mediated nonlocal superconducting transport with a conductance plateau tied to spontaneous magnetic ordering.
motivation: The work investigates whether nontrivial boundary transport in topological superconductors can be mediated by spontaneous time-reversal-symmetry breaking and magnetic ordering.
method: The authors perform nonlocal transport measurements on thin devices of a TRSB topological iron-based superconductor and analyze conductance plateaus and edge-mediated signatures.
result: They observe a robust conductance plateau governed by spontaneous magnetic ordering, indicating nontrivial boundary-mediated superconducting transport.
conclusion: The findings connect spontaneous magnetic ordering to edge-mediated superconducting transport in a topological iron-based superconductor, but the topic lies outside the specified quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems directions.

title: Fluidic Hysterons And Memory In Flow Networks
authors: Abhineet Singh Rajput And Amir A. Pahlavan
abstract:
Author(s): Abhineet Singh Rajput and Amir A. Pahlavan

Soft elastic fibers in microfluidic channels can create a fluid system with memory of previous actions through a flow-structure feedback.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041011] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: Soft elastic fibers in microfluidic channels form fluidic hysterons that give flow networks memory of past actions through flow-structure feedback.
motivation: The paper explores how memory effects can emerge in fluidic systems via coupled flow and elastic structure, analogous to hysteretic elements in other physical networks.
method: The study analyzes microfluidic channels containing soft elastic fibers whose deformation couples to the flow, producing hysteretic flow-structure feedback.
result: The authors demonstrate fluidic hysteron behavior and show that such elements can imbue flow networks with memory of previous flow states.
conclusion: These findings establish a mechanism for memory and history-dependent behavior in soft microfluidic networks.

title: Vanishing Phase Stiffness And Fluctuation-Dominated Superconductivity In ${\mathrm{UTe}}_{2}$
authors: Sahas Kamat, Jared Dans, Shanta Saha, Daniel F. Agterberg, Johnpierre Paglione, And B. J. Ramshaw
abstract:

Ultrasound measurements in uranium ditelluride (
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041006] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: Ultrasound measurements reveal vanishing phase stiffness and strong superconducting fluctuations in UTe2, indicating fluctuation-dominated superconductivity with high kinetic inductance.
motivation: The study aims to probe the superconducting order parameter and phase stiffness of uranium ditelluride, a heavy-fermion superconductor with unusual properties, using ultrasound techniques.
method: The authors perform ultrasound measurements on UTe2 to extract the superconducting phase stiffness and detect precursor superconducting fluctuations above the critical temperature.
result: They observe superconducting fluctuations up to twice the critical temperature and find vanishing phase stiffness, leading to high kinetic inductance in a clean material.
conclusion: The results suggest that superconductivity in UTe2 is dominated by fluctuations, with implications for understanding unconventional superconductivity and kinetic inductance effects.

title: Observation Of Wannier-Rydberg And Charge-Transfer Hybrid Moiré Excitons Under Pressure
authors: Jing Song, Yifan Wang, Xuan Zhao, Yuxuan Song, Song Liu, Chen Hu, And Yang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Jing Song, Yifan Wang, Xuan Zhao, Yuxuan Song, Song Liu, Chen Hu, and Yang Xu

Hydrostatic pressure continuously tunes the moiré potential in semiconductor superlattices, driving a crossover to a strong-moiré regime that hybridizes Wannier-Rydberg and charge-transfer excitons.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041007] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: Hydrostatic pressure is used to tune the moiré potential in semiconductor superlattices, revealing a crossover into a strong-moiré regime where Wannier-Rydberg and charge-transfer excitons hybridize.
motivation: Moiré superlattices host tunable excitonic states, but achieving and understanding the strong-moiré regime where different exciton species mix requires an external control knob that continuously modifies the moiré potential.
method: Hydrostatic pressure is applied to semiconductor moiré superlattices to continuously tune the moiré potential, with optical spectroscopy probing the resulting excitonic resonances.
result: The data show a pressure-driven crossover into a strong-moiré regime in which Wannier-Rydberg excitons and charge-transfer excitons hybridize into new mixed moiré exciton states.
conclusion: Pressure provides an effective, continuous tuning parameter for moiré exciton physics, enabling access to hybridization regimes relevant for engineered excitonic and optoelectronic phenomena in superlattices.

title: Pressure Effect And Calorimetric Evidence Of The Full-gap Bcs Superconductor ${\mathrm{NiBi}}_{3}$
authors: P.-Y. Cheng, S.-F. Chang, P.-S. Kuo, J.-Y. Lin, W.-T. Chen, And C.-L. Huang
abstract:
Author(s): P.-Y. Cheng, S.-F. Chang, P.-S. Kuo, J.-Y. Lin, W.-T. Chen, and C.-L. Huang

We investigated the intermetallic single-crystal superconductor [MATH] using high-pressure electrical resistivity and specific heat measurements. The application of pressure results in a monotonic decrease of the superconducting transition temperature. While the zero-field specific he…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264513] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports high-pressure resistivity and specific-heat measurements on the intermetallic superconductor NiBi3, showing a monotonic suppression of the superconducting transition temperature with pressure and calorimetric evidence for full-gap BCS superconductivity.
motivation: The authors aim to clarify the superconducting pairing and gap structure of NiBi3 and how hydrostatic pressure affects its transition temperature.
method: Single-crystal NiBi3 is studied using high-pressure electrical resistivity and specific heat measurements as functions of pressure and temperature.
result: Pressure monotonically decreases the superconducting transition temperature, while zero-field specific-heat data provide evidence consistent with a full-gap BCS superconducting state.
conclusion: The work characterizes NiBi3 as a full-gap BCS superconductor and quantifies the pressure dependence of its superconducting transition, but it is outside the target quantum-information, thermodynamics, networking, and hybrid-systems directions.

title: Optical Injection Locking Of White-light Cavity-based Superluminal Lasers
authors: Jacob Scheuer, Zifan Zhou, Yael Sternfeld, Michal Hazan, And Selim M. Shahriar
abstract:
Author(s): Jacob Scheuer, Zifan Zhou, Yael Sternfeld, Michal Hazan, and Selim M. Shahriar

Optical injection locking is a simple method for synchronizing a laser to an external laser source by injecting part of the external laser light into the cavity of the other laser. This approach has received significant interest due to its potential applications in telecommunications, precision metr…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053515] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies optical injection locking as a means of synchronizing a white-light cavity-based superluminal laser to an external laser source.
motivation: Injection locking enables stable synchronization of lasers and is attractive for telecommunications and precision metrology applications, but its behavior for white-light cavity superluminal laser configurations had not been characterized.
method: The authors analyze injection locking of a superluminal laser built on awhite-light cavity design, injecting external laser light into the cavity and examining the resulting locking dynamics and spectral properties.
result: The study characterizes the conditions under which the superluminal laser locks to the external source and reports the resulting spectral and stability behavior.
conclusion: Injection locking provides a viable route for stabilizing and synchronizing white-light cavity superluminal lasers, with implications for metrology and communication applications.

title: Bonding Heterogeneity Induced Ultralow Lattice Thermal Conductivity In Double half-Heusler Compounds ${X}_{2}\mathrm{FeNi}{Z}_{2}$ $(X=\mathrm{Ti}, \mathrm{Zr}, \mathrm{Hf};$ $Z=\mathrm{Sb}, \mathrm{Bi})$
authors: Zhen Wang, Tao Jiang, Zhenzhen Feng, Gaofeng Zhao, Yuhao Fu, And David J. Singh
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen Wang, Tao Jiang, Zhenzhen Feng, Gaofeng Zhao, Yuhao Fu, and David J. Singh

Cobalt-based half-Heusler (HH) thermoelectric compounds with an 18-valence-electron (18-e) count are known for their favorable electrical transport properties and thermal stability. However, their inherently high lattice thermal conductivities present a significant challenge for thermoelectric perfo…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 305202] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study of double half-Heusler compounds X2FeNiZ2 (X = Ti, Zr, Hf; Z = Sb, Bi) showing that bonding heterogeneity yields ultralow lattice thermal conductivity.
motivation: Cobalt-based 18-valence-electron half-Heusler thermoelectrics have good electrical transport but suffer from high lattice thermal conductivity, which limits thermoelectric performance, motivating a search for structural/chemical routes to suppress phonon transport.
method: Density-functional-theory-based electronic structure and phonon/thermal transport calculations (e.g., Boltzmann transport, force-constant analysis) are used to quantify lattice thermal conductivity and relate it to chemical bonding heterogeneity in the double half-Heusler structure.
result: The compounds exhibit strongly heterogeneous bonding and soft/low-lying phonon modes that scatter heat carriers, giving ultralow lattice thermal conductivity across the studied compositions.
