conclusion: Bonding heterogeneity in double half-Heusler compounds is an effective design principle for reducing lattice thermal conductivity and improving thermoelectric performance.

title: Photoinduced Phase Heterogeneity And Charge Localization In SnSe
authors: Benjamin J. Dringoli, Stefano Mocatti, Giovanni Marini, Zhongzhen Luo, Matteo Calandra, Mercouri G. Kanatzidis, And David G. Cooke
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Dringoli, Stefano Mocatti, Giovanni Marini, Zhongzhen Luo, Matteo Calandra, Mercouri G. Kanatzidis, and David G. Cooke

Time-resolved multi-terahertz (THz) spectroscopy is used to observe pump-fluence-dependent dynamics in the optical conductivity of photoexcited tin selenide (SnSe) over an ultrabroadband spectral range of 0.5–11 THz at fluences from 0.1 to 7.5 [MATH]. A free carrier Drude sp…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 264303] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved multi-terahertz spectroscopy reveals pump-fluence-dependent photoinduced phase heterogeneity and charge localization in SnSe.
motivation: The paper aims to understand non-equilibrium optical conductivity and carrier dynamics in photoexcited tin selenide across a broad THz range.
method: The authors use ultrafast pump-probe multi-THz spectroscopy from 0.5 to 11 THz at fluences of 0.1 to 7.5 mJ/cm2 and analyze the resulting conductivity spectra.
result: The measurements show Drude-like free-carrier response together with signatures of phase heterogeneity and charge localization that depend on pump fluence.
conclusion: The work provides insight into photoinduced electronic phases in SnSe but is a condensed-matter spectroscopy study without direct relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Metastability Limit In The Supercooled Liquid State And Its Implications For Glass Formation And Crystallization
authors: Kengo Nishio
abstract:
Author(s): Kengo Nishio

A supercooled liquid is thermodynamically unstable relative to the crystal, yet it can persist for long times near the melting temperature. Its lifetime, however, decreases with decreasing temperature. In some systems, a metastability-limit temperature has been reported, below which the system cryst…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055417] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies a metastability-limit temperature in supercooled liquids below which crystallization becomes inevitable, and discusses consequences for glass formation.
motivation: Supercooled liquids are thermodynamically unstable against crystallization yet persist near melting, and understanding the temperature at which this metastability terminates is central to explaining why some systems form glasses rather than crystals.
method: Theoretical/numerical analysis of the lifetime of supercooled liquid states as a function of temperature, locating a metastability-limit temperature and relating it to glass-forming ability and crystallization kinetics.
result: A metastability-limit temperature is derived/reported below which the supercooled liquid crystallizes, providing a criterion connecting this limit to observed glass formation and crystallization behavior.
conclusion: The metastability limit offers a thermodynamic-kinetic framework for rationalizing glass formation versus crystallization in supercooled liquids.

title: Accurate Simulation Of Pulled And Pushed Fronts In The Nonautonomous Fisher-Kolmogorov-Petrovsky-Piskunov Equation
authors: Troy Tsubota, Smridhi Mahajan, Adrian van Kan, And Edgar Knobloch
abstract:
Author(s): Troy Tsubota, Smridhi Mahajan, Adrian van Kan, and Edgar Knobloch

This paper develops a numerical method for simulating front propagation with time-dependent growth and diffusion coefficients. The authors find that it compares well with previous approaches, and observe complex nonlinear behavior for such nonautonomous fronts.

#TechnicalAdvancement #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054216] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: A numerical method for simulating pulled and pushed front propagation in the Fisher-Kolmogorov-Petrovsky-Piskunov equation with time-dependent growth and diffusion coefficients.
motivation: Nonautonomous reaction-diffusion fronts with time-varying coefficients are hard to simulate accurately, and existing schemes have not been validated against each other for such regimes.
method: The authors develop and benchmark a numerical integration scheme for the FKPP equation with time-dependent growth and diffusion, comparing it against previous approaches and analyzing the resulting nonlinear front dynamics.
result: The proposed method agrees well with prior approaches and reveals rich nonlinear behavior, including distinguishing pulled versus pushed front regimes under nonautonomous driving.
conclusion: The scheme provides a reliable tool for studying time-dependent reaction-diffusion fronts, though the work remains within classical applied PDE analysis.

title: Prospective Coding And Path Integration Emerge As Equilibrium Solutions Of Self-organizing Neural Networks With Firing-rate Adaptation
authors: Facundo Emina And Emilio Kropff
abstract:
Author(s): Facundo Emina and Emilio Kropff

Continuous attractor neural networks traditionally rely on prewired recurrent connectivity to model spatial representations, path integration, and anticipatory dynamics. However, the biological mechanisms through which this structured connectivity emerges via learning remain relatively unexplored. T…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054405] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that prospective coding and path-integration-like dynamics can emerge as equilibrium solutions of self-organizing continuous attractor neural networks whose recurrent connectivity is learned rather than prewired, aided by firing-rate adaptation.
motivation: Continuous attractor networks typically assume structured recurrent connectivity is given, leaving open how such spatial-representation connectivity could arise biologically through learning.
method: The authors study self-organizing neural network models in which recurrent connections develop via learning rules and firing-rate adaptation, and analyze the resulting equilibrium states of the network dynamics.
result: The learned networks settle into equilibrium configurations that support anticipatory (prospective) coding and path-integration behavior comparable to prewired continuous attractor models.
conclusion: Structured connectivity underlying spatial representation and path integration can self-organize from plasticity and adaptation, offering a biologically plausible route to canonical navigation circuits.

title: Self-learning Mechanical Circuits
authors: Vishal P. Patil, Ian Ho, And Manu Prakash
abstract:
Author(s): Vishal P. Patil, Ian Ho, and Manu Prakash

Adaptivity and learning are ubiquitous in living systems, from cytoplasm and biofilms to animal flocks. However, the problem of designing nonliving mechanical systems capable of self-learning behavior continues to present theoretical and experimental challenges. Here we introduce self-learning mecha…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054211] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces self-learning mechanical circuits, demonstrating adaptive learning behavior in nonliving mechanical systems.
motivation: Adaptivity and learning are ubiquitous in living systems, but designing nonliving mechanical systems that can self-learn remains a theoretical and experimental challenge.
method: The authors design and experimentally realize mechanical circuits capable of self-learning behavior, likely using local physical interactions or learning rules embodied in the circuit structure.
result: They demonstrate self-learning behavior in mechanical circuits, showing that nonliving mechanical systems can adapt through experience.
conclusion: This work offers a route toward adaptive mechanical systems and broadens the scope of learning beyond biological or electronic substrates.

title: Decay Cascade Of The $3{d}^{−1}$ Vacancy In Krypton Clusters
authors: Lutz Marder, Catmarna Küstner-Wetekam, Nils Kiefer, Johannes Viehmann, Niklas Golchert, Emilia Heikura, Florian Trinter, Denis Cubaynes, Jérôme Palaudoux, Francis Penent, Arno Ehresmann, And Andreas Hans
abstract:
Author(s): Lutz Marder, Catmarna Küstner-Wetekam, Nils Kiefer, Johannes Viehmann, Niklas Golchert, Emilia Heikura, Florian Trinter, Denis Cubaynes, Jérôme Palaudoux, Francis Penent, Arno Ehresmann, and Andreas Hans

We report a comprehensive study of the decay cascade of [MATH] vacancies of Kr atoms in clusters using coincident detection of up to four electrons and one ultraviolet photon. We find that the intra-atomic Auger decays predominantly proceed similarly to the atomic case, with a cluster counterpa…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043160] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: A coincidence study of the multi-step Auger decay cascade of 3d vacancies in krypton clusters using up to four electron and one photon coincidence detection.
motivation: The authors aim to determine how the intra-atomic Auger relaxation of inner-shell vacancies is modified when atoms are embedded in a van der Waals cluster environment.
method: Coincident multi-electron (up to four) and vacuum-ultraviolet photon spectroscopy of Kr clusters following inner-shell ionization, compared with the isolated-atom case.
result: The Auger cascade proceeds largely as in the free atom, with a cluster-specific counterpart channel and modified branching ratios identified in the coincidence spectra.
conclusion: Cluster embedding perturbs but does not fundamentally alter the intra-atomic decay cascade, providing a benchmark for interatomic Coulombic decay studies in weakly bound matter.

title: Superconducting Half-Dome In Bilayer Nickelates
authors: Yidi Liu, Bai Yang Wang, Jiarui Li, Yaoju Tarn, Lopa Bhatt, Michael Colletta, Yi-Ming Wu, Sang-Jun Lee, Cheng-Tai Kuo, Jun-Sik Lee, Berit H. Goodge, David A. Muller, Zhi-Xun Shen, Srinivas Raghu, Harold Y. Hwang, And Yijun Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Yidi Liu, Bai Yang Wang, Jiarui Li, Yaoju Tarn, Lopa Bhatt, Michael Colletta, Yi-Ming Wu, Sang-Jun Lee, Cheng-Tai Kuo, Jun-Sik Lee, Berit H. Goodge, David A. Muller, Zhi-Xun Shen, Srinivas Raghu, Harold Y. Hwang, and Yijun Yu

Systematic oxygen tuning in bilayer nickelate thin films reveals an asymmetric half-dome superconducting phase driven by the competing electronic and structural roles of oxygen.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041050] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: Oxygen tuning in bilayer nickelate thin films reveals an asymmetric half-dome superconducting phase arising from competing electronic and structural roles of oxygen.
motivation: Bilayer nickelates are an emerging family of unconventional superconductors, and understanding how oxygen content controls their superconducting phase is key to clarifying the underlying pairing mechanism.
method: The authors systematically vary oxygen content in bilayer nickelate thin films and characterize the resulting electronic and structural changes using transport, spectroscopy, and microscopy techniques.
result: They observe a half-dome-shaped superconducting phase that is asymmetric with respect to oxygen tuning, driven by the dual electronic and structural effects of oxygen.
conclusion: The work establishes oxygen as a critical tuning parameter in bilayer nickelate superconductors and highlights the interplay between electronic and structural degrees of freedom in determining the superconducting phase.

title: Order By Inertia In Spinning Active Matter: Holey Fluids And Spin-Textured Crystals
authors: Camille Jorge And Denis Bartolo
abstract:
Author(s): Camille Jorge and Denis Bartolo

Experiments with macroscopic spinning particles that stir the surrounding fluid at high Reynolds numbers reveal that inertia plays an organizing role in active systems, promoting the emergence of collective structured phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041034] Published Fri Nov 06, 2026.
tldr: Macroscopic spinning particles that stir fluid at high Reynolds number show that inertia organizes active systems into collective structured phases such as holey fluids and spin-textured crystals.
motivation: Active matter studies typically neglect inertia, so the authors ask whether inertial effects can play an organizing role in collectively moving active systems.
method: Experiments with macroscopic spinning particles driving flows at high Reynolds numbers, combined with analysis of the resulting collective phases and their ordering.
result: Inertia is found to promote the emergence of novel collective structured phases, including 'holey' fluid states and spin-textured crystalline arrangements.
conclusion: Inertia, rather than being a mere nuisance, is an organizing principle in active matter, yielding new nonequilibrium phases with textured spin order.

title: Ionization And Dissociation Energies Of Molecular Hydrogen
authors: Ioana Doran, Charlaine Roth, Nicolas Hölsch, Maximilian Beyer, Andrés Martínez de Velasco, Vincent Barbé, Mathieu Collombon, Elmer Gründeman, Julian J. Krauth, Jinjun Liu, Josef A. Agner, Urs Hollenstein, Andreas Osterwalder, Hansjürg Schmutz, Daniel Sprecher, Andrea Wüest, Wim Ubachs, Christian Jungen, Kjeld S. E. Eikema, And Frédéric Merkt
abstract:
Author(s): Ioana Doran, Charlaine Roth, Nicolas Hölsch, Maximilian Beyer, Andrés Martínez de Velasco, Vincent Barbé, Mathieu Collombon, Elmer Gründeman, Julian J. Krauth, Jinjun Liu, Josef A. Agner, Urs Hollenstein, Andreas Osterwalder, Hansjürg Schmutz, Daniel Sprecher, Andrea Wüest, Wim Ubachs, Christian Jungen, Kjeld S. E. Eikema, and Frédéric Merkt

A fivefold improvement in the accuracy of the ionization and dissociation energies of molecular hydrogen is achieved, establishing stringent benchmarks for two-electron quantum calculations in the context of searches for physics beyond the standard model.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041032] Published Thu Nov 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports highly precise ionization and dissociation energies of molecular hydrogen, improving accuracy fivefold for benchmarking two-electron quantum calculations and fundamental-physics tests.
motivation: Molecular hydrogen provides a clean two-electron system for testing quantum electrodynamics and searching for physics beyond the Standard Model, motivating precision spectroscopic benchmarks.
method: High-resolution spectroscopic measurements determine ionization and dissociation energies of H2 with substantially improved accuracy.
result: The ionization and dissociation energies are measured with a fivefold accuracy improvement, establishing stringent benchmarks for two-electron quantum calculations.
conclusion: The results provide precise reference values for fundamental physics tests but are not directly connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Electric-Field-Induced X-Ray Nonreciprocal Dichroism In Hematite
authors: Takeshi Hayashida, Koei Matsumoto, Keito Arakawa, Yves Joly, Sergio Di Matteo, Kenji Tamasaku, Yoshikazu Tanaka, And Tsuyoshi Kimura
abstract:
Author(s): Takeshi Hayashida, Koei Matsumoto, Keito Arakawa, Yves Joly, Sergio Di Matteo, Kenji Tamasaku, Yoshikazu Tanaka, and Tsuyoshi Kimura

X-ray absorption spectroscopy under an applied electric field uncovers signatures of hidden higher-order magnetic multipoles in hematite (
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041015] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: Electric-field-induced X-ray nonreciprocal dichroism in hematite reveals signatures of hidden higher-order magnetic multipoles, supported by theoretical calculations.
motivation: The study aims to uncover hidden magnetic multipole order in hematite through electric-field-controlled X-ray absorption spectroscopy.
method: The authors perform X-ray absorption spectroscopy under an applied electric field and compare the observed nonreciprocal dichroism with theoretical calculations.
result: They observe electric-field-induced X-ray nonreciprocal dichroism attributed to higher-order magnetic multipoles in hematite.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a spectroscopic route to detect hidden magnetic multipole order in a condensed-matter material, but it is not directly relevant to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Retrieval Of Equivalent Material Parameters For Metamaterials At Exceptional Points And Lines Of Degeneracy
authors: Peyman Abdipour And George V. Eleftheriades
abstract:
Author(s): Peyman Abdipour and George V. Eleftheriades

The analysis and synthesis of electromagnetic metamaterials are commonly carried out through homogenization techniques or methods for the extraction of equivalent material parameters (EMPs). In this regard, equivalent homogenized media are proposed such that similar electromagnetic behaviors can be …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254205] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops homogenization and equivalent-material-parameter retrieval techniques for electromagnetic metamaterials operating near exceptional points and exceptional lines of degeneracy.
motivation: Standard parameter extraction (S-parameter retrieval, homogenization) breaks down or becomes ambiguous when the effective medium is non-Hermitian and sits at an exceptional point, where eigenmodes coalesce; a consistent retrieval scheme is needed.
method: Analytical and numerical treatment of equivalent homogenized media for metamaterial slabs, extending retrieval algorithms to exceptional-point and exceptional-line regimes and comparing retrieved parameters against target electromagnetic responses.
result: The authors show how equivalent material parameters can be retrieved such that the homogenized medium reproduces the desired scattering behaviour, clarifying the role of degeneracies in the extraction procedure.
conclusion: Retrieval of equivalent parameters remains viable at and around exceptional points/lines, providing a practical design tool for non-Hermitian electromagnetic metamaterials.

title: Solving The Domain Wall Problem: Primordial Magnetic Fields As A Dynamical Solution
authors: Zizhuo Zhao, Yuefeng Di, Ligong Bian, And Jing Shu
abstract:
Author(s): Zizhuo Zhao, Yuefeng Di, Ligong Bian, and Jing Shu

To prevent overclosing the Universe, stable domain walls must decay—a problem typically addressed by breaking the Peccei-Quinn symmetry with a bias term. In this Letter, we present a novel mechanism in which a helical primordial magnetic field provides a spatially inhomogeneous Chern-Simons source t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 211001] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: A cosmological mechanism in which a helical primordial magnetic field supplies a spatially inhomogeneous Chern-Simons source that biases and destabilizes stable domain walls, solving the domain wall problem without an explicit Peccei-Quinn bias term.
motivation: Stable domain walls would overclose the Universe, so they must decay; the standard remedy is to break the Peccei-Quinn symmetry with an ad hoc bias term, which the authors aim to replace with a dynamical, field-based mechanism.
method: The authors construct a model in which a helical primordial magnetic field couples to the axion sector through a Chern-Simons term, producing an inhomogeneous potential bias on the domain-wall network, and they analyze the resulting wall dynamics and annihilation.
result: The induced Chern-Simons bias is shown to be sufficient to drive domain walls to decay, alleviating the overclosure problem while simultaneously linking the wall dynamics to the presence of helical magnetic fields.
conclusion: Primordial magnetic fields can act as a dynamical solution to the domain wall problem, offering a cosmologically motivated alternative to explicit Peccei-Quinn symmetry breaking and potentially leaving observable imprints tied to magnetogenesis.

title: Minding The Gap Between Hard And Diffractive Structure Functions At The Electron-Ion Collider
authors: June-Haak Ee, Christopher Lee, And Stella T. Schindler
abstract:
Author(s): June-Haak Ee, Christopher Lee, and Stella T. Schindler

Diffraction is characterized by forward scattering and a large rapidity gap. Ordinary hard scattering also produces gapped events and presents a significant background to identification of diffractively produced events. We present a fully differential factorization of gapped hard [MATH] scattering. We…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 211902] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a fully differential factorization framework for gapped hard scattering to separate diffractive events from ordinary hard-scattering backgrounds at a future Electron-Ion Collider.
motivation: Diffractive events are identified by forward scattering and large rapidity gaps, but ordinary hard QCD scattering also produces gapped events, creating a serious background problem for diffractive event identification at the EIC.
method: The authors derive a fully differential QCD factorization for gapped hard scattering, allowing a systematic comparison of the gap-producing contributions from hard versus diffractive processes.
result: The factorization clarifies how the hard-scattering gap spectrum can be computed and distinguished from diffractive production, quantifying the background that must be controlled in EIC measurements.
conclusion: A rigorous treatment of rapidity-gap events is needed to disentangle genuine diffraction from ordinary hard scattering in EIC data, motivating refined experimental analyses.

title: System Size Dependence Of Collisionless Reconnection Rate
authors: Yi-Min Huang, Naoki Bessho, Li-Jen Chen, Judith T. Karpen, And Amitava Bhattacharjee
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Min Huang, Naoki Bessho, Li-Jen Chen, Judith T. Karpen, and Amitava Bhattacharjee

It is a widely accepted paradigm that collisionless magnetic reconnection proceeds at a universal fast rate of [MATH] when normalized to a properly defined reconnecting magnetic field and Alfvén speed, effectively independent of the macroscopic system size. This conclusion, derived primarily from ki…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 215201] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: A plasma-physics study showing that the collisionless magnetic reconnection rate can depend on the macroscopic system size, challenging the paradigm of a universal fast rate.
motivation: The widely accepted view holds that collisionless reconnection proceeds at a universal fast rate (~0.1) independent of system size, an inference drawn mainly from kinetic simulations of limited domain size; the authors test whether this universality survives at larger scales.
method: Kinetic (particle-in-cell) simulations of collisionless magnetic reconnection are performed with systematically increasing domain sizes, and the resulting normalized reconnection rates are compared across system sizes.
result: The reconnection rate is found to exhibit a dependence on the macroscopic system size, contradicting the presumed universal, size-independent fast rate.
conclusion: The universality of the fast collisionless reconnection rate must be revisited, with implications for reconnection in large astrophysical and space-plasma systems.

title: Four-Loop Nonsinglet Splitting Functions In Qcd
authors: Thomas Gehrmann, Andreas von Manteuffel, Vasily Sotnikov, And Tong-Zhi Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Gehrmann, Andreas von Manteuffel, Vasily Sotnikov, and Tong-Zhi Yang

The scale evolution of parton distributions is governed by splitting functions. We compute the four-loop splitting functions in perturbative QCD that control the evolution of quark nonsinglet distributions. We confirm previous partial results and obtain, for the first time, fully analytic expression…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 211901] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The authors compute the four-loop QCD nonsinglet splitting functions fully analytically, which govern the scale evolution of quark nonsinglet parton distributions.
motivation: Precise knowledge of splitting functions is required for high-precision collider phenomenology and for controlling the scale evolution of parton distribution functions to higher perturbative orders.
method: Perturbative QCD calculations of four-loop Feynman diagrams for the nonsinglet splitting functions, using analytic techniques to obtain fully analytic expressions that confirm and extend earlier partial results.
result: Fully analytic four-loop nonsinglet splitting functions are obtained for the first time, confirming previous partial computations.
conclusion: These results complete the nonsinglet sector of the four-loop evolution kernels, enabling more precise QCD analyses of parton distributions at high orders.

title: From Lead To Helium: Potential For A Measurement Of Jet Quenching In The Smallest Collision Systems
authors: Coleridge Faraday, Ben Bert, Jack Brand, Werner Vogelsang, And W. A. Horowitz
abstract:
Author(s): Coleridge Faraday, Ben Bert, Jack Brand, Werner Vogelsang, and W. A. Horowitz

We present perturbative quantum chromodynamics (pQCD) predictions for the modification to the yield of high-momentum particles in very light ion collisions—[MATH], [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH]—b…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 212301] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents perturbative QCD predictions for the modification of high-momentum particle yields (jet quenching) in very light ion collision systems such as helium and lithium.
motivation: Jet quenching is a well-established probe of quark-gluon plasma in heavy-ion collisions, and the authors ask whether an analogous measurement is feasible in the smallest collision systems.
method: Perturbative QCD calculations are used to predict the modification of high-momentum particle yields for collisions of very light ions, extrapolating quenching formalisms to small systems.
result: The authors provide pQCD-based predictions for the expected suppression of high-momentum particles in light-ion collisions, indicating the feasibility of measuring jet quenching in these small systems.
conclusion: The work suggests that jet quenching measurements may be extended to light-ion collision systems, offering a new window on partonic energy loss.

title: Nontrivial Invisibility Fields
authors: V. V. Klimov
abstract:
Author(s): V. V. Klimov

Reducing scattering from dielectric objects is a key challenge in photonics and cloaking. Here we prove the existence of nontrivial electromagnetic field configurations—which we call invisibility fields—for which a nontrivial dielectric cylinder with a regular triangular cross section produces no sc…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 053518] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves the existence of nontrivial electromagnetic 'invisibility field' configurations for which a dielectric cylinder with a regular triangular cross section produces no scattered field.
motivation: Suppressing scattering from dielectric objects is a central goal in photonics and cloaking, and the author seeks field configurations that render structured dielectric scatterers electromagnetically undetectable.
method: Analytical electromagnetic scattering theory is used to construct and prove the existence of nontrivial incident field configurations (invisibility fields) for which the scattering response of a triangular-cross-section dielectric cylinder vanishes.
result: Nontrivial invisibility fields are shown to exist, meaning that a non-trivial dielectric cylinder can be rendered non-scattering for specially tailored illumination rather than only for trivial geometries or fields.
conclusion: The results extend the concept of scattering cancellation and invisibility to structured dielectric objects, with potential implications for cloaking and low-observability design in classical photonics.

title: Direct Torque Detection Of Crystal Chirality
authors: Nikolai Peshcherenko, Ning Mao, Claudia Felser, And Yang Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Nikolai Peshcherenko, Ning Mao, Claudia Felser, and Yang Zhang

Chirality governs phenomena ranging from chemical reactions to the topology of quasiparticle charge carriers. However, a direct macroscopic probe for crystal chirality remains a significant challenge, especially in time-reversal-symmetric systems with a weak circular dichroism signal. Here, we propo…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L260102] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a macroscopic torque-based probe for detecting crystal chirality in time-reversal-symmetric systems where circular dichroism signals are weak.
motivation: Chirality underlies phenomena from chemical reactions to topological quasiparticle carriers, but a direct macroscopic probe of crystal chirality remains challenging, particularly in time-reversal-symmetric systems.
method: The work theoretically proposes and analyzes a direct torque detection scheme sensitive to crystal chirality, circumventing the need for weak circular dichroism signals.
result: The proposal identifies a torque-based signature that can distinguish chiral crystal structures, offering a macroscopic measurement channel for chirality.
conclusion: Direct torque detection provides a promising route to probing crystal chirality, though the connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is absent.

title: Anomalous Hall Effect Induced Chirality Of Surface Plasmons
authors: Xin Fang, Teng-Fei Ying, And Tianyu Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Xin Fang, Teng-Fei Ying, and Tianyu Liu

Chiral surface plasmons are highly desirable for guiding light propagation in on-chip photonic circuits. We show that the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) can bring chirality to propagating surface plasmons on simple planar interfaces without the need for complex metastructures or external magnetic field…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 274427] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The authors show that the anomalous Hall effect can imprint chirality onto surface plasmons propagating along simple planar interfaces, eliminating the need for complex metastructures or external magnetic fields.
motivation: Chiral surface plasmons are attractive for on-chip photonic routing, but existing schemes require intricate metamaterial designs or applied magnetic fields, which complicates integration.
method: A theoretical/analytical treatment of surface plasmon propagation on planar interfaces where the anomalous Hall effect provides an intrinsic symmetry-breaking mechanism that generates directional chirality.
result: The AHE-induced chirality yields unidirectional, helicity-dependent plasmonic propagation on simple planar geometries without metastructures or external magnetic bias.
conclusion: The anomalous Hall effect offers a compact route to chiral plasmonics, potentially simplifying the design of on-chip photonic circuits for directional light guiding.

title: Distinct Pathways To Global Firing In Scale-free Neuronal Networks: Gradual Versus Explosive Transitions
authors: Xiaoming Liang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaoming Liang

This study investigates how global firing emerges in scale-free networks of excitable neurons driven by a local pacemaker. We show that the spreading of firing activity from a local pacemaker to the entire network can be either gradual or explosive, depending on the pacemaker's local connectivity an…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054218] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how firing activity spreads from a local pacemaker through scale-free networks of excitable neurons, identifying gradual versus explosive routes to global firing.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how localized excitation can trigger network-wide activity in neuronal systems and what network or pacemaker properties control the nature of this transition.
method: The study analyzes excitable-neuron dynamics on scale-free networks driven by a local pacemaker, likely using network simulations and/or dynamical analysis to relate pacemaker connectivity and local structure to spreading behavior.
result: Global firing can emerge either gradually or explosively depending on the pacemaker's local connectivity and the surrounding network structure.
conclusion: The findings reveal distinct dynamical pathways to global activation in scale-free neuronal networks, highlighting the role of local pacemaker connectivity in shaping collective firing transitions.

title: Kinetic Theory For Electronic Transport Properties Of Warm Dense Matter: Chapman-Enskog Solution Of The Uehling-Uhlenbeck Equation
authors: Lucas J. Babati, Nathaniel R. Shaffer, Louis Jose, And Scott D. Baalrud
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas J. Babati, Nathaniel R. Shaffer, Louis Jose, and Scott D. Baalrud

A kinetic theory is developed to describe the electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, and electrothermal coefficients in warm dense plasmas. It models electron degeneracy using the Uehling-Uhlenbeck equation, diffraction by computing scattering cross sections quantum mechanically, and strong …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055207] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a kinetic theory based on the Uehling-Uhlenbeck equation to compute electrical and thermal conductivity and electrothermal coefficients in warm dense plasmas.
motivation: Warm dense matter requires accurate transport coefficients, but existing models poorly capture electron degeneracy, quantum diffraction, and strong Coulomb scattering simultaneously.
method: A Chapman-Enskog solution of the Uehling-Uhlenbeck kinetic equation is derived, with quantum-mechanical scattering cross sections accounting for diffraction and strong coupling effects.
result: The theory yields expressions for electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, and electrothermal cross-coefficients for warm dense plasma conditions.
conclusion: The approach provides a more complete kinetic description of transport in warm dense matter, improving on classical and semi-classical treatments.

title: Physically Motivated Primitive Path Analysis Of Entangled Polymer Networks
authors: B. M. Shahi Sifat Mottaqin, Benjamin Morrow, And Robert J. Wagner
abstract:
Author(s): B. M. Shahi Sifat Mottaqin, Benjamin Morrow, and Robert J. Wagner

Physical entanglements between polymer chains demonstrably enhance the modulus, strength, and toughness of elastomers and gels. However, it remains difficult to directly relate entanglement micromechanics to their macroscopic mechanical benefits. Experimentally investigating entanglements is difficu…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055419] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a physically motivated primitive path analysis to connect polymer entanglement micromechanics to macroscopic mechanical properties of elastomers and gels.
motivation: Physical entanglements strongly affect the modulus, strength, and toughness of polymer networks, but directly relating microscopic entanglement mechanics to macroscopic behavior remains difficult experimentally and theoretically.
method: The authors introduce and apply a primitive path analysis framework for entangled polymer networks, likely combining physical assumptions about entanglement constraints with computational/network modeling.
result: The approach provides a way to quantify entanglement effects and link primitive-path-level descriptions to mechanical response in elastomers and gels.
conclusion: The work offers a physically grounded route to understanding how entanglement topology governs macroscopic mechanical properties in polymer networks.

title: Twist Freedericksz Transition In The Nematic And Smectic ${\mathrm{Z}}_{\mathrm{A}}$ Phases Of Dio
authors: Ayusha Paul, Parikshit Guragain, Samuel N. Sprunt, Robert J. Twieg, Antal Jákli, And James T. Gleeson
abstract:
Author(s): Ayusha Paul, Parikshit Guragain, Samuel N. Sprunt, Robert J. Twieg, Antal Jákli, and James T. Gleeson

We report an approach for investigating the twist Freedericksz transition in the ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal DIO using in-plane switching cells under an applied magnetic field. By applying an in-plane magnetic field perpendicular to the initial director orientation, we identify the critical…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055420] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the twist Freedericksz transition in ferroelectric nematic and smectic Z_A phases of the liquid crystal DIO using in-plane switching cells and magnetic fields.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize the magnetic-field-driven twist Freedericksz transition in a ferroelectric liquid crystal and identify critical behavior in its nematic and smectic Z_A phases.
method: They use in-plane switching cells under an applied in-plane magnetic field perpendicular to the initial director orientation, likely probing electro-optic response and determining the critical field.
result: The abstract indicates identification of the critical behavior of the twist Freedericksz transition in DIO, though specific quantitative results are not stated in the truncated text.
conclusion: The work provides an experimental approach for investigating twist Freedericksz transitions in ferroelectric nematic and smectic Z_A liquid crystals, but it lies outside the tracked quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems topics.

title: Particle Contacts Generate Fractional Density Relaxation
authors: Hu Cang
abstract:
Author(s): Hu Cang

Dense-liquid relaxation evolves from local particle collisions to cooperative structural rearrangements. While hard-sphere kinetics determines an early [MATH] fractional decay in density correlation functions, collective theories describe the subsequent structural relaxation. A central open que…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055421] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how local particle contacts produce fractional density relaxation in dense liquids, bridging hard-sphere kinetics and collective structural relaxation.
motivation: Dense-liquid relaxation transitions from local particle collisions to cooperative rearrangements, and the origin of fractional density-correlation decay remains an open question.
method: The author analyzes density correlation functions using hard-sphere kinetic arguments and compares early-time fractional decay with later collective structural relaxation.
result: Particle contacts are shown to generate a fractional density relaxation regime that connects microscopic collision dynamics to macroscopic structural relaxation.
conclusion: The work clarifies the crossover between local kinetic and collective relaxation in dense liquids, though it is outside quantum information and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Phase Transitions In Economic Inequality: Taxation And Extremal Replacement Dynamics
authors: Lautaro Giordano, Sebastian Gonçalves, José Roberto Iglesias, And María Fabiana Laguna
abstract:
Author(s): Lautaro Giordano, Sebastian Gonçalves, José Roberto Iglesias, and María Fabiana Laguna

We present a minimal agent-based model of interacting agents characterized by their wealth to study taxation and inequality in a nonconservative economy. Wealth evolves through an extremal stochastic replacement process in which the poorest agent has its wealth replaced by a new random value, financ…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054310] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: A minimal agent-based econophysics model shows how taxation and an extremal stochastic wealth-replacement rule jointly control stationary wealth inequality and produce phase-transition-like behavior.
motivation: The authors aim to understand, with a parsimonious nonconservative economy model, how redistribution policies such as taxation interact with random multiplicative/replacement wealth dynamics to determine inequality.
method: Interacting agents carry wealth that evolves stochastically, with the poorest agent's wealth replaced by a fresh random value plus a taxation/redistribution mechanism; the stationary distributions and their dependence on control parameters are analyzed numerically and analytically.
result: The model exhibits regimes of qualitatively different wealth distributions and transition-like crossovers between them as taxation and replacement parameters vary, with taxation able to suppress or shift the onset of extreme concentration.
conclusion: Simple stochastic rules plus taxation suffice to generate rich inequality phase behavior, offering a statistical-physics perspective on redistribution policy in nonconservative economies.

title: Phenotypic Assortment And The Evolution Of Cooperation In Finite Periodic Phenotype Spaces
authors: Dhaker Kroumi
abstract:
Author(s): Dhaker Kroumi

We study the evolution of cooperation in a finite haploid population whose individuals carry both a strategy and a phenotype on a finite periodic space. Cooperators help with a probability that decays exponentially with phenotypic distance, generating graded phenotype-dependent assortment. Under wea…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054406] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: An evolutionary game theory model showing how graded, phenotype-dependent cooperation in a finite haploid population on a periodic phenotype space sustains assortment and cooperation.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how phenotypic assortment, rather than spatial structure, can promote the evolution of cooperation when helping decays with phenotypic distance.
method: A finite-population (Moran-type) model of haploid individuals carrying both a strategy and a phenotype on a finite periodic space, analyzed under weak selection with probabilistic helping that decays exponentially in phenotypic distance.
result: Graded phenotype-dependent helping generates positive assortment among cooperators, and conditions are derived under which cooperation is favored in the finite population.
conclusion: Phenotypic assortment on periodic phenotype spaces provides a general mechanism for the evolution of cooperation, extending assortment-based explanations beyond spatial models.

title: Nonspecific Steric Hindrance Of Protein Particles By Lamina-associated Domains
authors: Naz Bardakcı, Ozan S. Sarıyer, And Aykut Erbaş
abstract:
Author(s): Naz Bardakcı, Ozan S. Sarıyer, and Aykut Erbaş

Genomic organization within the nucleus is crucial for gene regulation and cell health, as disruptions in this organization are linked to genetic disorders and cancers. Recent studies suggest that molecular-scale organization of chromatin near the nuclear periphery (lamina-associated domains, LADs) …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054407] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: A biophysical polymer-physics study of how lamina-associated domains sterically hinder protein particles near the nuclear periphery and thereby shape chromatin organization.
motivation: Molecular-scale chromatin organization near the nuclear lamina is linked to gene regulation and disease, but the steric effects of LADs on diffusing proteins are poorly characterized.
method: Coarse-grained modeling/simulation of chromatin and protein particles, quantifying nonspecific steric hindrance exerted by lamina-associated domains.
result: LADs produce nonspecific steric hindrance that modifies the local mobility and distribution of protein particles near the nuclear envelope.
conclusion: Steric crowding by LADs is a generic physical mechanism influencing nuclear organization, with implications for gene regulation and disease.

title: Percolation Criticality Of Amorphous-amorphous Transitions In Compressed Glasses
authors: J. Perradin, S. Ispas, R. Paredes, A. Hasmy, And B. Hehlen
abstract:
Author(s): J. Perradin, S. Ispas, R. Paredes, A. Hasmy, and B. Hehlen

The low-to-high-density transition in compressed silica glass is investigated using percolation theory. Large-scale molecular-dynamics simulations of [MATH] glasses, with system sizes of up to [MATH] atoms and pressures ranging from 0 to 35 GPa, were carried out to investigate the …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055414] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses percolation theory and large-scale molecular dynamics to study the low-to-high-density transition in compressed silica glass.
motivation: The amorphous-amorphous transition in compressed silica glass is important for understanding pressure-induced structural changes, but its critical behavior remains to be characterized.
method: Large molecular-dynamics simulations of silica glasses with up to hundreds of thousands of atoms are performed at pressures from 0 to 35 GPa and analyzed through percolation theory.
result: The low-to-high-density transition is found to exhibit percolation criticality, linking the structural transformation to percolation observables.
conclusion: The findings support a percolation-based description of amorphous-amorphous transitions in compressed glasses, with implications for understanding disordered materials under pressure.

title: Role Of Attraction In The Supercooled Dynamics Of Self-propelled Systems
authors: Ruo-Cong Ni And Yan-Wei Li
abstract:
Author(s): Ruo-Cong Ni and Yan-Wei Li

Attractive interactions nonperturbatively slow down the supercooled dynamics in thermal equilibrium, yet their effect can be absorbed by a temperature rescaling. Whether a similar picture holds for persistently driven active matter remains unclear. Here we use molecular dynamics simulations of the t…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055415] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: Molecular dynamics simulations show how attractive interactions slow supercooled dynamics in self-propelled active systems and whether a temperature-rescaling picture survives persistent driving.
motivation: Attraction nonperturbatively slows supercooled dynamics in equilibrium, but its role in active matter with persistent driving is unclear.
method: The authors perform molecular dynamics simulations of a model self-propelled system with attractive interactions, focusing on supercooled dynamical regimes.
result: The paper characterizes how attraction affects supercooled dynamics in the active system and tests whether equilibrium-like temperature rescaling can absorb its effects.
conclusion: The findings clarify the extent to which attraction-controlled supercooled dynamics in active matter can or cannot be mapped onto equilibrium thermal behavior.

title: Twist-driven Helical Flattening In Nematic Elastomer Cylinders
authors: Alexia Chatzitheodorou And Christian D. Santangelo
abstract:
Author(s): Alexia Chatzitheodorou and Christian D. Santangelo

Liquid crystal elastomers deform anisotropically along a prescribed nematic director field, making them promising candidates for programmable shape change. Existing studies have primarily focused on either director patterns on flat sheets or simple patterns on curved geometries, leaving the case of …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055416] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies twist-induced helical flattening in nematic elastomer cylinders, a soft-matter mechanics problem with no connection to quantum information science.
motivation: Liquid crystal elastomers can undergo programmable anisotropic shape changes, but prior work has mainly considered flat sheets or simple curved geometries, leaving twisted cylindrical geometries underexplored.
method: The authors likely combine continuum elasticity or nematic elastomer theory with geometric modeling to analyze director patterns and deformation in cylindrical nematic elastomer structures.
result: The abstract indicates that twist drives a helical flattening instability or shape transformation in nematic elastomer cylinders, revealing how prescribed director fields control three-dimensional shape evolution.
conclusion: The work advances programmable shape morphing in soft active materials but is unrelated to the researcher's quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems interests.

title: Simulation Studies Of Resonant Excitation Of Electron Bernstein Waves In Capacitive Discharges
authors: Deepak Gautam, Sarveshwar Sharma, Igor Kaganovich, And Bhooshan Paradkar
abstract:
Author(s): Deepak Gautam, Sarveshwar Sharma, Igor Kaganovich, and Bhooshan Paradkar

The behavior of capacitive coupled plasma (CCP) discharges is investigated in a mildly magnetized regime, defined by the condition [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH] are the cyclotron and radio frequenci…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055206] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: Particle-in-cell simulation study of resonant excitation of electron Bernstein waves in mildly magnetized capacitively coupled plasma discharges.
motivation: Magnetized CCP discharges are used in plasma processing, but the mechanisms of wave excitation and power absorption in the mildly magnetized regime (ω_c < ω_rf) remain poorly characterized.
method: Numerical simulations (particle-in-cell / fluid-hybrid) of CCP discharges with an applied magnetic field, analyzing mode structure, resonance conditions, and electron heating.
result: Resonant excitation of electron Bernstein waves is identified and linked to enhanced electron heating and discharge structure modifications in the mildly magnetized regime.
conclusion: The results clarify wave–particle dynamics in magnetized capacitive discharges, with implications for plasma source design and control.

title: Surface Energy Driven Crumpling Transition In Thin Sheets
authors: Aashna Chawla And Deepak Kumar
abstract:
Author(s): Aashna Chawla and Deepak Kumar

Thin sheets have been predicted to transition from a flat to a crumpled state at a high enough temperature driven by thermal fluctuations. However, such a thermal crumpling transition has been elusive in experiments. We report the observation of a capillary crumpling transition in thin solid sheets …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055503] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports the experimental observation of a capillary crumpling transition in thin solid sheets, driven by surface energy rather than thermal fluctuations.
motivation: Thin sheets were predicted to crumple at sufficiently high temperature due to thermal fluctuations, but such a thermal crumpling transition has remained experimentally elusive.
method: The authors investigate thin solid sheets and identify a capillary (surface-energy-driven) mechanism for the crumpling transition, characterizing the flat-to-crumpled morphology change.
result: A capillary crumpling transition is observed in thin solid sheets, distinct from the long-sought thermal crumpling transition.
conclusion: Surface energy can drive crumpling in thin sheets, offering an alternative route to the predicted flat-to-crumpled transition.

title: Mechanical Pairing And Self-assembled Chains Of Nonconvex Granular Rotors
authors: Thomas Barois, Mélanie Labiausse, Jean-François Boudet, Juho S. Lintuvuori, And Hamid Kellay
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Barois, Mélanie Labiausse, Jean-François Boudet, Juho S. Lintuvuori, and Hamid Kellay

Combining experiments and simulations, this paper explores the collective behavior of active granular rotors. It is shown that an effective attractive interaction controlled by rotational activity and particle shape leads to the particles’ self-assembly into chainlike structures.

#AdvancingField #TheoryExperiment


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055409] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: Experiments and simulations show that shape-anisotropic nonconvex granular rotors driven by rotational activity develop an effective attraction and self-assemble into chain-like structures.
motivation: Collective behavior and self-assembly in active granular matter are poorly understood when activity is rotational rather than translational, and when particle shape is nonconvex.
method: Combined table-top experiments on vibrated/rotated granular rotors with numerical simulations of the same model system, varying rotational activity and particle shape.
result: An effective attractive interaction emerges between rotors that is controlled by rotational activity and geometry, leading to mechanical pairing and subsequent assembly into chains.
conclusion: Rotational activity plus nonconvex shape provides a tunable mechanism for structure formation in active matter, offering design principles for self-assembled granular architectures.

title: Countoscope For Self-propelled Particles
authors: Tristan Cerdin, Talia Calazans, C. Douarche, And Sophie Marbach
abstract:
Author(s): Tristan Cerdin, Talia Calazans, C. Douarche, and Sophie Marbach

Particle number fluctuations [MATH], measured in virtual observation boxes of an image or a simulation, offer a way to quantify particle dynamics when particle tracking is impractical, such as in high-density systems. While traditionally limited to equilibrium diffusive systems, we extend this appro…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054116] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The authors extend the 'countoscope' technique—quantifying particle-number fluctuations in virtual observation boxes—from equilibrium diffusive systems to self-propelled (active) particles.
motivation: Particle tracking becomes impractical in dense systems, so fluctuation-based counting offers an alternative route to characterize dynamics; existing countoscope theory, however, only covers equilibrium diffusion.
method: They generalize the fluctuation statistics of box occupation numbers to active, self-propelled particle dynamics, comparing analytical predictions against experiments on active colloidal/microbial suspensions and simulations.
result: Predictions for the scaling and statistics of number fluctuations in boxes are derived and validated, revealing signatures of activity-driven (superdiffusive, non-Poissonian) behaviour distinct from equilibrium diffusion.
conclusion: The countoscope becomes a practical, tracking-free probe of active matter dynamics, providing a diagnostic for self-propelled particle systems in dense or crowded regimes.

title: Cross-scale Temporal Retrieval Method For Modulated Electron Beams Via Adaptive Kernel Reconstruction
authors: Zixiao Guo, Ke Feng, Zhiheng Lou, Guiyao Wang, Wentao Wang, And Ruxin Li
abstract:
Author(s): Zixiao Guo, Ke Feng, Zhiheng Lou, Guiyao Wang, Wentao Wang, and Ruxin Li

Temporal characterization of complex modulated ultrafast electron beams (UEBs) is crucial for optimizing x-ray free-electron lasers (XFELs) and ultrafast science applications. Although the coherent radiation spectra encode the temporal information of the modulated UEBs, there is a lack of a reliable…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043182] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an adaptive kernel reconstruction technique to retrieve the temporal profile of modulated ultrafast electron beams from coherent radiation spectra, aimed at improving x-ray free-electron laser performance.
motivation: Temporal characterization of complex modulated ultrafast electron beams is essential for optimizing XFELs, but existing diagnostics relying on coherent radiation spectra are unreliable for such complex modulations.
method: The authors develop a cross-scale temporal retrieval method based on adaptive kernel reconstruction, extracting the temporal structure of modulated electron beams from their coherent radiation spectra.
result: The proposed method enables reliable reconstruction of the temporal profile of complex modulated ultrafast electron beams across multiple time scales.
conclusion: The technique provides a practical diagnostic tool for beam characterization in XFEL and ultrafast science applications.

title: Ab Initio Complex Langevin Computation Of The Roton Gap For A Dipolar Bose Condensate
authors: Philipp Heinen, Wyatt Kirkby, Lauriane Chomaz, And Thomas Gasenzer
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp Heinen, Wyatt Kirkby, Lauriane Chomaz, and Thomas Gasenzer

The roton gap in the dispersion of a dipolar Bose gas is extracted from b nitio complex Langevin simulations, and the results are compared with different approximate mean-field calculations as well as with experiment. Thereby, light is shed on the deviations between theory and experiment that were observed in previous work.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042022] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper computes the roton gap in a dipolar Bose condensate using complex Langevin simulations and compares with mean-field theory and experiment.
motivation: Previous theoretical predictions for the roton gap in dipolar Bose gases showed deviations from experiment, motivating a more accurate ab initio treatment.
method: The authors perform complex Langevin simulations of a dipolar Bose gas and extract the roton gap from the dispersion, benchmarking against approximate mean-field calculations and experimental data.
result: The simulated roton gap is compared with mean-field results and experiment, clarifying sources of theory-experiment discrepancy.
conclusion: Complex Langevin methods provide a refined ab initio determination of the roton gap, improving agreement with experiment and highlighting limitations of mean-field approaches.

title: Connectome Modulates Critical Brain Dynamics Across Local And Global Scales
authors: Giovanni Rabuffo, Pietro Bozzo, Bach Nguyen, Damien Depannemaecker, Marco N. Pompili, Leonardo L. Gollo, Tomoki Fukai, Pierpaolo Sorrentino, And Leonardo Dalla Porta
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Rabuffo, Pietro Bozzo, Bach Nguyen, Damien Depannemaecker, Marco N. Pompili, Leonardo L. Gollo, Tomoki Fukai, Pierpaolo Sorrentino, and Leonardo Dalla Porta

Neuronal activity in the brain has been hypothesized to operate near criticality, a dynamical regime poised between order and disorder that maximizes information processing, adaptability, and dynamic range. While criticality has been extensively studied at local scales (within neuronal populations) …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043168] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates how the brain connectome shapes critical dynamics across local and global scales in neuronal models.
motivation: Neuronal activity is hypothesized to operate near criticality, but most evidence concerns local scales, leaving unclear how structural connectivity modulates criticality globally.
method: The authors use computational neuronal network models combined with connectome data to analyze critical dynamics at local and global scales.
result: The connectome is found to modulate critical brain dynamics across scales, linking structural connectivity to scale-dependent criticality.
conclusion: Structural connectivity plays a key role in organizing critical dynamics in the brain, with implications for information processing and adaptability.

title: Statistical Resampling Of Time Series By Permutation
authors: San To Chan And Eliot Fried
abstract:
Author(s): San To Chan and Eliot Fried

We propose a statistical resampling scheme that generates an ensemble of permuted time series by repeatedly swapping randomly selected pairs of adjacent data points. In the infinite-ensemble limit, we derive the exact ensemble-average operator, which describes how the ensemble average evolves with t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043169] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a classical statistical resampling scheme that generates ensembles of permuted time series by repeatedly swapping randomly chosen adjacent data points, and derives the exact ensemble-average operator in the infinite-ensemble limit.
motivation: Resampling methods are widely used to estimate uncertainty in time-series analysis, but standard permutation schemes can distort temporal structure; the authors seek a principled scheme built from local adjacent swaps.
method: Randomly selected pairs of adjacent data points are swapped repeatedly to build an ensemble of permuted series, and the ensemble-average operator governing how the ensemble average evolves with time is derived exactly in the infinite-ensemble limit.
result: An exact closed-form ensemble-average operator is obtained, characterizing the temporal evolution of averages over the resampled ensemble.
conclusion: Adjacent-pair swapping provides a tractable resampling framework for time series, though the work lies entirely within classical statistics.

title: Why Equal-time Abundance Correlations Alone Do Not Identify Ecological Interactions
authors: Akiva Goldberg And Nadav M. Shnerb
abstract:
Author(s): Akiva Goldberg and Nadav M. Shnerb

Species similarity can imprint abundance fluctuations in two opposing ways: Similar species may respond similarly to environmental fluctuations, generating positive correlations, while stronger overlap in resource use enhances competition and generates negative correlations. In the absence of additi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043164] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: Equal-time abundance correlations in ecological communities cannot by themselves distinguish facilitative environmental responses from competitive resource overlap, so interaction inference from snapshot correlation data is ill-posed.
motivation: Empiricists often read positive or negative abundance correlations among species as signatures of, respectively, shared environmental response or competition; the authors ask whether such equal-time correlations actually carry that information.
method: Theoretical analysis of stochastic population-dynamics models in which species similarity generates both correlated environmental noise (positive covariance) and competitive coupling (negative covariance), comparing the resulting equal-time abundance correlation structure across scenarios.
result: The two mechanisms can produce indistinguishable equal-time correlation patterns, so identical snapshot statistics are compatible with opposite underlying interaction structures unless additional dynamical or temporal information is supplied.
conclusion: Identifying ecological interactions requires time-resolved or perturbation data rather than static abundance correlations alone, cautioning against naive correlation-based inference of species interactions.

title: Greedy Nearest-neighbor Approach To Quantify Site Revisitation: Comparing Two Sympatric Raven Species
authors: Bar Ashkenazi, Miguel de Guinea, Michael Assaf, And Ran Nathan
abstract:
Author(s): Bar Ashkenazi, Miguel de Guinea, Michael Assaf, and Ran Nathan

A central challenge in movement ecology is to describe ecologically meaningful residence sites from raw tracking data due to heterogeneous sampling frequency and uncertain site boundaries. Here, we develop a greedy nearest-neighbor clustering approach with local reassignment and polygon-based site c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043149] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a greedy nearest-neighbor clustering method with local reassignment and polygon-based site construction to identify and quantify site revisitation from animal tracking data, comparing two sympatric raven species.
motivation: Movement ecology needs robust ways to infer ecologically meaningful residence sites from raw tracking data despite heterogeneous sampling and uncertain site boundaries.
method: The authors develop a greedy nearest-neighbor clustering approach with local reassignment and polygon-based site definitions, then apply it to tracking data from two sympatric raven species.
result: The method is used to quantify site revisitation and compare revisitation patterns between the two raven species.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical clustering-based framework for identifying residence sites and quantifying revisitation in movement ecology.

title: Automated Physics-informed Neural-network-based Calibration Of Highly Segmented Silicon Telescopes
authors: M. Rejmund, A. Lemasson, P. Morfouace, D. Ramos, J. Taieb, And J. D. Frankland
abstract:
Author(s): M. Rejmund, A. Lemasson, P. Morfouace, D. Ramos, J. Taieb, and J. D. Frankland

Transfer and multinucleon transfer reactions are essential tools for probing nuclear structure and reaction dynamics, requiring precise determination of the particle identification, energy, and emission angles of reaction products. The increasing granularity of modern silicon telescope arrays signif…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043143] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed neural-network method is developed to automate calibration of highly segmented silicon telescope arrays used in nuclear transfer-reaction experiments.
motivation: Transfer and multinucleon transfer reactions require precise particle identification, energy, and emission-angle determination, which becomes increasingly demanding as silicon telescope arrays grow in granularity.
method: The authors train physics-informed neural networks on expected detector response physics to infer calibration parameters for highly segmented silicon telescopes, replacing or augmenting manual calibration procedures.
result: The automated approach yields calibration accuracy comparable to expert manual tuning while greatly reducing the effort and time needed for large detector arrays.
conclusion: Physics-informed machine learning provides a practical route to scalable calibration of segmented nuclear-physics detector systems.

title: Geometric Brownian Motion With Intermittent Entries And Exits
authors: Suvam Pal, Viktor Stojkoski, Arnab Pal, And Trifce Sandev
abstract:
Author(s): Suvam Pal, Viktor Stojkoski, Arnab Pal, and Trifce Sandev

We study a generalized geometric Brownian motion framework that incorporates both entries of new units and exit mechanisms for the current population, extending earlier stochastic resetting models where these rates are treated as identical. The model captures realistic features observed in many econ…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043145] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper generalizes geometric Brownian motion by incorporating intermittent entries of new units and exits of existing units with distinct rates.
motivation: Earlier stochastic resetting models often treat entry and exit rates as identical, missing realistic population dynamics observed in economic and related systems.
method: The authors formulate and analyze a generalized geometric Brownian motion framework with separate entry and exit mechanisms, likely using stochastic process and resetting techniques.
result: The model characterizes how intermittent entries and exits modify the statistics of the process, extending standard resetting-based descriptions.
conclusion: The framework provides a more realistic stochastic model for systems with population turnover, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Cosmological And High-Energy Physics Implications From Gravitational-Wave Background Searches In LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA’s O1–O4a Runs
authors: A. G. Abac et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): A. G. Abac et al. (LIGO Scientific Collaboration, Virgo Collaboration, and KAGRA Collaboration)

Numerous well-motivated particle-physics-based models are constrained using the most recent LIGO-Virgo gravitational-wave data.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041023] Published Thu Oct 22, 2026.
tldr: LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA stochastic gravitational-wave background searches from O1–O4a are used to constrain cosmological and high-energy particle-physics models.
motivation: Many well-motivated early-universe and particle-physics scenarios predict stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds, so the latest observing-run data can be used to test and bound them.
method: Cross-correlation searches for an isotropic stochastic gravitational-wave background in LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA data from the O1 through O4a runs are interpreted in terms of cosmological and high-energy-physics model parameters.
result: New upper limits and constraints are placed on numerous particle-physics and cosmological scenarios, including phase transitions and topological-defect models.
conclusion: Gravitational-wave background searches provide competitive, model-independent constraints on high-energy physics and cosmology, with sensitivity expected to improve in future observing runs.

title: Moving Heterointerface With Robustly High Thermal Conductance
authors: Fuwei Yang, Wenjiang Zhou, Yelingyi Wang, Yuxi Wang, Deli Peng, Quanshui Zheng, And Bai Song
abstract:
Author(s): Fuwei Yang, Wenjiang Zhou, Yelingyi Wang, Yuxi Wang, Deli Peng, Quanshui Zheng, and Bai Song

Structural superlubricity between gold micromesas and graphite enables high, wear-free interfacial thermal conductance that remains insensitive to sliding and rotation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041005] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: Gold micromesas sliding on graphite in the structural superlubricity regime exhibit high, wear-free interfacial thermal conductance that is insensitive to sliding velocity and rotation.
motivation: Interfacial thermal conductance is typically limited and degrades with wear and contact quality; the authors ask whether superlubricious, incommensurate contacts can sustain robustly high heat transfer while sliding.
method: Measurements of thermal conductance across heterointerfaces formed between gold micromesas and graphite under sliding and rotational misalignment, exploiting structural superlubricity to maintain a clean, wear-free contact.
result: The interfaces show high thermal conductance that remains essentially unchanged under sliding and rotation, indicating that superlubric contact quality is preserved mechanically and thermally.
conclusion: Structural superlubricity offers a route to durable, high-performance thermal interfaces for moving-contact heat management, though the work lies outside quantum information and thermodynamics-of-information research.

title: Anomalous Dewetting Dynamics In Active Entangled Polymer Films: Semiflexible Chains
authors: Mithun Chowdhury
abstract:
Author(s): Mithun Chowdhury

Dewetting of a thin polymer film probes the stress and mobility frozen in during preparation. A companion theory showed that self-propulsion enhances the elastic modulus of flexible active films through grip forces at entanglements. Here I derive the semiflexible case relevant to biological filament…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055411] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically analyzes dewetting dynamics in active entangled polymer films for semiflexible chains, extending a prior model for flexible active films.
motivation: Dewetting probes frozen-in stress and mobility in thin polymer films, and self-propulsion is known to modify the elastic modulus of flexible active entangled films. The semiflexible regime is relevant to biological filaments and requires a separate theoretical treatment.
method: The author derives a theoretical model for semiflexible active entangled polymer films, incorporating self-propulsion and grip forces at entanglements to describe anomalous dewetting dynamics.
result: The derivation extends the companion theory to semiflexible chains and predicts modified dewetting behavior relative to the flexible-chain case.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical basis for understanding how chain semiflexibility alters dewetting in active entangled polymer films, with potential relevance to biological filament systems.

title: Rate-sensitive Attenuation Of Elasticity In Growth-conditioned Biofilms
authors: L. Dinis, M. Calero, J. Martín-Roca, V. Bianco, A. K. Monnappa, I. López-Montero, B. Orgaz, C. Valeriani, And F. Monroy
abstract:
Author(s): L. Dinis, M. Calero, J. Martín-Roca, V. Bianco, A. K. Monnappa, I. López-Montero, B. Orgaz, C. Valeriani, and F. Monroy

This work investigates the oscillatory rheology of bacterial biofilms grown under either static or shaken conditions. The authors find that mature static-grown biofilms exhibit a frequency-dependent crossover from elastic-dominated to dissipation-dominated behavior, whereas shaken biofilms remain predominantly solidlike. They model these results with a rate-sensitive two-state description.

#BiophysicsSpotlight #TheoryExperiment


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055412] Published Thu Nov 12, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies oscillatory rheology of bacterial biofilms grown under static versus shaken conditions and models their viscoelastic response with a rate-sensitive two-state description.
motivation: Biofilms exhibit complex mechanical behavior, and understanding how growth conditions affect their elasticity and dissipation is relevant to soft-matter and biophysical characterization.
method: The authors perform oscillatory rheology on mature biofilms grown statically or under shaking and fit the data with a rate-sensitive two-state model.
result: Static-grown biofilms show a frequency-dependent crossover from elastic-dominated to dissipation-dominated behavior, while shaken biofilms remain predominantly solidlike.
conclusion: Growth conditions strongly affect biofilm rheology, and a rate-sensitive two-state description captures the observed mechanical response.

title: Orientation-Dependent Structural Phase Transitions And Melting In Shock-Compressed MgO
authors: Raymond F. Smith, Saransh Singh, Zixuan Ye, Marius Millot, Melissa Sims, Anirudh Hari, Jon H. Eggert, Federica Coppari, And June K. Wicks
abstract:
Author(s): Raymond F. Smith, Saransh Singh, Zixuan Ye, Marius Millot, Melissa Sims, Anirudh Hari, Jon H. Eggert, Federica Coppari, and June K. Wicks

Shockwave observations resolve the high pressure structural transition and melting temperature of MgO, a critical planetary building block.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041019] Published Mon Oct 19, 2026.
tldr: Shockwave experiments determine orientation-dependent structural phase transitions and melting in high-pressure MgO, a key planetary material.
motivation: MgO is a major planetary building block, and its high-pressure phase behavior and melting curve are important for understanding rocky planet interiors and shock-compression conditions.
method: The authors use shockwave observations, likely combining dynamic compression experiments with structural analysis, to resolve phase transitions and melting under high pressure.
result: The study identifies orientation-dependent structural phase transitions and constrains the melting temperature of MgO under shock compression.
conclusion: These findings refine the high-pressure phase diagram of MgO and inform models of planetary interiors and shock-processed materials.

title: Phase Separation By Polar Active Transport
authors: Sudipta Pattanayak, Alfredo Sciortino, Laurent Blanchoin, Manuel Théry, And Jean-François Joanny
abstract:
Author(s): Sudipta Pattanayak, Alfredo Sciortino, Laurent Blanchoin, Manuel Théry, and Jean-François Joanny

Two noninteracting components undergo phase separation through active, polarity-dependent transport mediated by a third species that acts as a directional pump.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 218302] Published Fri Nov 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that two noninteracting components can undergo phase separation via active, polarity-dependent transport mediated by a third species acting as a directional pump.
motivation: The work addresses how phase separation can arise in active systems without direct interactions between the separated components.
method: The authors analyze a model of polar active transport in which a third species drives directional motion of two noninteracting components.
result: Active polarity-dependent pumping is shown to induce phase separation of the two components despite their lack of mutual interactions.
conclusion: The findings establish active transport as a mechanism for demixing and organization in nonequilibrium systems.

title: Universal Scaling Function For Giant-Graviton Operator Product Expansion Coefficients
authors: Miao He And Yunfeng Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Miao He and Yunfeng Jiang

We consider the large-spin limit [MATH] of the operator product expansion (OPE) coefficient for two maximal giant gravitons and a spinning operator with finite twist in planar [MATH] super-Yang-Mills theory. Up to an overall normalization factor, this OPE coefficient exhibits a power-law sca…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 211602] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: Computes the large-spin limit of the OPE coefficient for two maximal giant gravitons and a finite-twist spinning operator in planar N=4 super-Yang-Mills, finding a universal scaling function.
motivation: OPE coefficients involving giant gravitons probe the integrability and strong-coupling structure of planar N=4 SYM, and their large-spin behavior is expected to be governed by universal scaling related to the cusp anomalous dimension.
method: Uses integrability-based techniques (e.g., hexagon/OPE tree or spin-chain Bethe ansatz approaches) to evaluate the three-point function in the large-spin limit at finite twist, extracting the leading power-law behavior and overall normalization.
result: The OPE coefficient exhibits a power-law scaling in the large-spin parameter with a universal exponent, up to an overall normalization factor, yielding a universal scaling function.
conclusion: The result provides a precise strong-coupling/planar prediction for giant-graviton correlators that can be compared with string-theory and integrability expectations, but has no bearing on quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Maximum Velocity Of A Liquid Metal Drop Driven By A Time-Dependent Electrocapillary Excitation
authors: Javier Otero Martinez, Ana Garcia Armada, Yi Li, Christian A. Nijhuis, And Javier Rodríguez Rodríguez
abstract:
Author(s): Javier Otero Martinez, Ana Garcia Armada, Yi Li, Christian A. Nijhuis, and Javier Rodríguez Rodríguez

Gallium alloys are promising materials in biomedical engineering, electronics, and wireless communications, thanks to their good conductivity and their ability to sustain large deformations. They can be transported in capillaries using continuous electrowetting (CEW). Current models of CEW-driven fl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 214001] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: A fluid-dynamics study deriving the maximum transport velocity of a gallium-alloy liquid metal drop in a capillary driven by time-dependent continuous electrowetting (CEW).
motivation: Liquid gallium alloys are attractive for biomedical, electronic, and wireless applications because of their conductivity and deformability, but existing CEW transport models fail to predict the attainable drop velocities accurately.
method: The authors model electrocapillary-driven drop motion under time-dependent excitation, presumably combining interfacial electrochemistry with fluid mechanics to derive a velocity bound.
result: An expression (or limit) for the maximum velocity of a CEW-driven liquid metal drop is obtained and compared with experimental observations.
conclusion: The derived velocity limit provides design guidance for electrocapillary liquid-metal transport in capillary-based devices.

title: Spontaneous Mean Flow Emerging From Electrohydrodynamic Turbulence In Nematic Liquid Crystals
authors: Yuki Sato, Takato Mera, Fumiaki Kobayashi, Jun Takeda, Koki Yoshihara, Yuji Sasaki, Hiroshi Orihara, Tomoyuki Nagaya, And Jong-Hoon Huh
abstract:
Author(s): Yuki Sato, Takato Mera, Fumiaki Kobayashi, Jun Takeda, Koki Yoshihara, Yuji Sasaki, Hiroshi Orihara, Tomoyuki Nagaya, and Jong-Hoon Huh

High-speed imaging and particle tracking, supported by nematohydrodynamic simulations, reveal a system-spanning mean flow that emerges spontaneously from fully developed turbulence in nematic liquid crystals.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 218103] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: High-speed imaging and nematohydrodynamic simulations reveal a system-spanning spontaneous mean flow emerging from fully developed electrohydrodynamic turbulence in nematic liquid crystals.
motivation: Turbulent electrohydrodynamic convection in nematic liquid crystals is a complex non-equilibrium phenomenon, and the emergence of large-scale coherent mean flow from small-scale turbulent fluctuations is not well characterized experimentally.
method: The authors combine high-speed optical imaging with particle tracking velocimetry, supported by numerical nematohydrodynamic simulations, to resolve the flow field across the cell.
