result: A system-spanning mean flow is observed to arise spontaneously out of fully developed turbulence, and simulations reproduce the emergent coherent structure.
conclusion: The work identifies a classical condensation-like mechanism whereby turbulent fluctuations organize into a macroscopic mean flow in an anisotropic fluid.

title: Two-Fluid Effects In Z-Pinch Ablation Characterized By Unified Bayesian Inversion
authors: Bowen Zhu, Jian Wu, Wei Wang, Yuanbo Lu, Zhiyuan Jiang, Zhiyin Deng, Delong Xiao, Zhigang Liu, Huantong Shi, Xingwen Li, Hao Wang, And Aici Qiu
abstract:
Author(s): Bowen Zhu, Jian Wu, Wei Wang, Yuanbo Lu, Zhiyuan Jiang, Zhiyin Deng, Delong Xiao, Zhigang Liu, Huantong Shi, Xingwen Li, Hao Wang, and Aici Qiu

In wire-array Z pinches, plasma ablation shapes the conditions for the subsequent implosion. Resolving separate ion and electron motion in these dense, magnetized flows remains an experimental challenge. Here, we report the first direct, spatially resolved measurements of radial ([MATH]) and azim…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 215102] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports the first spatially resolved measurements of radial and azimuthal ion/electron motion in wire-array Z-pinch ablation flows, obtained via a unified Bayesian inversion framework.
motivation: Plasma ablation in wire-array Z pinches sets the initial conditions for implosion, but separately resolving ion and electron dynamics in dense, magnetized flows has remained experimentally inaccessible.
method: The authors apply a unified Bayesian inversion to spectroscopic and imaging diagnostics of Z-pinch ablation, extracting spatially resolved radial and azimuthal velocity components for ions and electrons.
result: Two-fluid effects are directly characterized, revealing distinct ion and electron flow structures in the ablating plasma that had not previously been measured.
conclusion: The measurements provide new constraints on two-fluid ablation models and should improve predictive modeling of Z-pinch implosion dynamics.

title: Control Of The Bootstrap Current In Approximately Quasi-axisymmetric Magnetic Fields
authors: J. L. Velasco, I. Calvo, And J. M. García-Regaña
abstract:
Author(s): J. L. Velasco, I. Calvo, and J. M. García-Regaña

Quasi-axisymmetric stellarators are the stellarator analog of axisymmetric tokamaks, retaining many of their favorable confinement properties, their compactness, and their relative coil simplicity, while avoiding their principal limitation, the need for an inductively driven plasma current. Despite …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055208] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes how the bootstrap current can be controlled in approximately quasi-axisymmetric stellarator magnetic fields using neoclassical transport modeling.
motivation: Quasi-axisymmetric stellarators aim to combine tokamak-like confinement with the absence of a required inductive plasma current, but residual bootstrap currents can still arise and degrade the intended configuration.
method: Neoclassical transport calculations (likely drift-kinetic/Reaktor-type modeling) are used to evaluate bootstrap current contributions across magnetic field configurations and to identify knobs for controlling its magnitude and profile.
result: The authors quantify how deviations from exact quasi-axisymmetry and the choice of field parameters influence the bootstrap current, identifying configurations where it is substantially reduced or controlled.
conclusion: Control of the bootstrap current in quasi-axisymmetric stellarators is feasible through careful magnetic field design, supporting their viability as steady-state fusion devices.

title: Diffusive-scaling Lax-Wendroff Lattice Boltzmann Method On Nonuniform Grids: Theory, Stability, And Validation
authors: Irwan Ary Dharmawan
abstract:
Author(s): Irwan Ary Dharmawan

We analyze the diffusive-scaling asymptotics of the two-dimensional D2Q9 lattice Boltzmann scheme with a Bhatnagar–Gross–Krook (BGK) collision step and a Lax–Wendroff transport step on separable nonuniform grids, obtained from a uniform computational grid by two independent one-dimensional diffeomor…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055302] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops and analyzes a diffusive-scaling Lax-Wendroff lattice Boltzmann method on separable nonuniform grids, providing stability theory and numerical validation.
motivation: Nonuniform grids are needed to resolve multiscale flow features efficiently, but the stability and asymptotic behavior of Lax-Wendroff-type lattice Boltzmann schemes on such grids are not well understood.
method: The authors formulate a D2Q9 BGK lattice Boltzmann scheme with a Lax-Wendroff transport step on grids generated by independent 1D diffeomorphisms, and perform a diffusive-scaling asymptotic analysis plus linear stability analysis, validated by numerical tests.
result: The analysis yields conditions for stability and consistency of the scheme in the diffusive scaling limit on nonuniform grids, confirmed by numerical experiments.
conclusion: The proposed nonuniform-grid Lax-Wendroff lattice Boltzmann method is stable and accurate under the derived conditions, making it viable for simulations on stretched or graded meshes.

title: Reversible Linear Polymerization And Liquid-liquid Phase Separation: An Exact Field Representation, Restricted Uniform Mean-field And Fluctuation Analysis
authors: Ilia A. Baliakin, Xiaojun Han, Leonid D. Son, Roman E. Ryltsev, And Andrey A. Rempel
abstract:
Author(s): Ilia A. Baliakin, Xiaojun Han, Leonid D. Son, Roman E. Ryltsev, and Andrey A. Rempel

Liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) in associating systems is commonly attributed either to nonspecific attractions or to network formation induced by multivalent bonding. Here we derive an exact finite-grid field representation for a minimal model of bifunctional monomers undergoing reversible as…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055413] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an exact finite-grid field representation and mean-field fluctuation analysis for reversible linear polymerization coupled to liquid-liquid phase separation in associating monomer systems.
motivation: Liquid-liquid phase separation in associating systems is often explained either by nonspecific attractions or by multivalent bonding-induced network formation, motivating a unified minimal model for reversible polymerization and phase separation.
method: The authors derive an exact finite-grid field representation for bifunctional monomers undergoing reversible linear polymerization, then analyze it using a restricted uniform mean-field approach and fluctuation corrections.
result: The exact field representation provides a controlled framework for the coupled polymerization/phase-separation problem, while the mean-field and fluctuation analysis characterize how reversible bonding affects LLPS behavior.
conclusion: The work offers a statistical-physics treatment of reversible polymerization-driven phase separation, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Resonantly Driven Electron Bernstein Waves In Magnetized Low-pressure Capacitive Discharges
authors: Deepak Gautam, Sarveshwar Sharma, Igor Kaganovich, And Bhooshan Paradkar
abstract:
Author(s): Deepak Gautam, Sarveshwar Sharma, Igor Kaganovich, and Bhooshan Paradkar

The physics of capacitively coupled plasma (CCP) discharges is investigated in a mildly magnetized regime, defined by [MATH], where [MATH] and [MATH] denote the electron cyclotron frequency and the applied radio frequency, respectively. A disti…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L053202] Published Fri Nov 13, 2026.
tldr: A plasma-physics study of resonantly driven electron Bernstein waves in mildly magnetized low-pressure capacitively coupled radio-frequency discharges.
motivation: Capacitively coupled plasma discharges under weak magnetization are important for industrial plasma processing, but the wave physics in the regime where the electron cyclotron frequency is comparable to the driving frequency is poorly characterized.
method: The authors analyze CCP discharge physics in the mildly magnetized regime using theoretical wave dispersion analysis and presumably particle-in-cell or kinetic simulations, identifying resonant excitation of electron Bernstein waves.
result: Distinct resonant behavior of electron Bernstein waves is found in the mildly magnetized regime, with the wave dynamics shaping discharge structure and electron heating.
conclusion: The work clarifies wave-heating physics in magnetized CCP discharges, relevant to plasma source design rather than to quantum information science.

title: Spontaneous Bending Of Cylindrical Hydrogels
authors: Javier Rojo-González, Adrián Arenas-Gullo, And Alberto Fernandez-Nieves
abstract:
Author(s): Javier Rojo-González, Adrián Arenas-Gullo, and Alberto Fernandez-Nieves

Among thermoresponsive hydrogels, poly-N-isopropylacrylamide gels are well known for their marked deswelling behavior near [MATH]; under slow, quasistatic heating, the gel shrinks affinely. In contrast, a rapid temperature quench above [MATH] …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 055410] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies spontaneous bending instabilities that arise in cylindrical poly-N-isopropylacrylamide hydrogels when they are rapidly quenched through the volume phase transition instead of being heated quasistatically.
motivation: Thermoresponsive hydrogels such as PNIPAM shrink affinely under slow heating, but fast temperature quenches produce non-uniform deswelling and mechanical instabilities whose origin and morphology are not fully understood.
method: Cylindrical PNIPAM gel samples are subjected to rapid temperature quenches above the transition temperature, and the resulting shape evolution and bending behavior are characterized experimentally and interpreted with elasticity/deswelling arguments.
result: Rapid quenching produces inhomogeneous shrinkage across the gel that generates internal stresses, driving the cylinders to bend spontaneously rather than shrink affinely.
conclusion: The work clarifies how quenching rate controls the mechanical response of thermoresponsive hydrogels, showing that bending is a generic consequence of fast, non-uniform deswelling.

title: Asymptotics Of Protein Number Distribution In Stochastic Gene Expression Models Under Burst Approximation
authors: Yuntao Lu And Yunxin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yuntao Lu and Yunxin Zhang

The burst approximation is a widely used technique to simplify stochastic gene expression models. However, the dynamics and analytical properties of the protein number distribution in gene expression models under the burst approximation remain largely unexplored. In this study, we propose and system…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043148] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives asymptotic analytical properties of the protein number distribution in stochastic gene expression models under the burst approximation.
motivation: The burst approximation is widely used to simplify stochastic gene expression models, yet the dynamics and analytical structure of the resulting protein distributions are largely unexplored.
method: The authors propose and systematically analyze a stochastic gene expression model in the burst limit, deriving asymptotic expressions for the protein number distribution analytically.
result: Analytical asymptotic forms for the protein number distribution are obtained, characterizing its tail behavior and dependence on model parameters.
conclusion: The results clarify the analytical structure of burst-approximation gene expression models, providing a theoretical basis for interpreting protein abundance distributions.

title: Dual Relaxation Modes Control Polymer Crystallization
authors: Ming Wang, Zijian Song, Alejandro J. Müller, Simone Napolitano, Guoming Liu, And Dujin Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Ming Wang, Zijian Song, Alejandro J. Müller, Simone Napolitano, Guoming Liu, and Dujin Wang

Crystallization in polymers provides a fundamental probe of how molecular relaxation governs the emergence of order in glass-forming systems. Despite the longstanding success of the Lauritzen-Hoffman theory, its empirical treatment of molecular diffusion fails to capture the crystallization kinetics…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 218102] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates how dual relaxation modes govern crystallization kinetics in glass-forming polymers, challenging the empirical diffusion treatment of Lauritzen-Hoffman theory.
motivation: Crystallization in polymers serves as a probe of how molecular relaxation controls ordering in glass-forming systems, but existing theory does not adequately capture the diffusion step.
method: The authors analyze polymer crystallization kinetics in relation to molecular relaxation modes, likely combining calorimetric or dielectric measurements with kinetic modeling.
result: They find that two relaxation modes jointly control crystallization, providing a better description of the kinetics than the standard Lauritzen-Hoffman diffusion treatment.
conclusion: The work clarifies the connection between molecular dynamics and crystallization in polymers and suggests a revised framework for describing order emergence in glass-forming systems.

title: Erratum: Bounds On Screened Dark Energy From Near-Earth Space-Based Measurements [Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 101002 (2026)]
authors: Fabiano Feleppa, Welmoed Marit de Graaf, Philippe Brax, And Gaetano Lambiase
abstract:
Author(s): Fabiano Feleppa, Welmoed Marit de Graaf, Philippe Brax, and Gaetano Lambiase
[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 219901] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting a Physical Review Letters paper that derived bounds on screened dark energy models from near-Earth space-based measurements.
motivation: The original work aimed to constrain screened scalar-tensor/dark energy theories (e.g., chameleon or symmetron models) using precision measurements in the near-Earth space environment.
method: The erratum reports corrections to the original analysis of space-based experimental constraints on screened dark energy parameters.
result: The erratum amends specific numerical results or equations from the published Letter [Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 101002 (2026)].
conclusion: The corrected bounds refine the constraints on screened dark energy models, but the work lies entirely in gravitational/cosmological physics with no bearing on quantum information science.

title: Multiple Propagating Modes In Random Polycrystals
authors: Ming Huang, Stanislav I. Rokhlin, And Michael J. S. Lowe
abstract:
Author(s): Ming Huang, Stanislav I. Rokhlin, and Michael J. S. Lowe

State-of-the-art grain-scale simulations confirm a decades-old theoretical prediction, demonstrating that forward multiple scattering allows multiple coherent wave modes to propagate through single-phase random polycrystals.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 217201] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: Grain-scale simulations confirm that forward multiple scattering in single-phase random polycrystals allows several coherent elastic wave modes to propagate simultaneously.
motivation: A decades-old theoretical prediction that multiple coherent wave modes can coexist in random polycrystals had never been verified at the grain scale.
method: State-of-the-art grain-scale numerical simulations of elastic wave propagation in random polycrystalline microstructures, compared against the existing multiple-scattering theory.
result: The simulations reproduce the predicted multiplicity of propagating coherent modes, validating the forward multiple-scattering picture.
conclusion: Multiple coherent mode propagation is a real, observable feature of random polycrystals, with implications for ultrasonic nondestructive evaluation and material characterization.

title: High-Heating Efficiency And Reproducibility In Double-Cone Ignition Experiments
authors: Xiao Su, Zekun Xu, Yangyi Lei, Meiqiao Wang, Jinglong Li, Yihang Zhang, Zhiwei Wang, Kaitian Ye, Ke Fang, Chenglong Zhang, Zhengdong Liu, Yufeng Dong, Yu Dai, Bofang Jiang, Zude Lin, Fuyuan Wu, Weimin Wang, Xiaohui Yuan, Zhe Zhang, Jingquan Liu, Xuechun Li, Jian Zheng, Yutong Li, Jianqiang Zhu, And Jie Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiao Su, Zekun Xu, Yangyi Lei, Meiqiao Wang, Jinglong Li, Yihang Zhang, Zhiwei Wang, Kaitian Ye, Ke Fang, Chenglong Zhang, Zhengdong Liu, Yufeng Dong, Yu Dai, Bofang Jiang, Zude Lin, Fuyuan Wu, Weimin Wang, Xiaohui Yuan, Zhe Zhang, Jingquan Liu, Xuechun Li, Jian Zheng, Yutong Li, Jianqiang Zhu, and Jie Zhang

We report the first integrated experiments of the double-cone ignition scheme, conducted on the ShenGuang II Upgrade facility using 14 kJ nanosecond laser beams and a 450 J picosecond (ps) laser beam. Two carbon-deuterium shells were imploded by the nanosecond laser beams inside dual compressing con…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 215101] Published Mon Nov 16, 2026.
tldr: The first integrated double-cone ignition experiments on the ShenGuang II Upgrade laser facility demonstrate improved heating efficiency and reproducibility for inertial confinement fusion.
motivation: Double-cone ignition is a proposed laser-fusion scheme that aims to achieve high energy gain, but it had not yet been tested in an integrated experimental setting combining compression and picosecond heating.
method: Two carbon-deuterium shells were imploded by 14 kJ nanosecond laser beams within dual compressing cones, then heated by a 450 J picosecond laser beam, with diagnostics measuring heating efficiency and shot-to-shot reproducibility.
result: The experiments achieved high heating efficiency and reproducible implosion-and-heating performance across shots.
conclusion: The results provide experimental support for the double-cone ignition pathway toward inertial fusion energy, though significant physics and engineering challenges remain.

title: Thermodynamics Of Stacking Faults And Phase Stability In Cobalt-based Alloys
authors: Zheng Zhong, Ziqi Cui, Yu Zhuo, Tianyu Yu, Jianfeng Cai, Kaibo Zou, Jiacheng Shen, Bowen Huang, Zhuoming Xie, Huiqiu Deng, Yang Yu, Hao Zhang, Wangyu Hu, Tengfei Yang, And Jie Hou
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhong, Ziqi Cui, Yu Zhuo, Tianyu Yu, Jianfeng Cai, Kaibo Zou, Jiacheng Shen, Bowen Huang, Zhuoming Xie, Huiqiu Deng, Yang Yu, Hao Zhang, Wangyu Hu, Tengfei Yang, and Jie Hou

Stacking fault energy dictates phase stability and deformation behavior in Co alloys and WC-Co cemented carbides, yet a quantitative assessment of alloying effects at finite temperatures remains poorly established. By integrating first-principles thermodynamics with microstructural characterization,…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 254109] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: First-principles thermodynamics combined with microstructural characterization quantifies how alloying elements affect stacking fault energy and phase stability in Co-based alloys and WC-Co cemented carbides at finite temperature.
motivation: Stacking fault energy governs phase stability and deformation in Co alloys and WC-Co cermets, but a quantitative, temperature-dependent understanding of alloying effects was lacking.
method: The authors combine first-principles (DFT-based) thermodynamic calculations of stacking fault and phase energies with experimental microstructural characterization of alloyed Co and WC-Co samples.
result: Alloying-dependent stacking fault energies and phase stability trends are obtained quantitatively at finite temperatures and cross-validated against measured microstructures.
conclusion: The work provides a predictive thermodynamic framework for tuning composition to control stacking faults and phase stability in Co-based alloys and cemented carbides.

title: Invasion With Size-dependent Dispersion Range
authors: Ulysse Marquis
abstract:
Author(s): Ulysse Marquis

The coalescing colony model provides a minimal framework for biological invasions with long-range dispersion. In its standard formulation, the dispersion range is assumed independent of the size of the invading population. Here, we relax this assumption and consider size-dependent dispersal: a main …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 054408] Published Thu Nov 19, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical ecology paper extending the coalescing colony model of biological invasions to allow dispersal range to depend on the size of the invading population.
motivation: The standard coalescing colony model assumes size-independent dispersal, which is unrealistic for many spreading populations; the author relaxes this assumption to capture size-dependent spreading behavior.
method: Analytical and/or numerical treatment of a modified coalescing colony model in which the main colony emits satellite colonies whose dispersal kernel depends on population size.
result: The size-dependent dispersion modifies the invasion front dynamics and growth laws compared with the constant-dispersal case, yielding altered spreading exponents/velocities.
conclusion: Size-dependent dispersal can qualitatively change invasion dynamics, showing that the standard assumption is not universally valid for spreading populations.

title: Electrohydraulic Fields Generated By Active Transport At Tissue Interfaces
authors: Amit Singh Vishen, Ahandeep Manna, And Frank Jülicher
abstract:
Author(s): Amit Singh Vishen, Ahandeep Manna, and Frank Jülicher

Living cells and tissues can generate complex patterns of electric fields and fluid flows, which can play important role in physiology. Both fields and flows are rooted in ion transport across biological interfaces—cell membranes and epithelial cell layers. Here, we develop a unified electrohydrauli…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043150] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: Develops a unified electrohydraulic theory describing how ion transport across cell membranes and epithelial layers generates coupled electric fields and fluid flows in living tissues.
motivation: Endogenous electric fields and fluid flows in tissues are physiologically important, yet a unified continuum framework linking ion transport at biological interfaces to both fields and flows was lacking.
method: A theoretical/continuum modeling approach deriving coupled electrohydrodynamic equations for ion transport, electric potential, and fluid flow at membrane and epithelial interfaces, with analysis of resulting field and flow patterns.
result: The framework reproduces and unifies the generation of complex electric field and flow patterns from active ion transport across tissue interfaces, characterizing how interfacial transport drives electrohydraulic behavior.
conclusion: Electrohydraulic coupling at biological interfaces provides a general physical mechanism for pattern formation in tissues, with implications for physiology and bioelectric signaling.

title: Mapping The Limits Of Equilibrium In Sheared Granular Liquid Crystals
authors: Jacopo Bilotto, Martin Trulsson, And Jean-François Molinari
abstract:
Author(s): Jacopo Bilotto, Martin Trulsson, and Jean-François Molinari

While elongated particles in viscous fluids follow Jeffery orbits, their dynamics in dense granular flows remain unresolved. We demonstrate that sheared, low-friction granular rods do not follow these orbits, but instead reach a quasiequilibrium state quantitatively described by classical liquid cry…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043151] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026.
tldr: Sheared low-friction granular rods in dense granular flows fail to follow Jeffery orbits and instead settle into a quasiequilibrium state described quantitatively by classical liquid-crystal theory.
motivation: Elongated particles suspended in viscous fluids trace Jeffery orbits, but whether this paradigm holds in dense, dissipative granular flows was unresolved, motivating a systematic study of rod dynamics under shear.
method: The authors perform particle-scale numerical simulations (discrete element-type modelling) of sheared granular rods with low inter-particle friction, characterizing orientational statistics and comparing them with predictions from classical liquid-crystal theory and Jeffery-orbit kinematics.
result: The rods do not follow Jeffery orbits; instead their orientational distribution reaches a quasiequilibrium state that is quantitatively captured by classical liquid-crystal descriptions.
conclusion: The work maps the limits of equilibrium-like descriptions in sheared granular media and shows that a liquid-crystal analogy applies to dense granular rod flows, with implications for modelling of granular and soft matter under shear.

title: Piecewise Omnigenous Magnetohydrodynamic Equilibria As Fusion Reactor Candidates
authors: V. Fernández-Pacheco, J. L. Velasco, E. Sánchez, J. M. García-Regaña, J. A. Alonso, I. Calvo, D. Carralero, And R. Gaur
abstract:
Author(s): V. Fernández-Pacheco, J. L. Velasco, E. Sánchez, J. M. García-Regaña, J. A. Alonso, I. Calvo, D. Carralero, and R. Gaur

A new family of magnetic fields reshapes stellarator design.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041045] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a new family of omnigenous magnetic field configurations ('piecewise omnigenous' equilibria) intended to improve stellarator reactor design.
motivation: Stellarators require magnetic fields that confine particle orbits well; omnigenity is a desirable property that is hard to achieve simultaneously with other engineering and physics constraints, motivating a search for broader classes of viable equilibria.
method: The authors construct and analyze magnetohydrodynamic equilibria with piecewise-omnigenous Boozer-spectrum structure, presumably using numerical equilibrium and neoclassical transport codes to assess confinement quality.
result: A new family of magnetic fields is identified that reshapes stellarator design space, offering configurations with favorable particle-orbit confinement properties.
conclusion: Piecewise omnigenous equilibria expand the set of candidate stellarator configurations for fusion reactors, potentially relaxing design trade-offs.

title: Why Ice Is So Slippery
authors: Sigbjørn Løland Bore, B. N. J. Persson, And Henrik Andersen Sveinsson
abstract:
Author(s): Sigbjørn Løland Bore, B. N. J. Persson, and Henrik Andersen Sveinsson

We simulate nanoscale ice-glass friction from first principles and upscale it by modeling frictional heating. Nanoscale simulations alone overestimate friction and miss its velocity dependence. Frictional heating warms the contact toward the melting point, thickening the premelting film tenfold and …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 216201] Published Wed Nov 18, 2026.
tldr: Nanoscale simulations of ice-glass friction, upscaled via a frictional-heating model, explain why ice is slippery through thickening of the premelting film.
motivation: Nanoscale simulations alone overestimate friction and fail to reproduce its velocity dependence, so a multiscale description of ice friction is needed.
method: First-principles nanoscale simulations of ice-glass contacts are combined with a model of frictional heating to upscale the results to macroscopic sliding.
result: Frictional heating warms the contact toward the melting point, thickening the premelting film roughly tenfold and reducing friction in a velocity-dependent way.
conclusion: The slipperiness of ice arises from a feedback between frictional heating and premelting-film growth, reconciling nanoscale simulation with macroscopic observations.

title: Granular Mass Perturbations On The Pulsar-Supermassive Black Hole System
authors: Zexin Hu And Lijing Shao
abstract:
Author(s): Zexin Hu and Lijing Shao

The uncertain mass distribution of stars and compact objects in the galactic center significantly alter the timing uncertainty of the observed pulses from the pulsar orbiting the supermassive black hole at the center of our galaxy.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 211401] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes how granular mass perturbations in the Galactic Center affect pulsar timing for a pulsar orbiting the supermassive black hole.
motivation: The uncertain distribution of stars and compact objects near the Galactic Center introduces timing noise that can limit tests of gravity and black-hole physics using pulsar timing.
method: The authors model stochastic mass perturbations from granular structures and quantify their impact on the observed pulse timing residuals for a pulsar-SMBH system.
result: They find that granular mass distributions can significantly alter pulsar timing uncertainty, with implications for precise timing and parameter estimation.
conclusion: Accurate modeling of Galactic Center mass perturbations is necessary for robust pulsar-based tests of gravity and supermassive black hole properties.

title: Transformation-Induced Plasticity In Metals Activated By Shape-Memory Ceramics
authors: Wangshu Zheng, Xuyang Feng, Lei Zhao, Linghai Li, Ying Hu, Shulin Liu, Runxia Li, Wen Yin, Upadrasta Ramamurty, Zhili Dong, Chee Lip Gan, Di Zhang, And Qiang Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Wangshu Zheng, Xuyang Feng, Lei Zhao, Linghai Li, Ying Hu, Shulin Liu, Runxia Li, Wen Yin, Upadrasta Ramamurty, Zhili Dong, Chee Lip Gan, Di Zhang, and Qiang Guo

Secondary-phase fillers usually strengthen metals at the expense of plasticity and functionality. Here, we show that embedding stimulus-responsive, shape-memory ceramics into a metal activates a transformation-induced plasticity response through a distinct constraint-relief mechanism. During process…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 216101] Published Tue Nov 17, 2026.
tldr: Embedding stimulus-responsive shape-memory ceramics in metals activates transformation-induced plasticity via a constraint-relief mechanism, yielding simultaneous strengthening and retained ductility.
motivation: Secondary-phase fillers typically strengthen metals but sacrifice plasticity and functionality, motivating a filler design that instead enhances deformability.
method: Shape-memory ceramic particles are incorporated into a metal matrix and the composite's mechanical response during processing and loading is characterized, revealing a constraint-relief mechanism driven by the ceramic's phase transformation.
result: The composite exhibits a transformation-induced plasticity response that relieves local microstructural constraints, improving strength–ductility synergy relative to conventional fillers.
conclusion: Stimulus-responsive shape-memory ceramics offer a design route for metal matrix composites that avoid the usual strength–plasticity trade-off.
